DUBAI/ISTANBUL:

Contacts between Iran and the United States to end their eight-month war are continuing, Tehran said on Monday, after days of ?Iranian talks with Qatari mediators ended with altered proposals but no breakthrough.

"Consultations through mediators are very intensive. We have presented our conditions and proposals and everything depends on the political rationality of Washington," Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said in comments carried by ?state media outlet IRNA.

Amid fears the conflict could reignite after Tuesday's midterm elections in the United States, China and Russia both spoke out on Monday against the possibility of renewed military action in a war that has hit the ?global economy.

While oil prices fell nearly 4% on Monday on hopes that the latest round of mediation could lead to a diplomatic solution to the crisis, Iranian sources said they believed a new US attack was still more likely than a deal.

Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said the plan Iran had submitted in September to end the war remained the focus of discussions, but he confirmed comments attributed to Araqchi on Saturday that the ?proposal could be shortened.

"The basis of dialogue and talks between Iran and the US via mediators is still Iran's seven-step proposal, which is now condensed, making it possible to implement it within two days," he said.

US President Donald Trump rejected the seven-step proposal in September.

The plan would call for the US to end its blockade on Iranian ports, Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz waterway, a US waiver on Iranian oil sales, the cancellation of new sanctions on Iran and then talks on other issues.

Baghaei reiterated that ?condensing the plan would not change Iran's underlying stance that a return to talks on the country's nuclear programme could only happen after it verified that all its conditions were met.

Asked whether the possibility of transferring Iran's highly enriched uranium stockpile to another country was raised in the talks, and whether Iran might agree to that, he said no.

An official briefed on the talks said Iran's negotiators had left on Sunday but not because of any problems in the talks, and added that a draft proposal was being circulated without elaborating.

RUSSIAN AND CHINESE CONCERNS

The war, which the US and Israel launched suddenly on February 28, has led to Iran's closure of the key Strait of Hormuz waterway, the US blockade on Iranian ports, repeated bouts of Iranian drone and missile fire on Gulf states and renewed conflict in Yemen.

Trump has repeatedly said there would be no new attack on Iran before Tuesday's midterm elections. Iran has said it will respond to any resumed attack aggressively with plans to strike targets both within and outside the Middle East.

China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Monday that all parties to the conflict should focus on political solutions rather than resorting to arms again, after a meeting with senior Iranian security official Ali Bagheri Kani in Beijing.

China, a major customer for Gulf energy products, is engaging more actively in Middle East diplomacy this week, hosting Oman's Sultan Haitham bin Tariq al-Said, whose country flanks the southern side of the Strait of Hormuz.

Wang also met Saudi Arabia's national security advisor Musaed bin Mohammed al-Aiban in Beijing on Monday, China's Foreign Ministry said, adding that all sides should work to safeguard regional energy and shipping lane security.

In Moscow, the Russian Foreign Ministry said reports of new military action against Iran were a cause for extreme concern and called for increased diplomatic efforts.

Russian President Vladimir Putin spoke by phone with Iran's top security official Mohsen Rezaei on Monday, Iranian state media reported.

Underscoring the risks to global energy supply, a Qatari liquefied natural gas (LNG) tanker was struck in the Gulf by unidentified objects on Friday, its operator Nakilat said on Sunday.

While attacks on oil tankers in the Gulf and Red Sea have been common during the conflict, attacks on LNG carriers have been rare, with the last reported incident with a ?Qatari tanker happening in early July.

Trump could launch nuclear strike

US commentator Tucker Carlson claimed late Sunday that the Trump administration could be days away from launching a nuclear strike on Iran, alleging that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pressuring President Donald Trump to authorize an attack on a suspected nuclear site in central Iran.

In a lengthy post on the US social media company X, Carlson identified the potential target as Pickaxe Mountain, where Israeli intelligence allegedly believes Iran has resumed its nuclear enrichment program.

Carlson is a conservative political commentator and former Fox News host whose program, Tucker Carlson Tonight, aired from 2016 to 2023.

He now hosts an independent political show on X, where he regularly comments on US foreign policy and international affairs.

Carlson claimed conventional US weapons could not penetrate the estimated 300 feet of solid granite protecting underground tunnels at the site, leaving a nuclear strike as the only military option.

"Bibi (Netanyahu) calls Trump about it every day," Carlson quoted an unnamed informed observer as saying.

Carlson argued that Netanyahu's political survival is driving his push for further military action. He claimed Netanyahu needs Trump's intervention to secure a 61-seat majority in the Knesset following the latest election results, warning that otherwise he could lose power and face investigations and possible imprisonment.

He also alleged that Netanyahu has been pressing senior US officials, including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and US Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper, to resume major combat operations.

Carlson also claimed that Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA Director John Ratcliffe were following Netanyahu's lead.

He further said former President Barack Obama had also opposed the Iran peace agreement being drafted in Doha.

Fears of regional escalation

Carlson said US allies in the Middle East were increasingly concerned about renewed fighting. He claimed Netanyahu secretly traveled to Abu Dhabi on Sept 27 to persuade the UAE to support a final attack on Iran, but Emirati officials refused.

Warning of the economic consequences, Carlson said eight months of conflict had severely affected Gulf economies, as well as global energy and fertilizer markets. He claimed 11 of the world's approximately 850 oil supertankers were badly damaged in the Strait of Hormuz in October alone.

He also warned that a nuclear explosion at Pickaxe Mountain could contaminate the Gulf and threaten the water supply of around 100 million people.

Carlson argued that a US nuclear strike could establish a dangerous precedent, potentially encouraging Russia to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine, triggering renewed nuclear tensions between India and Pakistan, and prompting North Korea to attack Seoul.

"After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final," he wrote.

He further alleged that the Trump administration had quietly revised US nuclear doctrine since February to make the first use of so-called "battlefield nukes" easier and more likely.

Vance, Witkoff urge Trump to pursue diplomacy

Carlson said Trump could decide by Nov 7 whether to authorize the use of nuclear weapons, adding that Vice President JD Vance and special envoy Steve Witkoff were urging him to pursue a diplomatic agreement with Tehran.

Although acknowledging that negotiations would be difficult, Carlson said people who had spoken with Iranian decision-makers believed there was a consensus that further conflict would benefit no one and that an agreement was worth pursuing.

He concluded by warning that the consequences of a nuclear strike would extend far beyond Iran, arguing that the international public had been excluded from decisions that could threaten millions of lives.

"Now would be the time for them to speak up," Carlson wrote.

US could hit Iran's remaining nuclear sites 'in 10 minutes'

Carlson's claims follow Trump's remarks to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Saturday that one or two Iranian nuclear facilities remained potential targets and that the US could strike them within 10 minutes.

Trump specifically mentioned Pickaxe Mountain, saying he had military plans for the area, but did not indicate that a nuclear strike had been authorized.

"You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly," he added.

In an Oct 16 interview with Newsmax, he explicitly ruled out using nuclear weapons against Iran.

headline: Hackers shut down shop fridges across Europe
description: Hackers shut down shop fridges across Europe
author: Reuters
article_text:
A hacking attack on European supermarkets spread across the continent on Monday, hitting fridges and freezers from Sweden to Belgium and forcing stores to throw away food in an incident that echoed a similar attack in France last month.

The attack, which raised temperatures in refrigerator and freezer units at dozens of stores, hit supermarket groups Ahold Delhaize and Colruyt in Belgium and Luxembourg, as well as Swedish grocers ICA and Coop. Furniture-to-meatballs retailer IKEA also saw at least one store affected.

"Everything is destroyed," Engla Ingwall, sales manager at an ICA franchise store in Stockholm, told Reuters during a visit to the store on Monday, adding the attack occurred at 2 a.m. (0100 GMT) but was only noticed hours later.

"There has been a cyberattack and all our freezers reached 50 degrees (Celsius)."

A spokesperson for privately held ICA said the company was aware that a "limited number of stores were affected by an incident overnight, which impacted their refrigeration and freezer systems".

The latest incidents follow an attack in France last month when police said hackers seized control of cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets, causing fires and food losses. Ahold also reported a cybersecurity incident to police last month.

While no one has claimed responsibility for either attack, the incidents have heightened concerns among European authorities about hybrid threats to infrastructure amid growing security tensions since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

headline: Nine killed in Florida business jet crash
description: Nine killed in Florida business jet crash
author: Reuters
article_text:
A Learjet crashed on Sunday afternoon in a residential area in Palm Beach County, Florida, killing all nine people on board, US transportation officials said.

The private jet had taken off from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas, the Federal Aviation Administration said in a statement.

"It was a big-time tragedy that happened," Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said at a press conference near the crash site in Lake Worth Beach. "When you see that video, it's a jarring thing. It was like a missile coming down, and a massive explosion, debris going everywhere."

The National Transportation Safety Board said it had launched an investigation into the crash, which Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called a "horrific tragedy."

The crash left a "massive crater" by the road near the entrance to a mobile home park, Palm Beach County Commissioner Joel Flores said at the news conference. About 600 people were being evacuated from the area and relocated to two shelters in the county, Flores said.

Heavy rainfall and thunderstorms were occurring in the area at the time, forecaster AccuWeather said in a statement.

An audio recording from a Miami air traffic control center posted on LiveATC, a site that broadcasts air traffic control communications, captured the plane's final moments before the crash in unusual detail.

At first, someone in the plane's cockpit reported to an air traffic controller that they were "managing the ice" but faced "moderate" turbulence and were seeking "better rides".

Less than a minute later, the person said "Mayday, mayday," reporting that the plane was suddenly descending at a rate of 10,000 feet per minute.

Seconds later, the person said they were declaring an emergency, with the rate of descent accelerating to 20,000 feet per minute.

Less than 20 seconds later, the person said: "We're going to crash into the ground" before saying that the descent rate had reached 22,000 feet per minute as the plane started banking.

About 35 seconds after the initial mayday announcement, the last thing heard from the cockpit was a rapidly spoken "We're out of time."

Flight tracking website Flightradar24 said data showed the vertical descent rate at one point exceeded 32,000 feet per minute.

headline: Spain deports asylum seekers
description: Spain deports asylum seekers
author: Reuters
article_text:
Spain has returned to Morocco more than a dozen sub-Saharan African and Asian migrants who reached the Spanish enclave of Ceuta and were turned down for asylum, the first deportation of its kind from the enclave since a mass border crossing in July.

The Interior Ministry said the group had been sent back to Morocco after it agreed to receive them and they remained on Moroccan territory at present. It declined to give numbers or nationalities but migrant and rights charities operating in Ceuta said 16 people from Senegal, Nigeria, Yemen, Cameroon and Bangladesh were deported.

The NGOs claim such returns fail to take into account the risks associated with Morocco's treatment of migrants from other countries and fly in the face of the values espoused by Spain's leftist government.

Virginia Alvarez, an Amnesty International researcher, said Spain's posture was hypocritical.

"Spain, despite its (progressive) speeches in Europe, is not ensuring that human rights guarantees are met for people who cross its borders in Ceuta and Melilla," she said. "Morocco does not respect many human rights."

Morocco's Interior Ministry did not respond to Reuters requests for comment.

headline: Xi calls for lasting peace in Middle East
description: Xi calls for lasting peace in Middle East
author: agencies
article_text:
The Middle East and Gulf region should not become a battleground for great-power rivalry and China is willing to work with Arab nations to achieve lasting peace, Chinese President Xi Jinping told Oman's sultan on Monday.

Xi told Omani Sultan Haitham bin Tariq al-Said that the world is undergoing profound changes.

"The Middle East Gulf region should not become an arena for great-power rivalry and geopolitical conflict. Peace and stability in the region require joint nurturing and protection by all parties," Xi said, according to China's Foreign Ministry.

China has consistently been committed to stopping the war, and hopes to contribute "wisdom and solutions to resolving the region's security dilemmas," he added.

China is willing to strengthen communication and coordination with Arab countries, including the Gulf Cooperation Council states, to work together toward restoring peace and achieving lasting stability and security, Xi said.

In a 20-point joint statement, both sides said they agree that normal and safe navigation should resume in the Strait of Hormuz. The countries also called for the US and Iran to pursue peaceful options, return to the agreement struck in June aimed at ending the conflict and restart dialogue.

China's Foreign Ministry said later on Monday that Zhai Jun, its special envoy to the Middle East, would visit Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia this month.

Haitham arrived in Beijing on Sunday for a two-day visit, the first by an Omani head of state since the countries established ties in 1978.

Haitham told Xi his government had deep appreciation for China's positions on key issues concerning the region, Omani state media reported.

"We believe that development

and stability are inextricably linked," he said.

"The prosperity of nations requires an environment defined by security, peace, respect for state sovereignty, and adherence to international law - an environment where disputes are resolved through peaceful means."

He also said Oman was open to entering into a preferential bilateral trade and investment agreement with China.

China's Foreign Ministry said later on Monday that Zhai Jun, its special envoy to the Middle East, would visit Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia this month.
Haitham arrived in Beijing on Sunday for a two-day visit, the first by an Omani head of state since the countries established ties in 1978.
Haitham told Xi his government had deep appreciation for China's positions on key issues concerning the region, Omani state media reported.
"We believe that development
and stability are inextricably linked," he said.

"The prosperity of nations requires an environment defined by security, peace, respect for state sovereignty, and adherence to international law - an environment where disputes are resolved through peaceful means."
He also said Oman was open to entering into a preferential bilateral trade and investment agreement with China.

headline: Russian bombing kills 24 in Ukraine
description: Russian bombing kills 24 in Ukraine
author: Reuters
article_text:
.

Russian forces bombed a school in a village in Ukraine's southeastern Zaporizhzhia region on Monday, killing 24 people, Ukraine's emergency services said.

The emergency services said two members of a rescue crew were among the dead in the village of Komyshuvakha.

President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, writing on Telegram, said Russian forces initially dropped aerial bombs on a school in the village, used for distributing humanitarian assistance.

"After the first air strike, there was a repeat strike with nine more bombs, directly on the shelter where people were gathered," Zelenskiy wrote.

"The Russians could not have been unaware that every week residents who have remained in Komyshuvakha were receiving assistance right there. This is yet further proof that Russia does not want any kind of de-escalation, any real justice."

headline: BD protests turn violent
description: BD protests turn violent
author: Reuters
article_text:
Bangladesh's garment factories briefly resumed operations on Monday after a widespread shutdown a day earlier, but fresh clashes between workers and police forced hundreds of plants to suspend production again.

The unrest has raised concerns over shipment delays and buyer confidence in Bangladesh, a key supplier to brands including H&M, Zara, Walmart and Primark, at a critical point in the production cycle for spring and summer export orders.

Workers demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka ($243), up from 12,500 taka, blocked roads, vandalised factories and clashed with police across major manufacturing districts, prompting 679 factories to halt production.

Bangladesh is the world's second-largest garment exporter after China and the ready-made garment sector accounts for more than 80% of the South Asian nation's export earnings. It employs about 4 million workers and accounts for roughly 10% of economic output.

In a bid to defuse the crisis, the government on Sunday formed a six-member wage board to review workers' demands, which have gained momentum amid persistent inflation and rising living costs.

Police said they used tear gas to disperse garment workers attempting to block roads in Dhaka after protesters hurled bricks and stones at officers. Unrest was also reported in Ashulia and Gazipur, two manufacturing hubs on the outskirts of the capital.

Police and industry

officials said protesters

set fire to a police

vehicle and vandalised a number of factories.

The clashes follow Sunday's protests and factory closures, with workers continuing to demand higher wages and the resolution of employment grievances.

"Bangladesh has among the lowest garment wages in the world," said Babul Akhter, general secretary of the Bangladesh Garment and Industrial Workers Federation and a workers' representative on the wage board.

"If factory owners cannot pay workers properly, they should negotiate better prices with international buyers. They cannot build a business on the backs of underpaid workers."

headline: Cleric arrested after Bajaur madrassa child death
description: Cleric arrested after Bajaur madrassa child death
author: HANIFULLAH
article_text:
DPO Bajaur Khan Zaib Mohmand described the death of the innocent child as deeply tragic

A 12-year-old boy died after allegedly being tortured at a madrassa in the Qaddafi Bandagai area of Bajaur district, prompting Regional Police Officer (RPO) Malakand Division Zahid Nawaz to take immediate notice and order swift action.

Acting on the RPO's notice and under the special instructions and supervision of District Police Officer (DPO) Bajaur, Utman Khel police station, led by SHO, launched a prompt and effective operation and arrested the fugitive cleric accused in the case.

A formal case has been registered against the suspect, who has been taken into police custody. Further investigation and legal proceedings are underway, and the accused will be brought to justice in accordance with the law.

DPO Bajaur Khan Zaib Mohmand described the death of the innocent child as deeply tragic, saying Bajaur police stand with the bereaved family in this hour of grief and that all legal requirements will be met to secure justice for them.

He made clear that the investigation will be conducted strictly on merit and that no one will be considered above the law. Bajaur police, he added, remain committed to upholding the rule of law, delivering justice to the oppressed, and protecting the lives and property of the public.

headline: Governor vows action against illegal Afghans
description: Governor vows action against illegal Afghans
author: Ahtesham Bashir
article_text:
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Monday declared that the provincial government's policy on Afghan nationals residing illegally in the province is fully aligned with the federal government's stance, and action against them will continue. He made it clear, however, that Afghans entering Pakistan on valid visas would be welcomed.

Speaking to the media in Peshawar, the governor said no country in the world permits foreigners to stay without legal status. "Therefore, action will also be taken against Afghan citizens living illegally in Pakistan," he stated. Those arriving with proper visas, he added, would be received as welcome guests.

On the ongoing campaign against encroachments, Kundi was categorical. The operation to remove illegal structures would continue and no pressure of any kind would be accepted in this regard. "Measures initiated in the public interest will be sustained," he said.

Addressing the issue of prolonged power load-shedding in the province, the governor said he would take up the matter with the relevant authorities. At the same time, he reminded the public that electricity is neither free nor a war trophy. "Consumers must pay their bills for the power they use," he asserted. Kundi revealed that work is under way to introduce new technology that would improve the power distribution and load-shedding system. Under the proposed arrangement, load-shedding would be managed at the transformer level rather than the feeder level, allowing more precise and equitable cuts.

The governor also welcomed the federal government's decision to provide Rs 160 billion for development in K-P, describing it as a significant gesture of support. He said 70 per cent of the amount would be spent in areas that had historically been deprived of development projects and fair resource allocation.

Responding to a question about corruption allegations, Kundi said the law applies equally to everyone. Whether it concerns Chief Minister Sohail Afridi or any other individual, if there are credible charges of corruption, legal action must follow. "No one should be considered above the law when allegations arise," he emphasised.

The governor also took note of the inconvenience caused by electricity poles standing in the middle of roads. He said he would discuss the matter with PESCO officials so that such poles could be relocated, reducing difficulties for citizens and easing traffic problems.

Kundi's remarks reaffirm the provincial administration's determination to enforce the law on illegal residency, protect public land from encroachments, and address long-standing issues of power supply and urban infrastructure while insisting that citizens fulfil their own obligations, particularly the payment of utility bills.

PESHAWAR:

Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Monday declared that the provincial government's policy on Afghan nationals residing illegally in the province is fully aligned with the federal government's stance, and action against them will continue. He made it clear, however, that Afghans entering Pakistan on valid visas would be welcomed.

Speaking to the media in Peshawar, the governor said no country in the world permits foreigners to stay without legal status. "Therefore, action will also be taken against Afghan citizens living illegally in Pakistan," he stated. Those arriving with proper visas, he added, would be received as welcome guests.

On the ongoing campaign against encroachments, Kundi was categorical. The operation to remove illegal structures would continue and no pressure of any kind would be accepted in this regard. "Measures initiated in the public interest will be sustained," he said.

Addressing the issue of prolonged power load-shedding in the province, the governor said he would take up the matter with the relevant authorities. At the same time, he reminded the public that electricity is neither free nor a war trophy. "Consumers must pay their bills for the power they use," he asserted. Kundi revealed that work is under way to introduce new technology that would improve the power distribution and load-shedding system. Under the proposed arrangement, load-shedding would be managed at the transformer level rather than the feeder level, allowing more precise and equitable cuts.

The governor also welcomed the federal government's decision to provide Rs 160 billion for development in K-P, describing it as a significant gesture of support. He said 70 per cent of the amount would be spent in areas that had historically been deprived of development projects and fair resource allocation.

Responding to a question about corruption allegations, Kundi said the law applies equally to everyone. Whether it concerns Chief Minister Sohail Afridi or any other individual, if there are credible charges of corruption, legal action must follow. "No one should be considered above the law when allegations arise," he emphasised.

The governor also took note of the inconvenience caused by electricity poles standing in the middle of roads. He said he would discuss the matter with PESCO officials so that such poles could be relocated, reducing difficulties for citizens and easing traffic problems.

Kundi's remarks reaffirm the provincial administration's determination to enforce the law on illegal residency, protect public land from encroachments, and address long-standing issues of power supply and urban infrastructure while insisting that citizens fulfil their own obligations, particularly the payment of utility bills.

headline: K-P audit exposes billions in irregularities
description: K-P audit exposes billions in irregularities
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Adviser to the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Governor on Information and Public Relations, Relief, Rehabilitation and Settlement, Samar Haroon Bilour, has expressed serious concern over billions of rupees in financial irregularities and accounting discrepancies highlighted in the Audit Report for FY 2024-25.

In a press statement, she said expenditures amounting to Rs72.46 billion could not be fully verified, while additional entries of Rs104.26 billion were recorded beyond the budget approved by the Provincial Assembly.

She said the report also identified Rs153.68 billion in development expenditures incorrectly recorded under various accounting heads and a negative balance of Rs39.58 billion in the Public Account.

Bilour further pointed out that records of external loans worth Rs98.89 billion were incomplete, while payments of Rs51.85 billion against foreign loans and interest remained unverified. Records of provincial domestic loans had not been updated since 2017-18, while federal government loan records had remained incomplete since 2013-14.

She said additional entries were also identified in the development budget and key departments, including Health, Education, Police and Highways.

Calling for an impartial investigation, she stressed that public money was a national trust and those responsible for its management must be held accountable wherever irregularities were established.

Meanwhile, Samar Haroon Bilour has formally assumed charge of the Department of Relief, Rehabilitation and Settlement.

On the occasion, she expressed her gratitude to the Governor for reposing confidence in her and entrusting her with this important responsibility.

headline: JI questions PTI's lack of protests over governor's rule
description: JI questions PTI's lack of protests over governor's rule
author: Yasir Ali
article_text:
Baloch says a deep trust deficit existed between the government, state institutions, and the public

Jamaat-e-Islami Pakistan Acting Amir Liaquat Baloch has questioned the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) leadership's failure to mobilise public protests against the imposition of governor's rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, saying the absence of public resistance despite the party's tall claims and popular mandate raises serious questions.

He said PTI leaders had made grand claims during their long march and held negotiations, while emergency and governor's rule had also been imposed. However, despite all these developments, the party failed to bring people onto the streets against governor's rule or even the removal of its provincial government. The lack of protests, he added, had strengthened unpopular measures.

He stressed that protecting the lives and property of people must remain the government's foremost responsibility. Establishing peace in terrorism-affected areas of the province should be the top priority, requiring serious and practical measures.

Addressing a press conference at Markaz Islami, the provincial headquarters of Jamaat-e-Islami in Peshawar, after attending a meeting of party office-bearers from 12 districts affected by the emergency, Baloch said a deep trust deficit existed between the government, state institutions and the public.

headline: Four polio workers kidnapped in Tank
description: Four polio workers kidnapped in Tank
author: Ramzan Seemab
article_text:
Police launched an investigation into the incident following the abduction

Four polio workers were abducted by unidentified armed men after being subjected to gunfire in the Tank district, while two other members of a polio vaccination team, who had been kidnapped in Lower South Waziristan, were subsequently released.

According to details, the incident in Tank occurred in the village of Jious, located in the Sheikh Attar union council, where unidentified armed men abducted four polio workers. Police sources said the gunmen took all four workers to an undisclosed location.

Police launched an investigation into the incident following the abduction. However, further details about the identity of the perpetrators and the whereabouts of the kidnapped workers were not immediately available.

In a separate incident, two members of a polio vaccination team were abducted by armed men in the Azam Warsak area of Lower South Waziristan.

Sources said armed men affiliated with the proscribed Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) were allegedly involved in the kidnapping. However, both polio workers were later released.

headline: Islamabad ATC grants bail to Imaan Mazari, Hadi Ali Chattha in road blockade, police clash case
description: ATC Judge Abual Hasnat approves bail against surety bonds of Rs5,000 each
author: Fiaz Mahmood
article_text:
An Islamabad anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Tuesday granted bail to lawyers Imaan Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha in a case involving allegations of blocking a road and clashing with police.

ATC Judge Abual Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain heard the bail applications and approved them against surety bonds of Rs5,000 each, with lawyer Riasat Ali Azad appearing on behalf of the accused.

During the hearing, police submitted the case record to the court. The judge then asked the parties whether they wished to make any further submissions before announcing his decision. Referring to the show-cause notice matter involving the police, the judge said, "I will look into the matter concerning the show-cause notice to the police."

The court subsequently approved the bail applications of both Imaan and Chattha.

According to the First Information Report (FIR) registered at Islamabad's Kohsar Police Station, which was filed last year and concerned a protest in the grounds of the Islamabad Press Club, Imaan and Hadi led a Baloch Student Council protest with at least 150 demonstrators present. The FIR added that the participants raised anti-state slogans and those against state institutions through loudspeakers and megaphones, while also obstructing police from carrying out their duties.

Filed under Sections 186, 188, 341, 353, and 506 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC), the FIR stated that the participants took a rally out and blocked a road, upon which police informed them that this was against Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Tuesday's verdict came less than a week after an ATC sentenced Imaan and Hadi to 10 years in prison each in a case involving the removal of security barriers. Both were convicted under Section 186 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) and sentenced to “1-year Simple Imprisonment” with a fine of Rs50,000 each, the order stated.

The court also convicted both under Section 353 of the PPC and sentenced them to “2 years' simple imprisonment with a fine of Rs50,000 each," while in case of non-payment, they would undergo an additional three months' simple imprisonment.

The court also convicted both under Section 7(h) of the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA), 1997, as defined under Section 6(2)(m). Under this provision, Imaan and Haadi were also sentenced to “ten years (RI) with a fine of Rs 100,000 each."

The couple was arrested by the capital police in October 2024 on terrorism charges after a confrontation with traffic police, who had barricaded the area to secure the movement of the English cricket team. They were accused of interfering with government protocol, leading to their detention under various sections of the Anti-Terrorism Act and the Pakistan Penal Code.

Imprisonment in social media case

In January, the couple was handed a combined 17-year sentence on multiple charges linked to controversial social media posts that the prosecution argued amounted to an anti-state narrative under cybercrime laws. The same month, they filed applications for suspension of their sentences.

Later, Imaan and her husband Hadi were rearrested on September 17, shortly after the Supreme Court granted them bail and suspended their sentences in the social-media posts case. They were produced before an Islamabad ATC in connection with a case registered at Kohsar Police Station.

headline: Nicolas Cage 'currently homeless' after sinkhole damages Malibu mansion
description: Nicolas Cage says he is living in hotels after sinkhole severely damaged his Malibu property
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Nicolas Cage has revealed that he is currently living in hotels after a massive sinkhole severely damaged his Malibu mansion, leaving the actor unable to stay at the property.

The 62-year-old actor discussed his living arrangements during an appearance at L.A. Comic Con on Saturday, October 31. Asked about his Halloween plans, Cage explained that the damage to his home had affected how he would usually celebrate the occasion.

“I’m currently a little bit homeless,” he said. “Something happened to my house in Malibu so I’m just sort of living in hotels so I don’t have normal trick or treaters I would like to enjoy tonight.”

Cage added that he would still take his four-year-old daughter, August, trick-or-treating in Santa Monica, California. He also planned to watch Stanley Kubrick's horror film The Shining after putting her to bed.

The actor's $10.5 million beachfront property was severely damaged in September following heavy rain and coastal erosion.

Photographs taken on September 8 showed a large sinkhole where the driveway had previously stood, with sections of asphalt and concrete collapsing alongside other debris.

The damage also affected neighbouring properties, prompting evacuations. According to reports, seven homes on the street were marked unsafe for occupancy, while another 24 were due to receive red tags because of limited vehicle access.

The City of Malibu explained that all 31 properties had been deemed unsafe because emergency services could no longer reliably reach residents. A statement from the city said, “The collapse of a beachfront driveway extended into the roadway, blocking resident and emergency access.”

Cage is reportedly attempting to save his property. He filed three permits shortly after the sinkhole appeared, including an emergency request to install sandbags to protect the home from waves and further coastal erosion. Additional permits covered debris removal and preparatory work for excavation and soil sampling.

headline: Oil edges up after report of US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island
description: US West Texas Intermediate crude rises 20 cents, or 0.21%, to $96.66 a barrel
author: Reuters
article_text:
Oil prices edged up on Tuesday after a report that the United States had struck Iran's Qeshm ​Island, raising concerns about an escalation of the eight-month conflict and prolonged disruptions to Middle ‌East oil supplies.

US West Texas Intermediate crude was up 20 cents, or 0.21%, at $96.66 a barrel, while Brent crude futures rose 3 cents, or 0.03%, to $104.8 a barrel by 0355 GMT.

Both benchmark prices dropped more than 7% on Monday as talks between Iranian and ​Qatari officials lifted hopes for an end to the US-Israeli war with Iran.

The United States struck Iran's ​Qeshm Island, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday, citing US officials. Some of the officials ⁠described the assaults as defensive in nature to prevent Iran from having the freedom to attack commercial ships ​in the Strait of Hormuz.

"The report added a degree of risk premium back into the oil price. Just ​when markets were starting to price in a more diplomatic path, this reminder of ongoing military activity has flipped the tone," said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade.

However, the inability of prices to sustain those gains suggests that a substantial ​geopolitical risk premium is already embedded in oil prices, said Priyanka Sachdeva, head of market insight at Phillip ​Nova.

"Unless there is concrete evidence of further disruption to physical supplies or critical energy infrastructure, fresh headlines alone may struggle ‌to sustain ⁠another rally."

Meanwhile, Tehran said on Monday that contacts between Iran and the US to end their war are continuing, after days of Iranian talks with Qatari mediators ended with altered proposals but no breakthrough.

Trump raised doubts on Monday about whether he would follow through on a threatened resumption of military strikes against Iran and said a deal ​with Tehran could happen.

The ​US-Iran conflict that began in ⁠late February has sharply reduced traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which previously carried about a fifth of global crude oil and natural gas supplies.

The Iran war ​is a leading cause of high gasoline prices that are weighing on voters, ​and Trump is ⁠under pressure to end the conflict.

Brent ended October at its highest in six months on concerns that the Middle East conflict could escalate again after Tuesday's US midterm elections.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei ⁠had granted ​the government certain authorities for peace talks.

Additionally, the US will bring together ​delegations from Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10 to 11 to discuss ending Moscow's war against Ukraine, post-war security agreements, ​and de-escalation.

Both benchmark prices dropped more than 7% on Monday as talks between Iranian and ​Qatari officials lifted hopes for an end to the US-Israeli war with Iran.

The United States struck Iran's ​Qeshm Island, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday, citing US officials. Some of the officials ⁠described the assaults as defensive in nature to prevent Iran from having the freedom to attack commercial ships ​in the Strait of Hormuz.

headline: Trump says 'not looking to kill lots of people' in Iran after midterms
description: US Vice President JD Vance says the US and Iran have made progress toward a negotiated settlement
author: Reuters
article_text:
US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that he was "not looking to kill lots of people" in Iran following the midterm elections, while warning that Washington would take decisive action if necessary.

"Look, I'm not looking to, you know, kill lots of people, but if we have to, we'll have to," Trump told Fox News amid reports that the US was weighing strikes on Iran following the polling.

Trump said American forces struck a newly completed Iranian anti-aircraft installation overnight after monitoring its construction for over two months. "Just a minor attack. It wasn't war."

Citing a US official, local media reported that the US military carried out "defensive" strikes against Iran’s Qeshm Island on Monday.

The US president argued that the confrontation with Iran differed from traditional wars such as the Russia-Ukraine war or World War II, asserting that Washington held total leverage over Tehran after crippling its naval and air assets during the ongoing Iran war.

"We have them totally where we want. We could finish them off, or we could be nice and let thousands of people live that would get killed in a war," he said.

IRGC claims shooting down two more US drones

The US carried out strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, a US official said on Monday. The strikes, earlier reported by the Wall Street Journal, appeared to be limited and were not a resumption of major combat operations, the official said, speaking on the condition of anonymity.

Another official said the strikes were defensive measures against Iranians using surface-to-air missiles against US assets.

The Pentagon referred a request for comment to the US Central Command, which oversees American forces in the Middle East. CENTCOM did not respond to requests for comment.

Earlier on Monday, Iranian state media outlet IRNA reported that there were several explosions on Qeshm Island. The Journal reported that the attack was the latest in a series of strikes carried out by Washington in recent weeks. Fox News, citing officials, said the strikes were defensive and carried out in response to Iran firing at a US aircraft.

Iran’s state news agency IRNA reported five explosions on Qeshm Island, located in the Strait of Hormuz. Separately, the semi-official Fars news agency said explosions were heard coming from the direction of the sea in Bandar Lengeh in Hormozgan province.

The cause of the explosions was not immediately known. Neither agency provided details on casualties or damage. The reports come amid continued diplomatic efforts between Tehran and Washington over tensions surrounding the Strait of Hormuz.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said Monday that the two countries were continuing to exchange messages through mediators. He confirmed that Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi had visited Doha to facilitate the exchanges through Qatari mediation.

Iran delivers ‘firm, rational’ response to US, says ‘ball in America’s court to prevent war’

Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Tuesday that Tehran has delivered a “firm and rational” response to Washington, stressing that the US must now decide whether to prevent another war.

Speaking during a parliamentary session, Ghalibaf, who is also leading Iran’s negotiating team in talks with the US, said Tehran remained prepared for both diplomacy and military confrontation.

“Iran has delivered a firm and rational response to the American side, and now the ball is in America’s court to prevent war,” he said.

He stressed that Iran’s armed forces remained at the highest level of defensive readiness.

“If Washington makes another strategic mistake, it should know that this time it will face a new battlefield and will find itself even more desperate to seek a way out,” he warned.

Ghalibaf also accused the US of pursuing a longstanding policy aimed at dominating Iran, saying Washington had previously relied on compliant governments but now employed military, economic and psychological warfare.

He said Iran would not surrender to military threats, warning that any miscalculation by Washington would trigger an unpredictable response.

Ghalibaf added that Iran’s military response to any renewed attack would not be limited by geographical boundaries.

Iran's foreign minister says talks with Saudi Arabia are ongoing; Yemen fighting intensifies

Talks between Iran and Saudi Arabia are ongoing as Tehran aims to reach new regional security arrangements for countries in the region without foreign military involvement, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on X on Tuesday.

Last week, top officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iranian officials in Tehran, the first high-level contact between Iran and the three nations since August. The US-Israeli war on Iran started in late February, and since then, fighting has spread to Saudi Arabia and Yemen.

Riyadh said the visit was intended to open negotiating channels to "prevent the return of military escalation," as fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis had intensified in recent weeks.

Houthi attacks on the kingdom escalated as the powerful militia advanced towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping chokepoint that lies on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula from the Strait of Hormuz.

The Houthis have also attacked Saudi oil facilities and airports, including Riyadh's international airport, disrupting flights and oil exports and drawing Saudi airstrikes on Yemen in response.

Impoverished Yemen has been mired in a civil war since the Houthis pushed the internationally recognised, Saudi-backed government out of the capital, Sanaa, in 2014.

Iran-US deal still out of reach, senior Iranian official tells Reuters

Iran and the United States are far from reaching a deal to end the war, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday, adding that Tehran would not accept Washington's "excessive demands".

The comments come at a time of heightened diplomatic efforts, with Qatar acting as a key intermediary, to prevent a potential return to active conflict after the midterms.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guard says it downed 2 US drones in Strait of Hormuz

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Monday that it downed two US drones south of Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency.

The report said the IRGC Aerospace Force used electronic warfare systems against the two MQM-170 drones, bringing the number of aircraft of that type reportedly captured by Iranian forces to four. Tasnim said the operation had prevented the drones from completing their missions. It provided no other operational details.

The report follows two similar Iranian announcements last week.

On Friday, the IRNA news agency reported that the IRGC Aerospace Force downed an MQM-170 drone over Qeshm Island using electronic warfare systems.

On Thursday, the IRGC Navy said it had seized control of another drone of the same type in the western Strait of Hormuz and landed it intact. The US military rejected Iran’s account of Thursday’s incident.

The latest report comes amid ongoing indirect diplomatic contacts between Tehran and Washington.

US, Iran have made progress toward negotiated settlement: Vance

US Vice President JD Vance said on Monday that Washington has made “progress” in talks with Iran, saying he and President Donald Trump feel “pretty good” about reaching a negotiated settlement.

“I actually just spoke with the president of the United States about an hour ago about this,” Vance told reporters. “Look, the president and I both feel pretty good about the prospects for potentially coming to a negotiated settlement. We’re going to keep on working at it.”

“The Iranians are always a little unpredictable, and as the president always says, he retains kinetic options. He retains non-kinetic options, but we’ve certainly made some progress. We’ll see if we can make some more,” he said.

Asked whether Iran had been given a deadline before strikes resume, Vance said: “No, we haven’t set deadlines.”

“Having destroyed their nuclear program, we want to make sure they don’t rebuild it or try to rebuild it. That’s what matters most to the United States,” he said.

“We do think that there is a pathway there, but it really does require a firm commitment and a verifiable commitment that they don’t rebuild that nuclear program,” he added.

Vance's remarks came hours after Trump said at the reopening of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in Washington that Iran wants to make a deal to end the conflict, now in its ninth month.

“They want to make a deal, and that could happen,” Trump said, adding that Iran had asked Washington to stop targeting its leaders, “and we will.”

US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that he was "not looking to kill lots of people" in Iran following the midterm elections, while warning that Washington would take decisive action if necessary.

"Look, I'm not looking to, you know, kill lots of people, but if we have to, we'll have to," Trump told Fox News amid reports that the US was weighing strikes on Iran following the polling.

BREAKING: "I'm not looking to, you know, kill lots of people, but if we have to, we'll have to."

President Trump delivers a blunt warning on what comes next in the war in Iran, pointing to the U.S. operation in Venezuela as an example of how quickly American military force can… pic.twitter.com/FI1J6vmWZ7

— Fox News (@FoxNews) November 3, 2026

Trump said American forces struck a newly completed Iranian anti-aircraft installation overnight after monitoring its construction for over two months. "Just a minor attack. It wasn't war."

"It's just a minor attack. It wasn't war."

President Trump reveals U.S. forces struck an Iranian anti-aircraft facility overnight, describing the operation as limited rather than a major military escalation.

Trump says Iran spent roughly two months building the facility while… pic.twitter.com/9Yi0G0jEAD

— Fox News (@FoxNews) November 3, 2026

Citing a US official, local media reported that the US military carried out "defensive" strikes against Iran’s Qeshm Island on Monday.

The US president argued that the confrontation with Iran differed from traditional wars such as the Russia-Ukraine war or World War II, asserting that Washington held total leverage over Tehran after crippling its naval and air assets during the ongoing Iran war.

"We have them totally where we want. We could finish them off, or we could be nice and let thousands of people live that would get killed in a war," he said.

IRGC claims shooting down two more US drones

The US carried out strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, a US official said on Monday. The strikes, earlier reported by the Wall Street Journal, appeared to be limited and were not a resumption of major combat operations, the official said, speaking on the condition of anonymity.

Another official said the strikes were defensive measures against Iranians using surface-to-air missiles against US assets.

The Pentagon referred a request for comment to the US Central Command, which oversees American forces in the Middle East. CENTCOM did not respond to requests for comment.

Earlier on Monday, Iranian state media outlet IRNA reported that there were several explosions on Qeshm Island. The Journal reported that the attack was the latest in a series of strikes carried out by Washington in recent weeks. Fox News, citing officials, said the strikes were defensive and carried out in response to Iran firing at a US aircraft.

Iran’s state news agency IRNA reported five explosions on Qeshm Island, located in the Strait of Hormuz. Separately, the semi-official Fars news agency said explosions were heard coming from the direction of the sea in Bandar Lengeh in Hormozgan province.

Read: Tehran engaged in ‘intensive shuttle diplomacy’ through Qatari, Pakistani mediators: Araghchi

The cause of the explosions was not immediately known. Neither agency provided details on casualties or damage. The reports come amid continued diplomatic efforts between Tehran and Washington over tensions surrounding the Strait of Hormuz.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said Monday that the two countries were continuing to exchange messages through mediators. He confirmed that Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi had visited Doha to facilitate the exchanges through Qatari mediation.

Iran delivers ‘firm, rational’ response to US, says ‘ball in America’s court to prevent war’

Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Tuesday that Tehran has delivered a “firm and rational” response to Washington, stressing that the US must now decide whether to prevent another war.

Speaking during a parliamentary session, Ghalibaf, who is also leading Iran’s negotiating team in talks with the US, said Tehran remained prepared for both diplomacy and military confrontation.

“Iran has delivered a firm and rational response to the American side, and now the ball is in America’s court to prevent war,” he said.

He stressed that Iran’s armed forces remained at the highest level of defensive readiness.

“If Washington makes another strategic mistake, it should know that this time it will face a new battlefield and will find itself even more desperate to seek a way out,” he warned.

Ghalibaf also accused the US of pursuing a longstanding policy aimed at dominating Iran, saying Washington had previously relied on compliant governments but now employed military, economic and psychological warfare.

He said Iran would not surrender to military threats, warning that any miscalculation by Washington would trigger an unpredictable response.

Ghalibaf added that Iran’s military response to any renewed attack would not be limited by geographical boundaries.

Iran's foreign minister says talks with Saudi Arabia are ongoing; Yemen fighting intensifies

Talks between Iran and Saudi Arabia are ongoing as Tehran aims to reach new regional security arrangements for countries in the region without foreign military involvement, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on X on Tuesday.

Last week, top officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iranian officials in Tehran, the first high-level contact between Iran and the three nations since August. The US-Israeli war on Iran started in late February, and since then, fighting has spread to Saudi Arabia and Yemen.

Riyadh said the visit was intended to open negotiating channels to "prevent the return of military escalation," as fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis had intensified in recent weeks.

Houthi attacks on the kingdom escalated as the powerful militia advanced towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping chokepoint that lies on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula from the Strait of Hormuz.

The Houthis have also attacked Saudi oil facilities and airports, including Riyadh's international airport, disrupting flights and oil exports and drawing Saudi airstrikes on Yemen in response.

Impoverished Yemen has been mired in a civil war since the Houthis pushed the internationally recognised, Saudi-backed government out of the capital, Sanaa, in 2014.

Iran-US deal still out of reach, senior Iranian official tells Reuters

Iran and the United States are far from reaching a deal to end the war, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday, adding that Tehran would not accept Washington's "excessive demands".

The comments come at a time of heightened diplomatic efforts, with Qatar acting as a key intermediary, to prevent a potential return to active conflict after the midterms.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guard says it downed 2 US drones in Strait of Hormuz

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Monday that it downed two US drones south of Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency.

The report said the IRGC Aerospace Force used electronic warfare systems against the two MQM-170 drones, bringing the number of aircraft of that type reportedly captured by Iranian forces to four. Tasnim said the operation had prevented the drones from completing their missions. It provided no other operational details.

The report follows two similar Iranian announcements last week.

Read more: Iran warns US of prolonged war after Trump signals more strikes

On Friday, the IRNA news agency reported that the IRGC Aerospace Force downed an MQM-170 drone over Qeshm Island using electronic warfare systems.

On Thursday, the IRGC Navy said it had seized control of another drone of the same type in the western Strait of Hormuz and landed it intact. The US military rejected Iran’s account of Thursday’s incident.

The latest report comes amid ongoing indirect diplomatic contacts between Tehran and Washington.

US, Iran have made progress toward negotiated settlement: Vance

US Vice President JD Vance said on Monday that Washington has made “progress” in talks with Iran, saying he and President Donald Trump feel “pretty good” about reaching a negotiated settlement.

“I actually just spoke with the president of the United States about an hour ago about this,” Vance told reporters. “Look, the president and I both feel pretty good about the prospects for potentially coming to a negotiated settlement. We’re going to keep on working at it.”

“The Iranians are always a little unpredictable, and as the president always says, he retains kinetic options. He retains non-kinetic options, but we’ve certainly made some progress. We’ll see if we can make some more,” he said.

Asked whether Iran had been given a deadline before strikes resume, Vance said: “No, we haven’t set deadlines.”

“Having destroyed their nuclear program, we want to make sure they don’t rebuild it or try to rebuild it. That’s what matters most to the United States,” he said.

“We do think that there is a pathway there, but it really does require a firm commitment and a verifiable commitment that they don’t rebuild that nuclear program,” he added.

Vance's remarks came hours after Trump said at the reopening of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in Washington that Iran wants to make a deal to end the conflict, now in its ninth month.

“They want to make a deal, and that could happen,” Trump said, adding that Iran had asked Washington to stop targeting its leaders, “and we will.”

The latest report comes amid ongoing indirect diplomatic contacts between Tehran and Washington.

US Vice President JD Vance said on Monday that Washington has made “progress” in talks with Iran, saying he and President Donald Trump feel “pretty good” about reaching a negotiated settlement.

“I actually just spoke with the president of the United States about an hour ago about this,” Vance told reporters. “Look, the president and I both feel pretty good about the prospects for potentially coming to a negotiated settlement. We’re going to keep on working at it.”

“The Iranians are always a little unpredictable, and as the president always says, he retains kinetic options. He retains non-kinetic options, but we’ve certainly made some progress. We’ll see if we can make some more,” he said.

Asked whether Iran had been given a deadline before strikes resume, Vance said: “No, we haven’t set deadlines.”

“Having destroyed their nuclear program, we want to make sure they don’t rebuild it or try to rebuild it. That’s what matters most to the United States,” he said.

“We do think that there is a pathway there, but it really does require a firm commitment and a verifiable commitment that they don’t rebuild that nuclear program,” he added.

Vance's remarks came hours after Trump said at the reopening of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in Washington that Iran wants to make a deal to end the conflict, now in its ninth month.

“They want to make a deal, and that could happen,” Trump said, adding that Iran had asked Washington to stop targeting its leaders, “and we will.”

headline: Zverev savours rise to world number one
description: German celebrates a landmark season after adding the French Open and US Open titles to his career achievements
author: AFP
article_text:
German celebrates a landmark season after adding the French Open and US Open titles to his career achievements

Alexander Zverev said Monday that rising to world number one was a special feeling as he heads into the Paris Masters guaranteed to be top of the pile come the end of the year.

German Zverev had been tipped to become one of the dominant forces of men's tennis but a combination of injuries and the rise of Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz had left him without a Grand Slam victory until he triumphed at this year's French Open.

Now 29, Zverev added the US Open to his trophy haul in September and on Monday celebrated on court with the ATP world number one trophy at the Paris Masters, where he is top seed.

"When I won my first Grand Slam, it was different kind of emotions... I had a lot of heartbreaks, a lot of tough moments, I had a lot of losses in the finals. So that was a different kind of feeling," Zverev told reporters.

"To finally make it, it was the biggest relief that I have ever felt in my career. But both trophies are individually special and individually different, because winning a Grand Slam is the biggest tournament that we can win in tennis.

"But this, you have to play the best season for an entire year. It's a completely different feeling, but this feels special, as well."

Zverev will kick off his Paris Masters campaign on Wednesday against Italy's Lorenzo Musetti, with whom he has lost three of his five matches.

headline: Samad to lead Shaheens in Asia Cup Rising Stars
description: Defending champions begin their campaign against UAE on November 20
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
The Pakistan Cricket Board has today announced the 15-member Pakistan Shaheens squad for the upcoming 50-over edition of the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 set to be played in Qatar from 19 to 29 November.

Abdul Samad will lead defending champions Pakistan Shaheens in the tournament where they are placed in Group B alongside India A, Nepal and United Arab Emirates (UAE). Shaheens will begin their campaign against UAE on 20 November and will face India A on 22 and Nepal on 24 November.

The semi-finals of the tournament will be played on 26 and 27 November, while the final will take place on Sunday, 29 November. All of Shaheens’ matches are day-night and will be played at the Eden Park International Stadium except the first one which is a day fixture and is scheduled to be played at the University of Doha Ground.

Apart from skipper Samad, Hasan Nawaz, Maaz Sadaqat, Haider Ali, Shahzaib Khan, Farhan Yousuf, Shamyl Hussain form a strong batting core for the Shaheens with Rohail Nazir listed as the designated wicket-keeper.

Left-arm spin bowling all-rounder Danish Aziz, leg-spinner Saad Masood and Sufyan Moqim are the trio of spinners in the squad. The pace contingent will be led by Mohammad Hasnain and it comprises of Ahmed Daniyal - Shaheens’ super-over hero from the previous edition of the tournament – left-arm pacer Akif Javed and Muhammad Imran Randhawa.

Shaheens won the last 50-over edition of the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars in 2023 in Sri Lanka when they beat India A by 128 runs. Meanwhile, in the previous edition, which was played in T20 format, the Shaheens clinched title by edging Bangladesh A in a thrilling final decided by super-over.

Pakistan were runners-up in the opening two editions of this tournament in 2013 and 2017, while they emerged victorious in 2019. In the 2026 edition, the Group A consists of Afghanistan A, Bangladesh A, Hong Kong China and Sri Lanka A.

15-member squad

Abdul Samad (captain), Ahmed Daniyal, Akif Javed, Danish Aziz, Farhan Yousuf, Haider Ali, Hasan Nawaz, Maaz Sadaqat, Mohammad Hasnain, Muhammad Imran Randhawa, Rohail Nazir (wk), Saad Masood, Shahzaib Khan, Shamyl Hussain, Sufyan Moqim

Pakistan Shaheens fixtures

20 November – 11am PKT - v United Arab Emirates at University of Doha Science and Technology

22 November – 3pm PKT – v India A at West End Park International Cricket Stadium

24 November – 3pm PKT – v Nepal at West End Park International Cricket Stadium

26 November – 3pm PKT – 1st Semi-final at West End Park International Cricket Stadium

27 November – 3pm PKT – 2nd Semi-final at West End Park International Cricket Stadium

29 November – 3pm PKT – Final at West End Park International Cricket Stadium

article_html:
The Pakistan Cricket Board has today announced the 15-member Pakistan Shaheens squad for the upcoming 50-over edition of the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 set to be played in Qatar from 19 to 29 November. 

Abdul Samad will lead defending champions Pakistan Shaheens in the tournament where they are placed in Group B alongside India A, Nepal and United Arab Emirates (UAE). Shaheens will begin their campaign against UAE on 20 November and will face India A on 22 and Nepal on 24 November. 

The semi-finals of the tournament will be played on 26 and 27 November, while the final will take place on Sunday, 29 November. All of Shaheens’ matches are day-night and will be played at the Eden Park International Stadium except the first one which is a day fixture and is scheduled to be played at the University of Doha Ground. 

Apart from skipper Samad, Hasan Nawaz, Maaz Sadaqat, Haider Ali, Shahzaib Khan, Farhan Yousuf, Shamyl Hussain form a strong batting core for the Shaheens with Rohail Nazir listed as the designated wicket-keeper. 

Left-arm spin bowling all-rounder Danish Aziz, leg-spinner Saad Masood and Sufyan Moqim are the trio of spinners in the squad. The pace contingent will be led by Mohammad Hasnain and it comprises of Ahmed Daniyal - Shaheens’ super-over hero from the previous edition of the tournament – left-arm pacer Akif Javed and Muhammad Imran Randhawa. 

Shaheens won the last 50-over edition of the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars in 2023 in Sri Lanka when they beat India A by 128 runs. Meanwhile, in the previous edition, which was played in T20 format, the Shaheens clinched title by edging Bangladesh A in a thrilling final decided by super-over. 

Pakistan were runners-up in the opening two editions of this tournament in 2013 and 2017, while they emerged victorious in 2019. In the 2026 edition, the Group A consists of Afghanistan A, Bangladesh A, Hong Kong China and Sri Lanka A.

headline: 'DWTS' Season 35 Week 8 recap: Disney Night delivers perfect scores and surprise elimination
description: The 8th week featured Broadway-inspired routines of Disney favourites , with Cynthia Erivo as a guest commentator
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Dancing With The Stars Season 35 reached a pivotal stage on Disney Night, as eight remaining couples competed for a place in the next round with individual performances and highly anticipated team dances.

The eighth week of the ABC competition featured Broadway-inspired routines celebrating Disney favourites, including Hercules, Mary Poppins, The Little Mermaid, Tangled and High School Musical. Broadway star Cynthia Erivo joined the ballroom as a special guest commentator.

Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson delivered one of the night's standout performances, earning a perfect 40 out of 40 for their jazz routine to "Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious" from Mary Poppins.

Jenna Dewan and Val Chmerkovskiy also secured their first perfect score of the season, receiving 40 points for their quickstep to "Be Our Guest" from Beauty and the Beast.

Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach impressed the judges with their samba to "Under the Sea", scoring 37 points, while Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov earned 34 for their quickstep inspired by Hercules.

The team dances added another competitive dimension. Team Slaytopia scored 36 points for its performance to "Zoo" from Zootopia 2, while Team Wildcats claimed the highest possible score of 40 for "We're All in This Together" from High School Musical.

Despite strong performances, Julia Stiles and Ezra Sosa were eliminated, bringing their Season 35 journey to an end.

Harry Shum Jr. secured immunity for the following week after winning the cumulative scoring tiebreaker against Jenna Dewan by one point.

The competition continues with Grammy Night next week, returning to its regular Tuesday time slot.

headline: Kane would trade Ballon d'Or for Champions League trophy
description: England striker says team success means more to him than individual recognition ahead of Bayern's clash with Atletico
author: AFP
article_text:
Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane said Monday he would trade that accolade for the Champions League trophy, ahead of Bayern Munich's visit to face Atletico Madrid.

Kane was named the world's best player last week, beating superstars Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to the prestigious award. However the England international said the reason he plays the game is to enjoy success with his team-mates.

"Team trophies are why we play football. The team aspect of our sport is really, really important," Kane told reporters in the Spanish capital.

"The Ballon d'Or last week was one of the best feelings I've had in my life and my career... but to have moments with the team, celebrations with the club, to be able to lift the Champions League with Bayern would be an incredible feeling.

"Of course the Ballon d'Or is a highlight, it puts me on an even bigger level, but you want to have these big finals, the Champions League, having that feeling of emotion with your team-mates as well.

"I would choose the Champions League, but I have the opportunity to do both -- let's see what happens."

The 33-year-old striker was hailed by Atletico coach Diego Simeone as an "incredible player" and "very good for football", before Tuesday's match. "I'd like to thank Diego Simeone, who is one of the best coaches of this era," said Kane.

"I'm proud to receive praise from someone like him. Winning the Ballon d'Or was a huge achievement for me –- I've had to overcome many challenges in my career, some people didn't think I'd get this far... but Simeone will do everything he can to stop me and the team tomorrow."

Bayern have only won one of their first three league phase games, with draws against Arsenal and Viking.

Kane suffered defeat in Atletico's Metropolitano stadium in 2019 when playing in the Champions League final for Tottenham against Liverpool. It is also the venue for this season's final.

"You have good memories in stadiums, sometimes you don't -- hopefully we can have a good memory tomorrow," added Kane.

"I play again here next week with England against Spain, and then hopefully at the end of the year we're back again for the Champions League final.

"So I have a chance and we have a chance to erase that painful memory from 2019 for sure, and that's what you can do in life and football, just take the next opportunity."

New deal

Kane also confirmed he was close to sealing a new deal to keep him in Munich for the foreseeable future.

"I'd say it's more days (than weeks)... we're extremely close now," said Kane, with his current contract expiring in June 2027.

Bayern assistant coach Aaron Danks, who is standing in for Vincent Kompany in the Belgian's absence with illness, said Michael Olise and Manuel Neuer were available after injury issues.

Kompany was released after five days in hospital last week following a collapse in training and subsequent diagnosis of meningeal irritation.

"The most important part of my role in Vinny's absence is to protect everything that we've built over the last two and a half years," said Danks.

"It's to protect the processes that we've put in place, to protect the identity of the team. So no, not too much will change."

MADRID:

Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane said Monday he would trade that accolade for the Champions League trophy, ahead of Bayern Munich's visit to face Atletico Madrid.

Kane was named the world's best player last week, beating superstars Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to the prestigious award.
However the England international said the reason he plays the game is to enjoy success with his team-mates.

"Team trophies are why we play football. The team aspect of our sport is really, really important," Kane told reporters in the Spanish capital.

"The Ballon d'Or last week was one of the best feelings I've had in my life and my career... but to have moments with the team, celebrations with the club, to be able to lift the Champions League with Bayern would be an incredible feeling.

"Of course the Ballon d'Or is a highlight, it puts me on an even bigger level, but you want to have these big finals, the Champions League, having that feeling of emotion with your team-mates as well.

"I would choose the Champions League, but I have the opportunity to do both -- let's see what happens."

The 33-year-old striker was hailed by Atletico coach Diego Simeone as an "incredible player" and "very good for football", before Tuesday's match.
"I'd like to thank Diego Simeone, who is one of the best coaches of this era," said Kane.

"I'm proud to receive praise from someone like him. Winning the Ballon d'Or was a huge achievement for me –- I've had to overcome many challenges in my career, some people didn't think I'd get this far... but Simeone will do everything he can to stop me and the team tomorrow."

Bayern have only won one of their first three league phase games, with draws against Arsenal and Viking.

Kane suffered defeat in Atletico's Metropolitano stadium in 2019 when playing in the Champions League final for Tottenham against Liverpool. It is also the venue for this season's final.

"You have good memories in stadiums, sometimes you don't -- hopefully we can have a good memory tomorrow," added Kane.

"I play again here next week with England against Spain, and then hopefully at the end of the year we're back again for the Champions League final.

"So I have a chance and we have a chance to erase that painful memory from 2019 for sure, and that's what you can do in life and football, just take the next opportunity."

New deal

Kane also confirmed he was close to sealing a new deal to keep him in Munich for the foreseeable future.

"I'd say it's more days (than weeks)... we're extremely close now," said Kane, with his current contract expiring in June 2027.

Bayern assistant coach Aaron Danks, who is standing in for Vincent Kompany in the Belgian's absence with illness, said Michael Olise and Manuel Neuer were available after injury issues.

Kompany was released after five days in hospital last week following a collapse in training and subsequent diagnosis of meningeal irritation.

"The most important part of my role in Vinny's absence is to protect everything that we've built over the last two and a half years," said Danks.

"It's to protect the processes that we've put in place, to protect the identity of the team. So no, not too much will change."
