headline: Demichelis set for Manchester City reunion
description: The former City defender hopes to revive Leipzig's Champions League campaign against his old club
author: AFP
article_text:
Coach Martin Demichelis will be looking to strike a blow against his former employers when his RB Leipzig side host Manchester City in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Former Argentina centre-back Demichelis spent three seasons at Manchester City, winning the 2013-14 Premier League title and two League Cups.

Demichelis, who also won four league titles as a player at Bayern Munich, is now hoping to bring success to Saxony in a budding coaching career.

Leipzig have beaten City just once in six attempts, but may feel Enzo Maresca's men are vulnerable.

In their past three games, City have lost twice and won the other match on penalties, as the spectre of sanctions for breaching financial rules looms.

Demichelis, 45, was controversially handpicked by then-Red Bull boss Jurgen Klopp to take over in the summer.

To bring in Demichelis, Leipzig sacked popular coach Ole Werner, who had taken a young team back into the Champions League, while overseeing the development of Yan Diomande.

Real Madrid paid a reported 125 million euros ($140 million) for Diomande, just a year after Leipzig signed him for 20 million euros.

Demichelis was relegated from La Liga during a short stint with Mallorca last season but Klopp and Leipzig had seen enough to convince them of his ability, after he oversaw a significant up-turn in the club's form.

After a rocky start with Leipzig including a 4-1 loss at Como in the Champions League and a 6-1 thrashing by Bayern Munich, Leipzig have won three games in a row.

The Red Bulls sit just three points off top spot in the Bundesliga, but are in desperate need of points in Europe.

The 2020 semi-finalists are 29th in the 36-team table after winning just one of three Champions League games this campaign.

'Competitive aura'

Demichelis benefited from the tutelage of several big-name coaches, including Louis van Gaal, Manuel Pellegrini, Diego Simeone and his idol Diego Maradona.

Leipzig centre-back Maxime Esteve said Demichelis has brought a "competitive aura" to the club.

"Even in small games in training, you can see that the coach does not want to lose," Esteve told AFP and other media on Monday.

"When he misses something, you can see he's a little bit angry. You can see he stopped playing football not that long ago.

"You can see the aura of his competitiveness."

Esteve played under another former City player, Vincent Kompany, during his time at Burnley and said Demichelis reminds him of the Belgian, who is now coach of Bayern.

"It's funny because they both spend a lot of time in the gym. They want to stay fit, because they have a big history in football.

"They play in games in training and you can see they are quite competitive. They don't want to lose.

"They are really energetic and spend a lot of time at the training ground.

"They are perfectionists and want to sort out the small details as soon as they can."

Esteve also has experience defending against Manchester City talisman Erling Haaland in the Premier League.

The Frenchman acknowledged his side had played against freshly minted Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane only two weeks ago, but called the big Norwegian "the best striker in the world".

"He's so powerful, so good with his head, so quick. He has all of the qualities to be a beast.

"So it will be a difficult game but when you want to progress in football, you have to play against the best opponents. And you want to perform in this type of game."

"He's so powerful, so good with his head, so quick. He has all of the qualities to be a beast.
"So it will be a difficult game but when you want to progress in football, you have to play against the best opponents. And you want to perform in this type of game."

headline: Judge blocks Trump administration from pressuring states over noncitizen voting
description: Ruling marks latest in series of legal setbacks ​for Trump's efforts to assert control over election administration
author: Reuters
article_text:
A US judge on Monday temporarily barred the Trump administration from moving ahead with a plan it says would prevent noncitizen voting, but that critics say risks disenfranchising eligible voters and ​infringing on states' authority over elections.

US District Judge Tanya Chutkan barred the Justice Department and the Department ‌of Homeland Security from sending states lists of registered voters the administration says may not be citizens, and from asking state election officials to separate those voters' ballots or not count them until citizenship is proven.

The ruling marks the latest in a series of legal setbacks ​for US President Donald Trump's efforts to assert federal control over election administration ahead of the November 3 midterms. Trump's fellow ​Republicans are battling to retain majorities in both houses of Congress.

However, the Trump administration notched a ⁠victory on Monday in a separate case where a panel of the San Francisco-based 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals ​cleared the government to threaten state and local election officials with prosecution if they did not comply with demands related to ​voting by alleged noncitizens. Chutkan is not bound by that ruling.

Noncitizen voting is illegal, and all available evidence shows that it is exceedingly rare. But Trump, who falsely asserts that his loss in the 2020 presidential election was due to fraud, has long accused states — which are responsible ​for administering elections — of facilitating noncitizen voting.

Over the past month, the Trump administration ramped up a pressure campaign against election officials ​over alleged noncitizen voting by sending letters to officials in California and Washington state demanding they not count any ballots from people on lists of ‌voters ⁠the administration said may not be citizens.

In response, voting rights and privacy advocates asked Chutkan to temporarily prevent the Trump administration from sending such lists to states and making such demands. The plaintiffs alleged the administration was violating the Privacy Act of 1974, which restricts the federal government's ability to disclose sensitive private information.

The Justice Department said in a court filing on Saturday ​that its letters to California ​and Washington were part of ⁠an effort to enforce a federal law banning noncitizen voting and did not amount to a distinct policy subject to review by a federal court.

Earlier this week, a federal judge in ​Los Angeles rejected the Justice Department's request to order California to temporarily set aside mailed ballots ​from more than ⁠20,000 registered voters it said were likely not citizens.

Chutkan, a Washington, DC-based appointee of former Democratic President Barack Obama, said the administration's data may not be reliable, meaning there was a risk that lawfully registered voters would be disenfranchised. An appeals court rejected on Friday ⁠the department's ​request for an emergency order pending appeal.

Also on Friday, a federal judge ​in San Francisco ordered the Justice Department to stop threatening to prosecute state and local election officials who do not comply with the Trump administration's demands over ​alleged noncitizen voting.

headline: US voters head to polls to deliver midterm verdict on Trump
description: All 435 seats in the US House of Representatives are up for election, along with 35 of the Senate's 100 seats
author: Reuters
article_text:
Americans headed to the polls in Tuesday's midterm elections to deliver a verdict on the first two years of President Donald Trump's second term, with surveys and nonpartisan analysts favouring Democrats to wrest the House of Representatives from Republicans while control of the Senate remains uncertain.

The battle for the Senate is unfolding across nearly 10 closely contested statewide races, most in ​Republican strongholds.

History is against Trump's Republicans: the sitting president's party has lost ground in Congress in all but two midterm elections since World War Two. Trump's approval rating is hovering near his all-time lows, dragged down by deep voter frustration over ‌the war with Iran and the resulting rise in fuel prices.

There is little doubt this year's election is all about Trump, the central US political figure for most of the last decade. Trump himself has told his supporters repeatedly to "pretend I'm on the ballot", a message Democratic leaders have happily echoed.

Trump, in a television interview on Tuesday morning, boasted of what he billed as his achievements in Venezuela and Iran and declared optimism for fellow Republicans in an election he has said should be treated as if he were on the ballot himself.

"I think the results are going to be better than you think," he told Fox News, adding that he would be watching the results ​come in later Tuesday night at the White House, where he is hosting a viewing reception.

In remarks that appeared aimed at swaying largely Democratic-leaning voters unhappy with US support for Israel, Trump said that Washington would stop $4 billion in annual funding to Israel after ​the end of this year.

US policy toward Israel has been a particular focus in Michigan, where progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed is running a closely watched campaign for Senate.

The president has sought to energise his ⁠base with more than two dozen campaign rallies since the start of October, the vast majority in states he easily won in 2024, underscoring the extent to which Republicans are playing defence.

Led by Trump, Republicans have portrayed Democratic candidates as radical, un-American and even communist.

"The Democrat Party has ​nominated the most extreme and dangerous slate of candidates in American history," Trump said on Monday during a speech in Washington.

But opinion polls show voters are most concerned about affordability, and disapprove of Trump's handling of the issue, after his sweeping tariff policy and his decision to attack ​Iran in February increased domestic costs. Republican candidates, meanwhile, have struggled to distance themselves from a president who demands fealty and rarely acknowledges mistakes.

All 435 seats in the US House of Representatives are up for election, along with 35 of the Senate's 100 seats, though the majority of contests are not considered competitive. Democrats must flip at least three House seats and four Senate seats to win a majority in each chamber.

Democrats have little margin for error. The party must defend all of its current seats while winning at least two states that voted for Trump by a double-digit margin two years ago: Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, Ohio, South Carolina ​and Texas.

Opinion polls show Democrats either narrowly leading or within striking distance in all of those states.

Michigan race roiled by cross-party endorsement

The Michigan Senate contest between El-Sayed, 42, and Republican former US Representative Mike Rogers, 63, received a fresh jolt on Sunday when Democrat Haley Stevens, who narrowly lost ​to El-Sayed in the party's primary election, endorsed Rogers in a surprise reversal.

In addition to the implications for Senate control, the Michigan race represents a high-profile test of whether Republicans' identity-based attacks – El-Sayed would be the nation's first Muslim senator — prove effective in a battleground state.

A win for El-Sayed, who has criticised ‌Israel and supports liberal ⁠policies such as universal healthcare, would also be seen as a boost for the party's left wing ahead of the 2028 presidential election.

The Alaska Senate race has been caught up in its own turmoil, after The New York Times reported that the campaign of Democratic candidate Mary Peltola, 53, helped recruit a third candidate who shares the first and last name of her Republican opponent, Dan Sullivan, 61.

Peltola has denied involvement. Trump's Justice Department has launched a criminal probe into the allegations and filed a lawsuit to block certification of the election results, though a judge dismissed the latter effort.

In Texas, Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico, 37, has his party once again dreaming of winning the biggest Republican state after decades of heartbreak. His scandal-plagued opponent, Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton, 63, has benefited from a nine-figure investment from the world's richest man, Elon Musk, who has spent hundreds of millions of ​dollars boosting Republicans.

In Kansas, Democrat Adam Hamilton, 62, a megachurch pastor, ​holds a narrow polling lead over Republican US Senator Roger ⁠Marshall, 66. The state voted for Trump by more than 16 percentage points in 2024 and has not elected a Democratic senator in nearly a century.

And in Maine, Republican US Senator Susan Collins, 73, is once again seeking to defy the Democratic leanings of her home state and win a sixth term. She faces Democrat Troy Jackson, 58, a former state senate president who unexpectedly became the nominee after Democratic oyster farmer Graham Platner dropped ​out amid accusations of misconduct, which he denied.

Other competitive Senate races are taking place in Iowa, Nebraska, Ohio and South Carolina, all Republican-held seats.

Trump's Justice Department intervenes

The US Justice Department said on Tuesday ​it was deploying 1,000 election monitors and ⁠observers to all 50 states in what it called the largest Election Day monitoring effort in history.

Department officials have said priorities include areas with a history of voter access issues and places with competitive races that could be targets of voter intimidation.

There are 47 US House races widely seen as competitive, according to a Reuters analysis of the leading election forecasters. If the other contests all proceed as predicted, Democrats would need to win only 13 of the competitive races to secure a majority.

The fight for the House has been waged largely on Republican turf, including some districts Trump carried by double digits in ⁠2024. A Trump-backed ​Republican effort to redraw districts in several states to make them safer for the party appears not to have yielded the gains the White House expected.

Democrats have warned that ​Trump, who has long falsely claimed that US elections are rigged, may attempt to challenge Tuesday's results if Republicans lose.

In addition to its actions in Alaska, Trump's Justice Department also filed a lawsuit in California to block ballots it says may be invalid, a break from decades of practice meant to insulate elections from political influence. The US Supreme Court on ​Monday rejected the administration's request for an emergency order in the case.

Three dozen governors' races will also take place on Tuesday, as well as thousands of state-level legislative contests and ballot measures on issues from a billionaires' tax to abortion rights.

Americans headed to the polls in Tuesday's midterm elections to deliver a verdict on the first two years of President Donald Trump's second term, with surveys and nonpartisan analysts favouring Democrats to wrest the House of Representatives from Republicans while control of the Senate remains uncertain.

The battle for the Senate is unfolding across nearly 10 closely contested statewide races, most in ​Republican strongholds.

History is against Trump's Republicans: the sitting president's party has lost ground in Congress in all but two midterm elections since World War Two. Trump's approval rating is hovering near his all-time lows, dragged down by deep voter frustration over ‌the war with Iran and the resulting rise in fuel prices.

Voting kicks off in Virginia as polls open across the United States in midterm elections that will serve as a referendum on President Donald Trump’s first two years back in office, with voter frustration over the Iran war and the resulting rise in fuel prices emerging as a key… pic.twitter.com/oV53W7D6sR

— Al Arabiya English (@AlArabiya_Eng) November 3, 2026

There is little doubt this year's election is all about Trump, the central US political figure for most of the last decade. Trump himself has told his supporters repeatedly to "pretend I'm on the ballot", a message Democratic leaders have happily echoed.

TRUMP: “I’m just asking everybody to pretend that I’m on the ballot.”

With Election Day just hours away, President Trump delivers his final message to voters during an appearance on “Hannity,” urging Republicans to turn out in the high-stakes midterm elections.

Trump warns that… pic.twitter.com/4DJh9IzlqG

— Fox News (@FoxNews) November 3, 2026

Trump, in a television interview on Tuesday morning, boasted of what he billed as his achievements in Venezuela and Iran and declared optimism for fellow Republicans in an election he has said should be treated as if he were on the ballot himself.

"I think the results are going to be better than you think," he told Fox News, adding that he would be watching the results ​come in later Tuesday night at the White House, where he is hosting a viewing reception.

TRUMP: “What we’ve done is amazing.”

President Trump defends Operation Midnight Hammer during an Election Eve interview with @seanhannity, claiming the U.S. has destroyed Iran’s military and navy.

“Their military is gone, the navy is gone, their air force is gone, their… pic.twitter.com/rdp6Z4qVz2

— Fox News (@FoxNews) November 3, 2026

In remarks that appeared aimed at swaying largely Democratic-leaning voters unhappy with US support for Israel, Trump said that Washington would stop $4 billion in annual funding to Israel after ​the end of this year.

BREAKING: President Trump says the U.S. will end roughly $4 billion in annual aid to Israel by the end of the year, revealing that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu agreed to the decision.

“Because they don’t need it,” Trump said during an exclusive interview on @foxandfriends,… pic.twitter.com/ItBUcMrtuZ

— Fox News (@FoxNews) November 3, 2026

Read: Trump says US will stop $4 billion in funding to Israel at end of 2026

US policy toward Israel has been a particular focus in Michigan, where progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed is running a closely watched campaign for Senate.

The president has sought to energise his ⁠base with more than two dozen campaign rallies since the start of October, the vast majority in states he easily won in 2024, underscoring the extent to which Republicans are playing defence.

Led by Trump, Republicans have portrayed Democratic candidates as radical, un-American and even communist.

"The Democrat Party has ​nominated the most extreme and dangerous slate of candidates in American history," Trump said on Monday during a speech in Washington.

But opinion polls show voters are most concerned about affordability, and disapprove of Trump's handling of the issue, after his sweeping tariff policy and his decision to attack ​Iran in February increased domestic costs. Republican candidates, meanwhile, have struggled to distance themselves from a president who demands fealty and rarely acknowledges mistakes.

All 435 seats in the US House of Representatives are up for election, along with 35 of the Senate's 100 seats, though the majority of contests are not considered competitive. Democrats must flip at least three House seats and four Senate seats to win a majority in each chamber.

Democrats have little margin for error. The party must defend all of its current seats while winning at least two states that voted for Trump by a double-digit margin two years ago: Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, Ohio, South Carolina ​and Texas.

Opinion polls show Democrats either narrowly leading or within striking distance in all of those states.

Michigan race roiled by cross-party endorsement

The Michigan Senate contest between El-Sayed, 42, and Republican former US Representative Mike Rogers, 63, received a fresh jolt on Sunday when Democrat Haley Stevens, who narrowly lost ​to El-Sayed in the party's primary election, endorsed Rogers in a surprise reversal.

I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today. pic.twitter.com/pQgfSBuhOJ

— Haley Stevens (@HaleyforMI) November 1, 2026

In addition to the implications for Senate control, the Michigan race represents a high-profile test of whether Republicans' identity-based attacks – El-Sayed would be the nation's first Muslim senator — prove effective in a battleground state.

A win for El-Sayed, who has criticised ‌Israel and supports liberal ⁠policies such as universal healthcare, would also be seen as a boost for the party's left wing ahead of the 2028 presidential election.

Read More: Michigan Senate race a test of attacks on Muslim candidate, progressive agenda

The Alaska Senate race has been caught up in its own turmoil, after The New York Times reported that the campaign of Democratic candidate Mary Peltola, 53, helped recruit a third candidate who shares the first and last name of her Republican opponent, Dan Sullivan, 61.

Peltola has denied involvement. Trump's Justice Department has launched a criminal probe into the allegations and filed a lawsuit to block certification of the election results, though a judge dismissed the latter effort.

In Texas, Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico, 37, has his party once again dreaming of winning the biggest Republican state after decades of heartbreak. His scandal-plagued opponent, Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton, 63, has benefited from a nine-figure investment from the world's richest man, Elon Musk, who has spent hundreds of millions of ​dollars boosting Republicans.

In Kansas, Democrat Adam Hamilton, 62, a megachurch pastor, ​holds a narrow polling lead over Republican US Senator Roger ⁠Marshall, 66. The state voted for Trump by more than 16 percentage points in 2024 and has not elected a Democratic senator in nearly a century.

And in Maine, Republican US Senator Susan Collins, 73, is once again seeking to defy the Democratic leanings of her home state and win a sixth term. She faces Democrat Troy Jackson, 58, a former state senate president who unexpectedly became the nominee after Democratic oyster farmer Graham Platner dropped ​out amid accusations of misconduct, which he denied.

Other competitive Senate races are taking place in Iowa, Nebraska, Ohio and South Carolina, all Republican-held seats.

Trump's Justice Department intervenes

The US Justice Department said on Tuesday ​it was deploying 1,000 election monitors and ⁠observers to all 50 states in what it called the largest Election Day monitoring effort in history.

Department officials have said priorities include areas with a history of voter access issues and places with competitive races that could be targets of voter intimidation.

There are 47 US House races widely seen as competitive, according to a Reuters analysis of the leading election forecasters. If the other contests all proceed as predicted, Democrats would need to win only 13 of the competitive races to secure a majority.

The fight for the House has been waged largely on Republican turf, including some districts Trump carried by double digits in ⁠2024. A Trump-backed ​Republican effort to redraw districts in several states to make them safer for the party appears not to have yielded the gains the White House expected.

Democrats have warned that ​Trump, who has long falsely claimed that US elections are rigged, may attempt to challenge Tuesday's results if Republicans lose.

In addition to its actions in Alaska, Trump's Justice Department also filed a lawsuit in California to block ballots it says may be invalid, a break from decades of practice meant to insulate elections from political influence. The US Supreme Court on ​Monday rejected the administration's request for an emergency order in the case.

Three dozen governors' races will also take place on Tuesday, as well as thousands of state-level legislative contests and ballot measures on issues from a billionaires' tax to abortion rights.

There are 47 US House races widely seen as competitive, according to a Reuters analysis of the leading election forecasters. If the other contests all proceed as predicted, Democrats would need to win only 13 of those 46 races to secure a majority.

The fight for the House has been waged largely on Republican turf, including some districts Trump carried by double digits in 2024. A Trump-backed Republican effort to redraw districts in several states ⁠to make them safer for the party appears not to have yielded the gains the White House expected.

Democrats have warned that Trump, who has long falsely claimed that US elections are rigged, may attempt to challenge Tuesday's results if Republicans lose.

In addition to its actions in Alaska, Trump's Justice Department also filed a lawsuit in California to block ballots it says may be invalid, a break from decades of practice meant to insulate elections from political influence. The US Supreme Court on Monday rejected the administration's request for an emergency order in the case.

Three dozen governors' races will also take place on Tuesday, as well as thousands of state-level legislative contests and ballot measures on everything from a billionaires' tax to abortion rights.

Economic discontent

Republicans insist that Trump's tax cuts and immigration crackdown will benefit Americans, and they are portraying Democratic candidates as left-wing radicals.

But in his final public campaign appearance Monday, Trump barely touched on the economy and spent most of the time in a rambling talk about his problem-plagued renovation of Washington's Reflecting Pool.

"This is the last day before the midterm elections, the most important midterm I believe in our lifetime," he said, 26 minutes into the speech, before quickly returning to talking about renovations.

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer branded it a "pathetic closing message."

Some Republican supporters remain confident.

"We're going to win. As a matter of fact, we've probably already won," Texas military veteran Yvonne Clouser told AFP.

But while Republicans hold a 53-47 Senate majority, the battlefield is extending into conservative states like Kansas, Texas, Iowa, Ohio and Alaska.

Decision Desk HQ's final forecast projected 241 House seats for Democrats against 194 for Republicans, and a narrower 52-48 Democratic Senate majority.

Polls can underestimate one party's support, and Republicans hope their voters turn out in force on Election Day.

More than 57 million Americans had already voted early before Tuesday, indicating the high energy.

The campaign has attracted more than $11 billion in political advertising, while billionaire Trump ally Elon Musk has poured hundreds of millions of dollars into Republican political efforts.

As soon as polls close, concerns will mount over whether results will be accepted by the Republicans.

Trump, who tried to overturn his 2020 election defeat, has repeatedly alleged widespread voter fraud and accused Democrats -- with no evidence -- of cheating.

The Justice Department, run by a close Trump ally, has already sued to potentially block certification of Alaska's Senate race if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan narrowly loses, although a court ruled against the effort on the eve of the election.

Trump, who will watch the midterm results at the White House on Tuesday night, signalled that if he does lose control of Congress, he could simply defy Democrats.

"I veto everything," he told a podcast Monday, although he said he might strike deals with Democrats eventually.

Americans headed to the polls in Tuesday's midterm elections to deliver a verdict on the first two years of President Donald Trump's second term, with surveys and nonpartisan analysts favouring Democrats to wrest the House of Representatives from Republicans while control of the Senate remains uncertain.

The battle for the Senate is unfolding across nearly 10 closely contested statewide races, most in Republican strongholds.

History is against Trump's Republicans: the sitting president's party has lost ground in Congress in all but two midterm elections since World War Two. Trump's approval rating is hovering near his all-time lows, dragged down by deep voter frustration over ‌the war with Iran and the resulting rise in fuel prices.

There is little doubt this year's election is all about Trump, the central US political figure for most of the last decade. Trump himself has told his supporters repeatedly to "pretend I'm on the ballot", a message Democratic leaders have happily echoed.

Trump, in a television interview on Tuesday morning, boasted of what he billed as his achievements in Venezuela and Iran and declared optimism for fellow Republicans in an election he has said should be treated as if he were on the ballot himself.

"I think the results are going to be better than you think," he told Fox News, adding that he would be watching the results come in later Tuesday night at the White House, where he is hosting a viewing reception.

In remarks that appeared aimed at swaying largely Democratic-leaning voters unhappy with US support for Israel, Trump said that Washington would stop $4 billion in annual funding to Israel after the end of this year.

US policy toward Israel has been a particular focus in Michigan, where progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed is running a closely watched campaign for Senate.

The president has sought to energise his ⁠base with more than two dozen campaign rallies since the start of October, the vast majority in states he easily won in 2024, underscoring the extent to which Republicans are playing defence.

Led by Trump, Republicans have portrayed Democratic candidates as radical, un-American and even communist.

"The Democrat Party has nominated the most extreme and dangerous slate of candidates in American history," Trump said on Monday during a speech in Washington.

But opinion polls show voters are most concerned about affordability, and disapprove of Trump's handling of the issue, after his sweeping tariff policy and his decision to attack Iran in February increased domestic costs. Republican candidates, meanwhile, have struggled to distance themselves from a president who demands fealty and rarely acknowledges mistakes.

All 435 seats in the US House of Representatives are up for election, along with 35 of the Senate's 100 seats, though the majority of contests are not considered competitive. Democrats must flip at least three House seats and four Senate seats to win a majority in each chamber.

Democrats have little margin for error. The party must defend all of its current seats while winning at least two states that voted for Trump by a double-digit margin two years ago: Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, Ohio, South Carolina and Texas.

Opinion polls show Democrats either narrowly leading or within striking distance in all of those states.

The Michigan Senate contest between El-Sayed, 42, and Republican former US Representative Mike Rogers, 63, received a fresh jolt on Sunday when Democrat Haley Stevens, who narrowly lost to El-Sayed in the party's primary election, endorsed Rogers in a surprise reversal.

In addition to the implications for Senate control, the Michigan race represents a high-profile test of whether Republicans' identity-based attacks – El-Sayed would be the nation's first Muslim senator — prove effective in a battleground state.

A win for El-Sayed, who has criticised ‌Israel and supports liberal ⁠policies such as universal healthcare, would also be seen as a boost for the party's left wing ahead of the 2028 presidential election.

headline: Two policemen martyred, one injured in attack on polio team in K-P's Mohmand
description: One personnel injured as Naqvi condemns 'unacceptable' incident, says elements involved do not deserve any leniency
author: Ali Murad
article_text:
Two policemen were martyred, and another was injured when unidentified armed men attacked a polio vaccination team in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's (K-P) Mohmand district on Tuesday, District Police Officer (DPO) Raza Muhammad Khan said.

The DPO said one terrorist was also injured in the incident while a search operation was underway following the attack.

The attack took place in the Tamanzai area, within the jurisdiction of Pandiali Police Station, during an anti-polio vaccination campaign. Police identified the martyred personnel as Zahoor and Arabi, while the injured officer was named Sabir.

President Asif Ali Zardari condemned the incident, expressing "profound grief and sorrow" over the martyrdom of the police personnel, paying tribute to their "dedication, bravery, and national services."

According to a post on X, President Zardari stated that the targeting of personnel performing their duties in the anti-polio campaign "to protect children" was "extremely regrettable and condemnable:"

He expressed heartfelt sympathy and condolences to the families of the martyrs, while extending prayers for the swift recovery of the injured personnel.

"Police personnel deployed to protect polio teams are performing a national duty; their sacrifices will not be forgotten," President Zardari said.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi condemned the firing on the personnel deployed on anti-polio duty, paying tribute to the two policemen martyred in the incident. Naqvi expressed "heartfelt sympathy and condolences to the families of the martyred," the statement said.

"The policemen deployed to protect polio workers are striving for our healthy future," Naqvi said. He also termed the incident "unacceptable," saying that "the elements involved in the firing do not deserve any leniency."

Earlier, four polio workers were abducted by unidentified armed men after being subjected to gunfire in the Tank district, while two other members of a polio vaccination team, who had been kidnapped in Lower South Waziristan, were subsequently released.

The incident in Tank occurred in the village of Jious, located in the Sheikh Attar union council, where unidentified armed men abducted four polio workers. The gunmen reportedly took all four workers to an undisclosed location.

In a separate incident, two members of a polio vaccination team were abducted by armed men in the Azam Warsak area of Lower South Waziristan. Sources said armed men affiliated with the proscribed Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) were allegedly involved in the kidnapping. However, both polio workers were later released.

The incidents came amid a special anti-polio campaign launched on November 2 in 97 selected districts across the country. According to the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) for Polio Eradication, the campaign will continue until November 8.

NEOC confirmed Pakistan’s seventh polio case of the year, reported from Khyber district of K-P. The affected child was a 13-month-old girl belonging to Jan Baz Union Council in Bara tehsil, the NEOC said. This was the second polio case reported from Khyber district this year and the sixth from K-P.

headline: Dortmund bring back painful memories for Pellegrini
description: The former Manchester City boss returns to Germany 13 years
author: AFP
article_text:
Veteran Real Betis coach Manuel Pellegrini has regularly produced impressive results at the highest level but his failure to win the Champions League means some hesitate to place him among the managerial elite.

The 73-year-old's team boast three wins from three in the league phase ahead of Wednesday's visit to face Borussia Dortmund, the scene of one of the most agonising defeats in his long career.

In 2013 Pellegrini's Malaga conceded twice in injury time against Jurgen Klopp's Dortmund, to miss out on a Champions League semi-final berth.

It was an especially cruel defeat for Pellegrini, who had attended his father's funeral in Chile before landing in Germany on the morning of the match.

"They did not want us in the semi-finals," complained Pellegrini about the officiating afterwards, with Felipe Santana's winner seemingly scored from an offside position.

That summer Pellegrini moved to Manchester City, winning the Premier League and two League Cups before departing in 2016, without a Champions League trophy.

The evergreen Chilean joined Betis in 2020 and is now enjoying the longest spell in charge of a club in his career. Pellegrini has stayed faithful to the idea that his teams must entertain and Betis fit the bill, boasting a host of exciting attackers like Isco and Ez Abde.

Pellegrini, who graduated in civil engineering in 1979 while playing at Universidad de Chile, took Betis to their first final in 17 years, winning the Copa del Rey in 2022.

Last season he steered the Andalusians back to Champions League qualification after two decades away from the elite.

"We started the first match of the season... and at the end of the team talk we wrote in green letters -- 'today we begin our journey to the Champions League'," explained Pellegrini in May.

'My own' way

Pellegrini returning Betis to the big-time is no surprise, given his track record.

The coach turned Villarreal into a Champions League semi-finalist in 2006, with his team knocked out by Arsenal.

Juan Roman Riquelme missed a last-gasp penalty in the second leg which could have taken the game to extra-time on Spain's east coast.

Pellegrini led Villarreal to a second-place finish in La Liga in 2008, finishing above giants Barcelona and Atletico Madrid.

His success earned him the Real Madrid job in 2009, where he achieved a then-club record 96 points, but was sacked at the end of the season to make way for Jose Mourinho.

Madrid chief Florentino Perez was desperate for the club's 10th Champions League trophy and thought the Portuguese would deliver it. Later at City, he was replaced by Pep Guardiola.

After Madrid, Pellegrini helped Malaga reach the Champions League for the first and only time in their history, with their journey ending in Dortmund.

"Manuel Pellegrini doesn't always get the recognition he deserves, because he has had an incredible career and achieved huge success," said Lille coach Davide Ancelotti in September.

"Those of us who are just starting out, like me, have immense admiration for him. I don't know if I'll manage until his age. I tell myself it's impossible."

Betis beat Lille 3-2 in a thriller before going on to overcome Porto and Feyenoord to maintain their perfect European start.

Pellegrini's side have qualified for European football for six straight seasons and in 2025, reached their first ever European final, in the Conference League, where they were defeated by Chelsea.

Betis beat Malaga on Saturday in La Liga in a happier reunion for Pellegrini than the trip to Dortmund.

"They were three unforgettable years (in charge)," said Pellegrini, who has never believed silverware should be the only measure of a coach or team's success.

"I don't take a team to see how many titles I win, but to improve what happened before and do it in my own way," explained the coach back in 2016.

Fans of Villarreal, Malaga and now Betis, enjoying some of their greatest days under his reign, would likely agree with his approach.

BARCELONA:

Veteran Real Betis coach Manuel Pellegrini has regularly produced impressive results at the highest level but his failure to win the Champions League means some hesitate to place him among the managerial elite.

The 73-year-old's team boast three wins from three in the league phase ahead of Wednesday's visit to face Borussia Dortmund, the scene of one of the most agonising defeats in his long career.

It was an especially cruel defeat for Pellegrini, who had attended his father's funeral in Chile before landing in Germany on the morning of the match.

"They did not want us in the semi-finals," complained Pellegrini about the officiating afterwards, with Felipe Santana's winner seemingly scored from an offside position.

That summer Pellegrini moved to Manchester City, winning the Premier League and two League Cups before departing in 2016, without a Champions League trophy.

The evergreen Chilean joined Betis in 2020 and is now enjoying the longest spell in charge of a club in his career.
Pellegrini has stayed faithful to the idea that his teams must entertain and Betis fit the bill, boasting a host of exciting attackers like Isco and Ez Abde.

Pellegrini, who graduated in civil engineering in 1979 while playing at Universidad de Chile, took Betis to their first final in 17 years, winning the Copa del Rey in 2022.

Last season he steered the Andalusians back to Champions League qualification after two decades away from the elite.

"We started the first match of the season... and at the end of the team talk we wrote in green letters -- 'today we begin our journey to the Champions League'," explained Pellegrini in May.

'My own' way

Pellegrini returning Betis to the big-time is no surprise, given his track record.

The coach turned Villarreal into a Champions League semi-finalist in 2006, with his team knocked out by Arsenal.

Juan Roman Riquelme missed a last-gasp penalty in the second leg which could have taken the game to extra-time on Spain's east coast.

Pellegrini led Villarreal to a second-place finish in La Liga in 2008, finishing above giants Barcelona and Atletico Madrid.

His success earned him the Real Madrid job in 2009, where he achieved a then-club record 96 points, but was sacked at the end of the season to make way for Jose Mourinho.

Madrid chief Florentino Perez was desperate for the club's 10th Champions League trophy and thought the Portuguese would deliver it.
Later at City, he was replaced by Pep Guardiola.

After Madrid, Pellegrini helped Malaga reach the Champions League for the first and only time in their history, with their journey ending in Dortmund.

"Manuel Pellegrini doesn't always get the recognition he deserves, because he has had an incredible career and achieved huge success," said Lille coach Davide Ancelotti in September.

"Those of us who are just starting out, like me, have immense admiration for him. I don't know if I'll manage until his age. I tell myself it's impossible."

Betis beat Lille 3-2 in a thriller before going on to overcome Porto and Feyenoord to maintain their perfect European start.

Pellegrini's side have qualified for European football for six straight seasons and in 2025, reached their first ever European final, in the Conference League, where they were defeated by Chelsea.

Betis beat Malaga on Saturday in La Liga in a happier reunion for Pellegrini than the trip to Dortmund.

"They were three unforgettable years (in charge)," said Pellegrini, who has never believed silverware should be the only measure of a coach or team's success.

"I don't take a team to see how many titles I win, but to improve what happened before and do it in my own way," explained the coach back in 2016.

Fans of Villarreal, Malaga and now Betis, enjoying some of their greatest days under his reign, would likely agree with his approach.

The 73-year-old's team boast three wins from three in the league phase ahead of Wednesday's visit to face Borussia Dortmund, the scene of one of the most agonising defeats in his long career.
In 2013 Pellegrini's Malaga conceded twice in injury time against Jurgen Klopp's Dortmund, to miss out on a Champions League semi-final berth.
It was an especially cruel defeat for Pellegrini, who had attended his father's funeral in Chile before landing in Germany on the morning of the match.
"They did not want us in the semi-finals," complained Pellegrini about the officiating afterwards, with Felipe Santana's winner seemingly scored from an offside position.
That summer Pellegrini moved to Manchester City, winning the Premier League and two League Cups before departing in 2016, without a Champions League trophy.

The evergreen Chilean joined Betis in 2020 and is now enjoying the longest spell in charge of a club in his career.

Pellegrini has stayed faithful to the idea that his teams must entertain and Betis fit the bill, boasting a host of exciting attackers like Isco and Ez Abde.
Pellegrini, who graduated in civil engineering in 1979 while playing at Universidad de Chile, took Betis to their first final in 17 years, winning the Copa del Rey in 2022.
Last season he steered the Andalusians back to Champions League qualification after two decades away from the elite.
"We started the first match of the season... and at the end of the team talk we wrote in green letters -- 'today we begin our journey to the Champions League'," explained Pellegrini in May.

The coach turned Villarreal into a Champions League semi-finalist in 2006, with his team knocked out by Arsenal.
Juan Roman Riquelme missed a last-gasp penalty in the second leg which could have taken the game to extra-time on Spain's east coast.
Pellegrini led Villarreal to a second-place finish in La Liga in 2008, finishing above giants Barcelona and Atletico Madrid.

headline: Russian strikes kill 26 in Ukraine after longest ceasefire ends
description: Russia targeted a village in Zaporizhzhia, adjacent to Kherson, with repeated strikes
author: AFP
article_text:
Russia said its emergency warnings app came under a "massive cyberattack" on Monday, hours after Ukraine reported a hack in an apparent exchange of blows between the foes, as their longest truce came to an end.

Moscow's emergency ministry said hackers posted "false information" on the app, which is designed to warn the public of incoming drone attacks and other threats.

Hours earlier, Ukraine said it suspected its air raid alert system had been compromised, after baseless alerts of a radiation threat appeared on the app.

The cyberattacks came as the longest truce of the war, limited to Ukraine's eastern Kherson region, ended on Sunday after Russia refused the offer of an extension, according to Kyiv.

Moscow did not immediately say who was behind the attack on its app, while Ukraine's Centre for Strategic Communications SPRAVDI blamed the hack it suffered on Russia.

The rare pause in fighting, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump and which began early Tuesday, had enabled a humanitarian mission to the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky as the war grinds through its fifth year.

"The ceasefire, which was in effect from October 27 to November 1, has ended," Ukraine's Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights, Dmytro Lubinets, said.

He called the temporary truce "an important step in our joint humanitarian efforts" with Russia.

US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine are set to resume this month, having been effectively frozen since the United States and Israel launched joint strikes on Iran in February.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Sunday his country would stop hitting Russian oil refineries – as US counterpart Donald Trump has demanded – if Washington provided Kyiv with powerful Patriot interceptor missiles.

Raid alert app hack

Kherson regional governor Oleksandr Prokudin warned local people to be particularly vigilant when the ceasefire ended and to "respond immediately to warnings about Russian attacks".

"The Air Alarm application has probably been subjected to hostile interference," Ukraine's air force said in a message. "There is no radiation threat."

Air force spokesperson Yuriy Ignat confirmed to AFP that the app had been hacked.

Hours later, Russia's emergency ministry said its teams were working to fix a "massive cyberattack" which was "enabling attackers to send false information to the public".

'Worse than before'

Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022 has destroyed parts of eastern and southern Ukraine, left hundreds of thousands of soldiers and civilians dead and forced millions to flee their homes.

AFP spoke to several Kherson residents, one of whom said the ceasefire had been a "breath of fresh air".

"We have to use this time to get things done," said Volodymyr Omeltchenko, a 38-year-old gardener, before the truce ended.

"We're pruning the rose bushes for winter."

Pope Leo, who had pressed Russia for a truce in Oleshky, had said he hoped the temporary pause would "strengthen the desire for dialogue and lead to new concrete peace initiatives".

A Ukrainian military officer, speaking on condition of anonymity, expressed concern that the fighting would be "worse than before" when it resumed.

Russian forces on the other side of the Dnipro River had taken advantage of the calm of the past few days to amass new troops, transport ammunition stocks and collect intelligence on Ukrainian positions using surveillance drones, the officer said.

Oil attacks

Russia and Ukraine exchanged strikes elsewhere on Sunday.

Russia said a drone had struck an "industrial enterprise" east of Moscow overnight, with Ukrainian media reporting that Kyiv had attacked the Kstovo oil refinery.

Kyiv has repeatedly struck Russian oil and gas sites, in what it says is fair retaliation for Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

Trump has been pressing Kyiv to stop the attacks, blaming them for rising diesel costs that analysts attribute to the Iran war.

Zelensky said on Fox News on Sunday that he told Trump and his team: "If you want us not to attack Russia's refineries, they have not to attack our energy system."

"Another alternative, give us Patriot missiles," he said.

Ukraine's energy ministry reported fresh power outages across the country Sunday, including in Kyiv, following Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

headline: Hila Klein files for divorce from 'H3 Podcast' co-host Ethan Klein following affair allegation
description: According to documents, Hila filed the divorce papers, listing October 13 as their date of separation
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Hila Klein has filed for divorce from her husband, YouTuber and podcast host Ethan Klein, following allegations of infidelity that have brought their 14-year marriage to an end.

According to documents, Hila filed the divorce papers, listing October 13, 2026 as their date of separation.

The couple married on October 10, 2012. TMZ initially reported the divorce filing.

Hila, represented by prominent divorce lawyer Laura Wasser, is seeking joint custody of their three children, spousal support, the restoration of her maiden name and payment of her legal fees by Ethan.

The separation follows Hila's public allegations that Ethan had been unfaithful.

In an Instagram statement last Thursday, she wrote: “I am living a nightmare I can’t wake up from. My husband has been having an affair. I have been fed lie after lie after lie for months.”

Hila said she had confronted Ethan about her concerns but received dismissive responses. She subsequently discovered what she described as a lie and decided to end the relationship.

According to Hila, Ethan eventually admitted to having an affair lasting more than six months.

The controversy has also affected the couple's professional partnership. The H3 Podcast team confirmed Ethan's departure, expressing support for Hila. Its statement read: “We stand with Hila and will support her every step of the way.”

Launched in 2016, the H3 Podcast has more than 2.5 million YouTube subscribers. Ethan and Hila, who met in 2007, share three sons: Theodore, Bruce and Sunny.

headline: Heidi Klum's Halloween costume team seemingly spoils 'The Batman: Part II' characters
description: The photographs shared by the team show several character moulds that could offer clues about the upcoming DC sequel
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Heidi Klum’s latest Halloween costume has unexpectedly drawn attention from Batman fans after an image showing its construction appeared to reveal possible character details from The Batman: Part II.

The photograph features several character moulds that could offer clues about the upcoming DC sequel.

Among the most notable is a head mould resembling actor Brian Tyree Henry, reportedly suggesting his character is Harvey Dent, who could become the villain Two-Face.

The image also includes a container labelled Victor Zsasz, strengthening speculation that Sebastian Stan will portray the serial killer.

Another mould marked "Owl 3" has fuelled theories that the film could introduce the Court of Owls, a secret organisation from DC Comics.

An unidentified older male mould has also attracted attention, although its connection to the film remains unclear.

Meanwhile, the absence of Scarlett Johansson from the collection has raised further questions about her character. Fan theories have suggested she could play Gilda Dent or a grounded interpretation of Poison Ivy.

Director Matt Reeves has also reportedly stepped away temporarily from directing because of a personal family matter, with Steven Soderbergh stepping in to complete filming. Reeves is expected to remain involved during post-production.

Despite previous delays, The Batman: Part II is currently scheduled to arrive in cinemas on February 18, 2028. Whether the recent production developments will affect its release date remains uncertain.

Neither the potential character revelations nor the costume-related theories have been officially confirmed.

headline: Scream 8: Neve Campbell confirms return as Sidney Prescott
description: When asked for further details, she remained cautious about revealing information but confirmed her involvement
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Neve Campbell has confirmed that she will reprise her role as Sidney Prescott in Scream 8, giving fans an update on the future of the long-running horror franchise.

In an interview with the Associated Press, reported by Just Jared on November 2, 2026, Campbell revealed that the eighth instalment is among her upcoming projects.

Discussing her professional plans, the actress said: “I’ve got two shows that I’m developing, one I’ve sold, and Scream 8. So, you know, that’s in the pipeline as well.”

View this post on Instagram

When asked for further details, Campbell remained cautious about revealing information surrounding the sequel but confirmed her involvement, stating: “You know, I can never tell you anything about Scream 8. I’ll be in it.”

Campbell's return continues her association with the franchise, having missed Scream VI in 2023 following a reported salary dispute.

She subsequently returned for Scream 7, released in February 2026, reprising her role as the series' central character.

The seventh film reportedly earned $207 million worldwide, compared with $166 million for its predecessor, demonstrating continued audience interest in the horror series.

Although plans for an eighth film were reportedly underway around the release of Scream 7, Campbell's latest comments provide confirmation of her participation.

Further details about the storyline, supporting cast and production schedule have yet to be announced.

For now, fans can look forward to seeing Campbell return as Sidney Prescott in the next chapter of the Scream franchise.

headline: Justin Timberlake reportedly developing four-part Apple documentary featuring Janet Jackson
description: Multiple sources are describing the project as a 'tell-all ', however, details have not yet been confirmed
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Justin Timberlake is reportedly preparing to revisit major moments from his personal life and music career in a new four-part documentary series for Apple, with Janet Jackson expected to feature.

According to an exclusive report by Variety, published on November 2, the project is being described by multiple sources as a "tell-all".

However, details about its release date and official production arrangements have not yet been confirmed.

The documentary is expected to explore Timberlake's more than three-decade career, from his early success with NSYNC to his achievements as a solo artist.

It could also address controversies involving his former partner Britney Spears and the 2004 Super Bowl halftime show with Jackson.

During the widely discussed performance, Timberlake pulled away part of Jackson's costume, briefly exposing her breast on live television.

The incident generated significant backlash, with Jackson facing considerable professional consequences.

According to sources cited by Variety, Jackson is expected to discuss the infamous "wardrobe malfunction" in the documentary.

Another source suggests Timberlake will address recent comments made by Spears.

In February 2021, Timberlake publicly apologised to both women, acknowledging his role in the controversies surrounding them.

The reported project would mark another collaboration between Timberlake and Apple. He previously starred in the 2021 film Palmer.

Although anticipation is building around the proposed series, neither its release date nor its complete list of contributors has been officially announced.

It could also address controversies involving his former partner Britney Spears and the 2004 Super Bowl halftime show with Jackson.
During the widely discussed performance, Timberlake pulled away part of Jackson's costume, briefly exposing her breast on live television.
The incident generated significant backlash, with Jackson facing considerable professional consequences.
According to sources cited by Variety, Jackson is expected to discuss the infamous "wardrobe malfunction" in the documentary.
Another source suggests Timberlake will address recent comments made by Spears.
In February 2021, Timberlake publicly apologised to both women, acknowledging his role in the controversies surrounding them.
The reported project would mark another collaboration between Timberlake and Apple. He previously starred in the 2021 film Palmer.
Although anticipation is building around the proposed series, neither its release date nor its complete list of contributors has been officially announced.

headline: AFC postpones Asian Cup 2027
description: The decision follows growing uncertainty over the tournament's staging amid recent Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
author: AFP
article_text: The 2027 Asian Cup football tournament in Saudi Arabia will be postponed from January to December due to "exceptional circumstances" in the region, the continent's governing body said on Tuesday. A number of big sports events in Saudi Arabia have been cancelled or postponed in recent weeks following Houthi attacks on the country. "The organising committee for AFC Asian Cup approved to reschedule the flagship national team tournament in light of the current exceptional circumstances arising from developments in the region," the Asian Football Confederation said in a statement. The AFC also cited "substantial logistical complexities and travel disruptions". "The new dates of the tournament will be presented to FIFA for approval," it said. The continental showpiece was originally scheduled to take place from January 7 to February 5 next year. The new dates are December 23, 2027, to January 21, 2028. Local organisers insisted last month that the Asian Cup was "on schedule", despite growing fears for the fate of the tournament. The Saudi cities of Jeddah, Riyadh and Al Khobar are set to stage the month-long competition. The decision to move the tournament back almost a year came after "extensive discussions and close consultation" between Saudi officials and the AFC, the governing body said. "Exceptional circumstances have been created for the organisation and delivery of the competition as originally scheduled, making the postponement necessary in the interest of all participating teams, officials, spectators and other stakeholders," it said.

headline: Kai Cenat announces 5-Game 'Grand Theft Auto' marathon ahead of 'GTA 6' release
description: Cenat revealed the plans during a livestream, confirming that he intends to play 5 major titles with his audience
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Popular Twitch streamer Kai Cenat has announced a five-game Grand Theft Auto marathon, starting on November 5, as he prepares for the release of GTA 6 later this month.

Cenat revealed the streaming plans during a livestream on November 2, confirming that he intends to play five major titles from the franchise with his audience.

The marathon will begin at 3 pm EST on Twitch and YouTube and cover GTA 3, Vice City, San Andreas, GTA 4 and GTA 5.

The challenge gives Cenat just 14 days to complete all five games before GTA 6 arrives on November 19.

The streamer has previously expressed his desire to revisit the franchise and experience its major instalments alongside his viewers.

The marathon also has a personal connection for Cenat, particularly through Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, which introduced him to the series during his childhood in Brooklyn.

During his November 2 broadcast, he recalled how his stepfather introduced him to the game, remembering starting it on a motorbike while Michael Jackson's "Billie Jean" played in the background.

“I know I said this a bunch of times, but I'mma say it one more time,” Cenat told viewers before sharing the memory. Reflecting on the experience, he added, “my life changed from there.”

Cenat has also revealed that he never properly completed San Andreas, despite exploring its open world.

With GTA 6 approaching, the marathon offers fans an opportunity to revisit the franchise's previous titles before the next chapter arrives.

headline: Yemeni army says it carried out over 1,200 operations against Houthi positions
description: Saudi-led coalition says drone intercepted over Makkah region as Houthis deny launching attack
author: Reuters
article_text:
The Yemeni army said Tuesday it carried out 1,208 military operations against Houthi positions, claiming to have "neutralized" around 370 commanders and fighters.

"Our armed forces continued carrying out their combat missions as part of Operation Dawn of Yemen, conducting 1,208 strikes targeting gatherings, movements, reinforcements, fortifications, firing positions and vehicles belonging to the terrorist Houthi militia, using fighter jets, drones, field artillery and rocket launchers," the army said in a statement.

The military also said that its operations destroyed or disabled approximately 120 vehicles and pieces of Houthi military equipment across several battlefronts.

It did not specify the timeframe for the operations, and the Houthis had not commented on the statement.

Houthis claim strike on Saudi airport, airbase

Earlier on Tuesday, the Houthis claimed to have struck an airport and an airbase in Saudi Arabia's Abha and Khamis Mushait areas.

In a post on X, Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed that the group had "carried out two military operations", further adding that the "first operation targeted Abha International Airport with a drone, and the strike was precise, leading to the disruption of air traffic at the airport".

The spokesman added that the second operation "targeted Khamis Mushait Air Base with a ballistic missile, and the strike was direct, by the grace of God".

Saudi-led coalition says drone intercepted over Makkah region as Houthis deny launching attack

The Saudi-led coalition said on Tuesday that it intercepted and destroyed a drone over the Makkah region in western Saudi Arabia amid escalating tensions with the Houthi group in Yemen.

Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki reported the interception on US social media company X, without giving any details about injuries or damage.

Meanwhile, the Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had not carried out any operation targeting Saudi territory today.

Last week, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said it intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile targeting southern Saudi Arabia and a drone in the Riyadh region amid escalating hostilities with the Yemeni group. The same day, the coalition said ​it had intercepted and destroyed ​a drone launched by the Houthis over the Makkah region, which Saree dismissed as false in a post on X, saying the group's operations were ⁠targeting Saudi oil facilities and military bases.

On October 24, the Saudi-led ​coalition said it destroyed two ballistic missiles fired ​by the Houthis towards Taif and Yanbu, with Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence briefly issuing alerts warning of potential danger in the holy city of Makkah and its second-largest city Jeddah.

Araghchi says talks between Iran, Saudi Arabia ongoing

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that talks between Iran and Saudi Arabia were ongoing as Tehran aimed to reach new regional security arrangements for countries in the region without foreign military involvement.

Last week, top officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan met Iranian officials in Tehran, the first high-level contact between Iran and the three nations since August. The US-Israeli war on Iran started in late February, and since then, fighting has spread to Saudi Arabia and Yemen.

Riyadh said the visit was intended to open negotiating channels to "prevent the return of military escalation," as fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis had intensified in recent weeks.

Houthi attacks on the kingdom escalated as the group advanced towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping chokepoint that lies on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula from the Strait of Hormuz.

The Houthis have also attacked Saudi oil facilities and airports, including Riyadh's international airport, disrupting flights and oil exports and drawing Saudi air strikes on Yemen in response.

Impoverished Yemen has been mired in a civil war since the Houthis pushed the internationally recognised, Saudi-backed government out of the capital, Sanaa, in 2014.

Meanwhile, the US carried out "defensive" strikes on Iran's Qeshm island overnight, with a US official saying the strikes targeted surface-to-air missiles used against US assets. Meanwhile, the Revolutionary Guards said they downed a US MQ-9 drone overnight in the skies over the east of the Strait of Hormuz.

"Mediators are working hard to narrow gaps between Tehran and Washington," the senior Iranian official said, after Qatari mediators travelled to Tehran on Monday night for talks on a version of the draft US-Iran deal that has been under negotiation for the past eight days.

“Tehran's conditions must be met if the US wants Hormuz reopened,” the Iranian official cautioned, adding that nuclear talks could only start afterwards and that Tehran would not accept Washington's "excessive demands".

headline: Off-duty violence against wife constitutes misconduct by civil servant: Supreme Court
description: Court observes that violence did not become private matter merely because it occurred within home
author: APP
article_text:
The Supreme Court (SC) ruled that serious misconduct by a civil servant in his private life, including violence against his wife, could constitute service misconduct even if the act was committed outside office hours and had no direct connection with official duties.

Dismissing a petition filed by an Intelligence Bureau (IB) employee, the apex court held that acquittal in a criminal case did not automatically invalidate departmental proceedings if evidence independently established misconduct.

The court upheld the compulsory retirement of Jawad Abbasi, who was serving as a cook in the IB and was accused of setting his wife on fire. He had challenged the Federal Service Tribunal’s decision maintaining the departmental penalty imposed on him.

In a judgment authored by Justice Shahid Waheed, with Justice Ayesha A. Malik as a member of the bench, the court observed that the dignity of women was a fundamental constitutional value and that a civil servant’s conduct at home could also reflect upon his suitability for public office and the reputation of the institution.

The court observed that violence did not become a private matter merely because it occurred within the home. Under the Civil Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 2020, conduct unbecoming of an officer and prejudicial to service discipline could constitute misconduct even outside the workplace.

It clarified that an FIR alone could not justify departmental punishment. However, in this case, the inquiry officer had examined 13 witnesses in the employee’s presence and provided him an opportunity to cross-examine them. The departmental inquiry independently established the charges, including the allegation of violence against his wife and his attempt to portray the incident as her suicide.

The court explained that criminal and departmental proceedings served different purposes and applied different standards of proof.

An acquittal meant that criminal guilt had not been established beyond reasonable doubt; it did not necessarily establish the accused’s innocence for departmental purposes or certify his fitness for government service.

It further observed that the employee had been given an opportunity to defend himself and that the compulsory retirement penalty was proportionate to the gravity of the misconduct.

Finding no legal error, violation of due process, or substantial question of law of public importance, the SC refused leave to appeal and dismissed the petition.

The Supreme Court (SC) ruled that serious misconduct by a civil servant in his private life, including violence against his wife, could constitute service misconduct even if the act was committed outside office hours and had no direct connection with official duties.

Dismissing a petition filed by an Intelligence Bureau (IB) employee, the apex court held that acquittal in a criminal case did not automatically invalidate departmental proceedings if evidence independently established misconduct.

The court upheld the compulsory retirement of Jawad Abbasi, who was serving as a cook in the IB and was accused of setting his wife on fire. He had challenged the Federal Service Tribunal’s decision maintaining the departmental penalty imposed on him.

In a judgment authored by Justice Shahid Waheed, with Justice Ayesha A. Malik as a member of the bench, the court observed that the dignity of women was a fundamental constitutional value and that a civil servant’s conduct at home could also reflect upon his suitability for public office and the reputation of the institution.

The court observed that violence did not become a private matter merely because it occurred within the home. Under the Civil Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 2020, conduct unbecoming of an officer and prejudicial to service discipline could constitute misconduct even outside the workplace.

It clarified that an FIR alone could not justify departmental punishment. However, in this case, the inquiry officer had examined 13 witnesses in the employee’s presence and provided him an opportunity to cross-examine them. The departmental inquiry independently established the charges, including the allegation of violence against his wife and his attempt to portray the incident as her suicide.

The court explained that criminal and departmental proceedings served different purposes and applied different standards of proof.

An acquittal meant that criminal guilt had not been established beyond reasonable doubt; it did not necessarily establish the accused’s innocence for departmental purposes or certify his fitness for government service.

It further observed that the employee had been given an opportunity to defend himself and that the compulsory retirement penalty was proportionate to the gravity of the misconduct.

Finding no legal error, violation of due process, or substantial question of law of public importance, the SC refused leave to appeal and dismissed the petition.

headline: 8, including trekkers, missing in Indian Himalayas as snowfall hampers rescue efforts
description: Rescuers find tent, belongings buried under snow at 4,000 meters, but no trace of missing group in Uttarakhand state
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Rescuers find tent, belongings buried under snow at 4,000 meters, but no trace of missing group in Uttarakhand state

Eight people, including trekkers, were missing in India's northern Uttarakhand state on Tuesday as heavy snowfall and poor visibility hampered rescue operations in the Himalayan region, local media reported.

Rescue teams discovered a tent buried under snow, along with clothing, slippers and food supplies, near Kedartal in Uttarkashi district, according to the Hindi daily Dainik Jagran.

A search covering a 2- to 3-kilometre (1.5-mile) radius around the site failed to locate the missing people, the newspaper reported on Tuesday.

The operation was suspended after continuing snowfall reduced visibility to near zero.

A 10-member rescue team was airlifted to the area on Monday, according to the Press Trust of India (PTI).

The missing group includes five trekkers from West Bengal, two women from Uttar Pradesh and a local guide.

They were among a trekking party that departed Gangotri on October 27 and was scheduled to return on October 29.

Four members, including three porters and a cook, were rescued Saturday after avalanches blocked the route.

Authorities said multiple avalanches had struck the trekking route, complicating ground searches and helicopter operations.

Meanwhile, authorities have closed high-altitude trekking routes above 4,000 meters following heavy snowfall, Dainik Jagran reported Tuesday.

Rescue operations are expected to resume when weather conditions improve.

headline: North Korea rejects US allegations over Binance crypto theft, warns of response
description: Kim Jong Un's sister accuses Washington of politicising allegations to damage Pyongyang's international standing
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
North Korea on Monday rejected US allegations linking it to a multibillion-dollar cryptocurrency theft involving Binance, accusing Washington of using cybercrime allegations to undermine its international reputation.

Kim Yo Jong, the influential sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and a senior Workers' Party official, called the allegations a "grave political provocation," state news agency KCNA reported on Tuesday.

She said the FBI was attempting to portray North Korea as a "cyber criminal state" by alleging that a hacking group supported by Pyongyang was involved in the theft.

"The US assertion is an absurd rhetoric and nothing new," Kim said in a statement. She accused Washington of routinely blaming North Korea for major international cyberattacks without providing credible evidence.

Kim also cited US allegations linking Pyongyang to last year's cryptocurrency theft involving the exchange Bybit.

North Korea has repeatedly denied US accusations of state-sponsored cyberattacks, while Washington has accused North Korean hacking groups of stealing digital assets to finance the country's weapons programs.

Kim suggested Washington could benefit from recovering stolen cryptocurrency, referring to US plans to establish a strategic cryptocurrency reserve.

She said Pyongyang was closely monitoring US provocations and that Washington's hostile attitude could prompt it to reconsider its position on several issues.

headline: ECP issues show-cause notice to MQM-P over intra-party elections
description: Commission gives the party 14 days to respond to the show-cause notice
author: Naeem Khanzada
article_text:
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) issued a show-cause notice to Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) for failing to fulfil the legal requirements for holding intra-party elections within the extended deadline of October 15, 2026, emerged on Tuesday.

According to the notice issued on October 26, the electoral watchdog said MQM-P had failed to conduct its intra-party elections within the prescribed extended period.

The ECP stated that the regular election of political party office-bearers was a legal requirement under the Elections Act, 2017, which made intra-party elections mandatory.

The notice further stated that political parties were required to submit an election certificate to the commission within seven days of holding intra-party elections.

The commission gave MQM-P 14 days to respond to the show-cause notice, warning that further action would be taken in accordance with the law if the party failed to submit its response.

The ECP also warned that failure to conduct intra-party elections could render MQM-P ineligible to obtain an electoral symbol.

The commission further stated that the party's electoral symbol could also be withheld for future elections if it failed to comply with the legal requirements.

On April 7, the ECP rejected MQM-P's request for a two-month extension to hold its intra-party elections, with the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) questioning the grounds for delay and warning of serious consequences for non-compliance.

A three-member bench headed by the CEC heard the case pertaining to MQM-P's intra-party polls. Officials from the ECP's Political Finance Wing, along with party representatives, appeared before the commission.

During the proceedings, the CEC asked, "What war is being fought in Pakistan? We cannot grant two months," directing that convener Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui or his lawyer must appear at the next hearing, cautioning that failure to do so could lead to serious repercussions.

Director General Political Finance Masood Sherwani informed the bench that MQM-P last conducted intra-party elections on October 16, 2021, while under its party constitution, fresh elections were required by October 16, 2025.

The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) issued a show-cause notice to Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) for failing to fulfil the legal requirements for holding intra-party elections within the extended deadline of October 15, 2026, emerged on Tuesday.

According to the notice issued on October 26, the electoral watchdog said MQM-P had failed to conduct its intra-party elections within the prescribed extended period.

The ECP stated that the regular election of political party office-bearers was a legal requirement under the Elections Act, 2017, which made intra-party elections mandatory.

The notice further stated that political parties were required to submit an election certificate to the commission within seven days of holding intra-party elections.

The commission gave MQM-P 14 days to respond to the show-cause notice, warning that further action would be taken in accordance with the law if the party failed to submit its response.

The ECP also warned that failure to conduct intra-party elections could render MQM-P ineligible to obtain an electoral symbol.

The commission further stated that the party's electoral symbol could also be withheld for future elections if it failed to comply with the legal requirements.

On April 7, the ECP rejected MQM-P's request for a two-month extension to hold its intra-party elections, with the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) questioning the grounds for delay and warning of serious consequences for non-compliance.

A three-member bench headed by the CEC heard the case pertaining to MQM-P's intra-party polls. Officials from the ECP's Political Finance Wing, along with party representatives, appeared before the commission.

During the proceedings, the CEC asked, "What war is being fought in Pakistan? We cannot grant two months," directing that convener Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui or his lawyer must appear at the next hearing, cautioning that failure to do so could lead to serious repercussions.

Director General Political Finance Masood Sherwani informed the bench that MQM-P last conducted intra-party elections on October 16, 2021, while under its party constitution, fresh elections were required by October 16, 2025.
