headline: Dar reaffirms govt's commitment to public relief in meeting with JI delegation
description: Parties discuss relief measures for common man, with specific focus on easing economic burden on low-income citizens
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday reaffirmed the government's commitment to providing relief to the public amid global economic challenges during a meeting with a Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) delegation led by Liaquat Baloch to discuss petroleum prices and measures to ease the financial burden on low-income citizens.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday met with a delegation of the Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) to discuss petroleum prices in the country, with both sides agreeing to "continue their consultations over the coming days to formulate a way forward on energy pricing and public relief," the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement.

"Dar met with the JI delegation led by Liaquat Baloch, holding candid discussions on practical measures to provide relief to the common man, with a specific focus on easing the economic burden on low-income citizens," said the Foreign Office in a post on X.

The meeting came after the government and JI, on October 27, agreed to form a six-member committee to finalise recommendations on expanding the existing petrol relief scheme and preparing proposals for a phased reduction in the petroleum levy. Under the agreement, three members each from the government and JI would examine measures to broaden the scope of the ongoing PM fuel relief scheme to ensure that the maximum number of deserving people benefit from it.

Agreeing to continue consultations, Dar also "reiterated the government’s commitment to prioritising public welfare and facilitating ordinary citizens amidst global economic challenges."

He also "emphasised that sustained cross-party dialogue remains key to addressing national economic challenges effectively."

The Foreign Office stated that the meeting was attended by the Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Inter-Provincial Coordination Rana Sanaullah, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister Tariq Bajwa, along with the finance secretary and the Special secretary for petroleum.

Background

JI’s campaign against the petroleum levy intensified in August, when the party organised demonstrations and sit-ins across the country against rising fuel prices, inflation and what it described as an additional tax burden on consumers. On August 16, JI workers staged sit-ins outside governors’ houses in the provincial capitals, demanding the withdrawal of the levy and a reduction in petrol prices.

The party subsequently expanded its protests to other cities, including Karachi, where it established additional protest camps across Sindh. JI maintained that the government should abolish the levy rather than offer limited reductions in fuel prices.

On September 3, the government and JI agreed to establish technical committees to examine proposals for reducing the petroleum levy and fuel prices. During the first round of negotiations on September 7, the party submitted six proposals to the government, while insisting that its protests would continue until meaningful relief was provided.

However, the negotiations failed to resolve the dispute. On September 12, JI chief announced a long march towards Islamabad for September 20, warning that the party would intensify its campaign if the government did not abolish the levy.

The march began on September 20, with participants travelling from Karachi by train. The caravan moved through Sukkur towards Multan, where Naeem addressed supporters. The march was subsequently suspended after PM Shehbaz telephoned the JI chief and requested that the party postpone its protest to allow further negotiations.

JI agreed to give the government an opportunity for talks but maintained that it had not abandoned its demand. The party’s position was that negotiations and protests could continue simultaneously, with any agreement required to address the complete abolition of the levy.

The JI chief then gave the government 10 days to abolish the petroleum levy and provide meaningful relief to the inflation-hit public, warning that his party would resume its long march towards Islamabad in mid-November if its demands were not met.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday reaffirmed the government's commitment to providing relief to the public amid global economic challenges during a meeting with a Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) delegation led by Liaquat Baloch to discuss petroleum prices and measures to ease the financial burden on low-income citizens.

 

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday met with a delegation of the Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) to discuss petroleum prices in the country, with both sides agreeing to "continue their consultations over the coming days to formulate a way forward on energy pricing and public relief," the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement.

"Dar met with the JI delegation led by Liaquat Baloch, holding candid discussions on practical measures to provide relief to the common man, with a specific focus on easing the economic burden on low-income citizens," said the Foreign Office in a post on X.

The meeting came after the government and JI, on October 27, agreed to form a six-member committee to finalise recommendations on expanding the existing petrol relief scheme and preparing proposals for a phased reduction in the petroleum levy. Under the agreement, three members each from the government and JI would examine measures to broaden the scope of the ongoing PM fuel relief scheme to ensure that the maximum number of deserving people benefit from it.

Read: Govt stands firm on petroleum levy

Agreeing to continue consultations, Dar also "reiterated the government’s commitment to prioritising public welfare and facilitating ordinary citizens amidst global economic challenges."

He also "emphasised that sustained cross-party dialogue remains key to addressing national economic challenges effectively."

The Foreign Office stated that the meeting was attended by the Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Inter-Provincial Coordination Rana Sanaullah, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister Tariq Bajwa, along with the finance secretary and the Special secretary for petroleum.

Background

JI’s campaign against the petroleum levy intensified in August, when the party organised demonstrations and sit-ins across the country against rising fuel prices, inflation and what it described as an additional tax burden on consumers. On August 16, JI workers staged sit-ins outside governors’ houses in the provincial capitals, demanding the withdrawal of the levy and a reduction in petrol prices.

The party subsequently expanded its protests to other cities, including Karachi, where it established additional protest camps across Sindh. JI maintained that the government should abolish the levy rather than offer limited reductions in fuel prices.

On September 3, the government and JI agreed to establish technical committees to examine proposals for reducing the petroleum levy and fuel prices. During the first round of negotiations on September 7, the party submitted six proposals to the government, while insisting that its protests would continue until meaningful relief was provided.

However, the negotiations failed to resolve the dispute. On September 12, JI chief announced a long march towards Islamabad for September 20, warning that the party would intensify its campaign if the government did not abolish the levy.

Read More: JI launches third phase of protest campaign against petroleum levy

The march began on September 20, with participants travelling from Karachi by train. The caravan moved through Sukkur towards Multan, where Naeem addressed supporters. The march was subsequently suspended after PM Shehbaz telephoned the JI chief and requested that the party postpone its protest to allow further negotiations.

JI agreed to give the government an opportunity for talks but maintained that it had not abandoned its demand. The party’s position was that negotiations and protests could continue simultaneously, with any agreement required to address the complete abolition of the levy.

The JI chief then gave the government 10 days to abolish the petroleum levy and provide meaningful relief to the inflation-hit public, warning that his party would resume its long march towards Islamabad in mid-November if its demands were not met.

headline: US intelligence sharing has fractured under Trump, officials say
description: Troubles came during Tulsi Gabbard's tenure as director of national intelligence, amid tensions with CIA
author: Reuters
article_text:
US intelligence sharing on Iran and other global threats with Congress and across the federal government has slowed and, in some cases, temporarily stopped during President Donald Trump's second term, according to eight current and former officials and people briefed on the matter.

Former officials and outside experts said the disruptions risk leaving policymakers with an incomplete picture of threats facing the country, echoing intelligence failures exposed after the September 11, 2001, al Qaeda attacks. The slowdown comes as the administration weighs whether to resume strikes on Iran after the midterm elections on Tuesday.

The problems emerged during Tulsi Gabbard's tenure as director of national intelligence, amid deep tensions between her office and the CIA. While those tensions have subsided since her resignation in June, problems stemming from the clash persist, according to two US officials familiar with the matter.

The CIA has stopped co-authoring assessments with the National Intelligence Council (NIC), an analytical group within the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), the officials said, reducing the number of reports that pull together the intelligence community's views for decision-makers on subjects including Iran.

Lawmakers and their staffs also briefly stopped receiving intelligence reports from Gabbard's office in the days after the US military intervention in Iran in June 2025 and again after the capture of former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in January 2026, according to two people familiar with the matter. Gabbard's team had accused lawmakers of leaking to the press.

The disruption in intelligence sharing has not been previously reported.

CIA spokesperson Liz Lyons said the CIA "participates fully" in the process of providing intelligence assessments through the Presidential Daily Brief, which is led by ODNI, and through the NIC.

Now, some former officials are working on a bipartisan basis at Stanford University's Hoover Institution to draw up plans to rebuild the intelligence community in the next administration, four former US officials said.

“All of these things are adding up in a really complex world where policymakers need to have a more sophisticated, nuanced, and integrated view of the world, and they are getting less,” said Beth Sanner, a former deputy director of national intelligence during Trump's first term.

Turf wars and reduced cooperation

The problems inside the intelligence community started last year amid significant cuts to national security agencies, including the ODNI and the CIA, as Trump moved to remove or sideline officials he viewed as disloyal.

Some analysts who remain at the intelligence agencies are now careful not to write assessments at odds with White House’s views for fear of political retaliation, two former officials and a current US official said. The officials did not say which topics the analysts were avoiding.

“Analysts still do the work, but this White House has made them irrelevant because the president treats unwelcome information as disloyalty,” said Julia Curlee, a former CIA analyst who said she was fired from the Trump National Security Council last year for being transgender.

The White House did not respond to a request for comment.

The situation was worsened by what officials described as one of the biggest turf wars in three decades between two of the most important agencies: the CIA and the ODNI, which was formed in the aftermath of the September 11 attacks.

Reuters earlier detailed the dispute between the agencies.

The infighting between the agencies — triggered when Gabbard's office revoked the security clearances of current and former intelligence officials a year ago — reached the point where White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles had to intervene several times to defuse tensions, three former officials said.

The National Intelligence Council, which for decades has been a key resource for officials and lawmakers making foreign policy decisions, lost its main author when the CIA stopped writing into the assessments last year.

The assessments are meant to consolidate the views of the nation’s 18 intelligence agencies, and the council relied heavily on the CIA for analysis on topics like Iran and Russia.

While the CIA continued sharing intelligence with the NIC and working with it on some reports, its analysts focused on their own assessments.

Since the move, the intelligence council, which was also hit by staff cuts, has slowed production of its assessments, two people familiar with the matter said. None have focused on the war in Iran, five current and former officials said.

In response to a request for comment, an ODNI official said the group has maintained assessment levels close to "historic trendlines."

"While Tulsi did not utilise the NIC, DNI Clayton has proven to be a good steward of the IC and recognises the value of the NIC," said a US official, referring to Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton.

New barriers

Some former intelligence officials worry that new barriers are appearing between agencies.

"The problem is that by taking actions which have the effect of hollowing out institutions where there's actual intelligence community coordination on things, you're creating little lily pads, and then everybody can pick their own lily pad to listen to,” said Morgan Muir, the former deputy director of national intelligence in the Biden administration who also briefed President George W. Bush.

Gabbard's office also stopped briefing Congress on election threats in 2025, according to two people familiar with the matter and a former US official.

Clayton, who became director of national intelligence in August, has resumed congressional briefings on election threats, officials said.

"Director Clayton remains committed to ensuring that ODNI and the intelligence community have the resources they need to continue informing key US government decision-makers and keeping Americans safe," ODNI said in a statement to Reuters.

In another clash between agencies, the FBI late last year stopped sharing some intelligence with the National Counterterrorism Centre for several weeks after the centre's then-head, Joe Kent, and his staff tried to investigate the shooting of Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk, two former officials said.

FBI leaders told Kent they believed NCTC was overstepping its authority.

The FBI did not respond to a request for comment.

headline: Taylor Swift opens up about why she hesitated to write a song for 'Toy Story 5'
description: Swift reveals why she was concerned about taking the 'Toy Story 5' song opportunity from another artist
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Taylor Swift has revealed that she initially worried about taking the opportunity to write an original song for Pixar’s upcoming film, Toy Story 5, from another artist.

The 36-year-old singer discussed the experience during a question-and-answer session with director Andrew Stanton following a special screening on Sunday, November 1.

According to Billboard, the conversation explored how Swift came to create “I Knew It, I Knew You” for the animated film.

Stanton explained that Swift was his preferred choice for the project as he wanted to take the soundtrack in a different direction.

Randy Newman, who has composed music for the franchise since the original 1995 film, was not returning for the same role.

“Nothing else made sense,” Stanton said.

Swift was initially unavailable, leading Stanton to believe the film might not have an original end-credits song. However, the singer continued contacting the director to check whether the opportunity was still available or had been offered to someone else.

She explained that she would have understood if the filmmakers had moved forward without her, given the months it took her to respond.

“I don’t want to kick somebody off of this project that you reached out to after [me],” she added. “I understand, but I’m not in the business of doing that.”

Swift eventually wrote “I Knew It, I Knew You”, which went on to reach No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and break multiple records.

The track has also attracted Oscar buzz, adding to anticipation surrounding its appearance in Toy Story 5.

A producer on the Pixar film also reportedly sent Swift a personal letter asking her to contribute an original song.

headline: Johnny Depp reveals one condition for returning to ‘Pirates of the Caribbean 6’
description: Johnny Depp says he trusts longtime friend and producer Jerry Bruckheimer with the franchise’s future
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Johnny Depp has opened up about the possibility of reprising his iconic role as Captain Jack Sparrow in Pirates of the Caribbean 6, revealing that he would consider returning for one important reason: giving the franchise a satisfying conclusion.

Speaking to Variety during the promotional tour for his upcoming film Ebenezer, Depp addressed speculation surrounding his potential involvement in the next instalment. Although he stopped short of confirming his return, the actor expressed a willingness to work with longtime friend and producer Jerry Bruckheimer.

“If things are exactly where they need to be with regard to how they are going to top off the ‘Pirates’ franchise… the only involvement I really want to have, truly, is just to send them off on a better note,” Depp said.

He also reaffirmed his trust in Bruckheimer, adding that he would work with the producer again regardless of the project. Their longstanding friendship, he explained, remains an important factor in his willingness to consider returning.

Bruckheimer previously expressed optimism about Depp reprising the role. In 2025, the producer told Entertainment Weekly that the actor could be interested if he liked the screenplay. At the time, the script was still being developed, with the creative team searching for the right story.

Depp played Jack Sparrow across five films released between 2003 and 2017. The franchise has generated approximately $4.5 billion worldwide, making it one of Disney’s most commercially successful film series.

Plans for a sixth film have been in development for years. Screenwriter Jeff Nathanson, who worked on Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales, was previously attached to the project. Bruckheimer has also publicly voiced support for Depp’s involvement.

However, no official casting confirmation or production announcement has been made regarding Depp’s return.

“If things are exactly where they need to be with regard to how they are going to top off the ‘Pirates’ franchise… the only involvement I really want to have, truly, is just to send them off on a better note,” Depp said.

He also reaffirmed his trust in Bruckheimer, adding that he would work with the producer again regardless of the project. Their longstanding friendship, he explained, remains an important factor in his willingness to consider returning.

Bruckheimer previously expressed optimism about Depp reprising the role. In 2025, the producer told Entertainment Weekly that the actor could be interested if he liked the screenplay. At the time, the script was still being developed, with the creative team searching for the right story.

Depp played Jack Sparrow across five films released between 2003 and 2017. The franchise has generated approximately $4.5 billion worldwide, making it one of Disney’s most commercially successful film series.

Plans for a sixth film have been in development for years. Screenwriter Jeff Nathanson, who worked on Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales, was previously attached to the project. Bruckheimer has also publicly voiced support for Depp’s involvement.
However, no official casting confirmation or production announcement has been made regarding Depp’s return.

headline: ‘Primetime’ digital release: Where to stream Robert Pattinson’s new thriller
description: The film explores a controversial television sting operation inspired by real events from 2006
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
A24’s thriller Primetime, starring Robert Pattinson as former television presenter Chris Hansen, is now available to watch at home following its theatrical release.

The film arrives on premium video on demand platforms on November 3, allowing viewers to rent or purchase it digitally. Available retailers include Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV and Fandango at Home.

On Apple TV, Primetime is listed for $19.99 to rent and $24.99 to purchase. Prices and availability may vary across platforms and regions.

The digital release comes a little over a month after the film premiered in US cinemas on September 25. It debuted at the Venice International Film Festival on September 5 before its theatrical rollout.

Directed by Lance Oppenheim, Primetime draws inspiration from events surrounding a 2006 television sting operation. The story follows Hansen as he pursues a career defining television moment, only for a high stakes operation to take a devastating turn. A24 describes the film as an exploration of performative justice.

Pattinson leads an ensemble cast that includes Merritt Wever, Skyler Gisondo, Matthew Maher, Bokeem Woodbine, Anna Faris, Alex Winter and Phoebe Bridgers. The screenplay was written by Ajon Singh and adapted from Luke Dittrich’s 2007 Esquire article, “Tonight on Dateline This Man Will Die.”

The film marks Oppenheim’s narrative feature directorial debut. His other work includes the documentary You Can See Everything, which he co directed.

Although Primetime is now available for digital purchase and rental, a subscription streaming release date has not been announced. A potential arrival on HBO Max has been speculated about based on A24’s distribution arrangements, but no official date has been confirmed.

headline: Experts urge regular phone updates amid surge in WhatsApp account hijacking
description: Hackers use phishing and spyware to hijack messaging apps, mimic victims and scam contacts for money
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Cybersecurity experts warn that phone software needs to be kept up to date to prevent security breaches amid a rise in WhatsApp account takeovers and fraud attempts.

Increasingly dangerous cyberattack methods are emerging in Türkiye and worldwide, especially targeting the popular messaging app WhatsApp.

Attackers can hijack WhatsApp accounts, mimic the compromised account holders’ chatting styles and send deceptive messages to people in their circles, pretending to be in urgent need of loans via bank transfers.

Ibrahim Gunduzgil, head of the cybersecurity program at Istanbul Commerce University, told Anadolu that attackers can gain access to WhatsApp accounts through phishing attacks, including fake links, and social engineering techniques.

“Security vulnerabilities in outdated apps or operating systems can be exploited by attackers, posing an additional risk through the exploitation of known vulnerabilities,” he said, noting that these attacks are not limited to WhatsApp accounts and can also play a role in hijacking active sessions on Telegram and similar apps.

He noted that the problem stems from the combined exploitation of technical security vulnerabilities and user behavior.

Gunduzgil stressed the importance of enabling two-factor authentication and other additional security features to make messaging apps more secure, and he warned against sharing two-factor authentication codes received via SMS or other channels.

He also advised checking connected devices and active sessions in apps and revoking access to unrecognized devices.

“Users who suspect their accounts have been compromised must immediately begin the recovery process and notify their close contacts,” he said, adding that explicit requests for money should prompt users to verify the other person’s identity through different communication methods.

Gunduzgil stated that the security vulnerabilities leading to account hijacking are not exclusive to either Android or iOS, but recent reports indicate that iOS devices running outdated software exhibit these vulnerabilities.

WhatsApp Web sessions left open on untrusted computers, as well as other attacks involving malware and fake QR codes, can allow malicious actors to gain unauthorized access to accounts.

“Users can continue using their messaging apps without realizing it, but the attacker can access their apps from another device, so users must ensure the security of their phones, computers and other devices linked to their accounts,” he said.

Sabri Erdemir, head of the computer programming department at Istanbul Commerce University, told Anadolu that screenshots of suspicious messages, links, phone numbers, bank account details used to request money, transfer receipts and the date and time of the incident must be preserved as evidence.

Erdemir warned that simply turning off internet access on compromised devices is not enough to prevent or stop the attack, as attackers can connect to the account from another device.

“The compromised device should not be reset to factory settings, apps must not be uninstalled, and existing records must be preserved,” he said, noting that resetting the phone could destroy forensic evidence of the attack and fraud attempts, which would be instrumental in identifying perpetrators.

“Relevant banks must be contacted immediately in the event of financial loss,” he added, noting that victims should file a report with law enforcement even if no financial loss occurs, as preserved evidence can help identify the perpetrators and prevent the compromised account from being used in the future.

headline: Bomb threats trigger security alerts at airports across Europe
description: Security checks have been carried out in all three incidents, with authorities investigating threats
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Spanish authorities began searching a Ryanair plane after a bomb threat involving a flight from Manchester that landed on Tuesday in the southeastern city of Murcia, authorities said.

“Security procedures have been activated following a bomb threat involving a plane from Manchester that has landed in Murcia,” Francisco Lucas, the Spanish government’s representative in Murcia, posted on X.

“The 114 passengers and seven crew members have disembarked and are undergoing security checks,” he added. “The aircraft is now being inspected.”

The plane landed on schedule at Murcia’s international airport in Corvera, according to airport operator Aena.

Other flights continued to operate at the airport normally, Aena told regional newspaper La Opinion de Murcia.

Poland and Bulgaria also reported bomb threats involving flights on Tuesday.

Warsaw Modlin Airport temporarily closed after a bomb threat involving a flight from London, according to the airport.

In the Bulgarian capital, Sofia, counterterrorism officers were deployed to inspect a plane arriving from Israel after authorities received a threat by email, according to local news agency BTA.

Polish airport closes after bomb threat involving flight from London

Warsaw-Modlin Airport in Poland was closed until further notice after a flight from London was diverted there following a reported bomb threat, the airport said in a statement.

The Boeing 737 MAX, originally bound for Warsaw Chopin Airport from London Heathrow, landed at Modlin at 10.01 am local time with 181 people on board.

The aircraft was directed to a designated area while authorities investigated the threat and carried out security checks.

Passengers began disembarking and were to wait in the arrivals hall, according to the statement.

Bomb threats trigger security alerts at airports across Europe

Plane from Israel makes emergency landing in Bulgaria after emailed threat

Meanwhile, a plane arriving from Israel made an emergency landing at Sofia Airport following a threat received by email, Bulgarian National Radio (BNR) reported, citing Interior Ministry Secretary General Lyubomir Nikolov.

Authorities did not initially disclose the airline, flight details, number of passengers or the aircraft’s exact route.

The content of the email threat was also not made public.

It was not immediately clear whether it referred to a possible explosive device.

Bulgarian authorities are expected to provide further details about the incident and the security measures taken.

On Monday, a Wizz Air flight from London to Sofia was diverted to Budapest following a bomb threat. No explosive device was found during checks, and the aircraft later continued to Bulgaria.

On October 18, an Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv to Vienna was diverted to Sofia following a bomb threat. Bulgarian MiG-29 fighter jets escorted the aircraft, which continued to Vienna after security checks found no threat.

headline: Apple shares slide as higher memory costs fuel margin concerns
description: Apple forecasts December-quarter gross margins of 45%-46%, including costs of upgrading its AI-powered Siri
author: Reuters
article_text:
Apple shares fell about 4% in premarket trading on Tuesday after the tech giant warned that rising memory costs would squeeze gross margins, stoking investor concerns ​over persistent supply-chain uncertainties and mounting AI expenses.

John Ternus delivered his first ‌earnings report as Apple CEO on Monday, describing the memory-pricing environment as "unprecedented" while expecting costs to rise beyond the quarter ending in December.

The iPhone maker has benefited from using memory purchased ​at lower prices, but that advantage is expected to diminish over ​time, leaving more of its purchases exposed to higher prices.

Gross margins, ⁠which measure the percentage of revenue retained after the costs of making its products, was ​47.9% for the September quarter, down from June-quarter levels even when factoring in ​the impact of tariff refunds.

Apple expects gross margin for the December-ending quarter to range between 45% and 46%, which also reflects the expenses tied to the ramp-up of its AI-powered ​Siri.

The CEO comments imply "Apple products are going to become even more expensive, which is ​not ideal at a time when the consumer is feeling the pinch from a higher ‌cost ⁠of living," said Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell.

However, Apple reported a record September quarter for iPhone revenue despite price increases and a staggered iPhone release schedule where only the premium 18 Pro models were launched in the last days of the ​company's fiscal 2026.

Fourth-quarter ​iPhone sales, which ⁠included iPhone 18 Pro models but not Duo, were $57.58 billion, above estimates of $56.54 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.

"We ​see the flagship iPhone as the linchpin of this ​ecosystem, from ⁠which Apple derives pricing power, switching costs, and a network effect," said William Kerwin, senior equity analyst at Morningstar.

Apple is set to lose over $170 billion in market value ⁠from ​its $4.94 trillion valuation if losses hold.

The stock trades at ​nearly 35 times expected earnings over the next 12 months, compared with 18.23 times for Alphabet and ​23.43 times for Microsoft.

headline: LPG soars in Pakistan, forcing rickshaw drivers to cut meals
description: Prices have surged since October 17, when two Iranian border crossings closed, halting ​imports, according to traders
author: Reuters
article_text:
For 13 years, Rashid Ali has driven a ​three-wheeled motorised rickshaw around Lahore.

His day starts at 6am and sometimes does not end ‌until midnight, but he was long able to make $6.50 a day — enough for his family's bare essentials. Now, with liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices surging, he doesn't even make half that.

Ali, 33, is among thousands of Pakistani drivers who run their vehicles on LPG, which is sold in cylinders and mainly ​used for cooking and heating.

Majeed Ghauri, chairman of the Awami Rickshaw Union, calls it "the fuel of the poor". He ​said about 70% of its members' 43,000 auto-rickshaws and nearly 8,000 Qingqis — motorcycle-based three-wheelers that carry several ⁠passengers on set routes — run on LPG.

LPG prices have surged since October 17, when two Iranian border crossings closed, halting ​imports, traders say, in the latest energy shock since the US-Iran war began in February.

With Ali now lucky to make $3 a ​day, his family has cut back on meals, eating only twice a day.

"Previously, when LPG was cheap, we could earn a decent income," Ali said. "Now, it's just not possible to get by on seven or eight hundred [rupees], is it?"

Before the border closures, Pakistan imported about 7,000 metric tonnes of ​LPG a day from Iran, the Pakistan LPG Association said.

Traders said the price of a 12-kg cylinder jumped 56% within days ​of the closure to Rs7,000 or about 583 rupees per kg in the open market.

The Balochistan government cited security and smuggling for the decision, while Iran's foreign ministry said technical issues were to blame. Iran's ambassador later said Iran had imposed no restrictions, including on LPG exports, and blamed changes in Pakistan's import paperwork.

Walking away

Ali pays Rs600 a day to rent his rickshaw, filling up with gas four or five times a day, at Rs300 to 400 a time.

As well as ​daily expenses, Ali also pays Rs​11,000 a month for ⁠his home and has two young children to support.

Adding to his problems, passengers, he said, do not want to pay higher fares.

"For a trip that should cost Rs200 or 250, they ​might only offer Rs80, 100, or 150," Ali said.

Passenger Mohammad Ramzan said when a ​driver asked Rs500 for a ride in the city, he offered half that. When the driver declined, he walked away, he said.

Inflation hit 9.6% in October, and the central bank last week raised interest rates to 12%, citing energy and wheat prices. Petrol hit a ⁠record Rs458 per litre on April 3 and remains about 40% above its ​pre-war price.

Back home at midday, Ali said his two boys still needed their lunch. He would go out again until late at night, he said, hoping ​to make enough to bring something for the children to eat at night.

article_html:
For 13 years, Rashid Ali has driven a ​three-wheeled motorised rickshaw around Lahore.

His day starts at 6am and sometimes does not end ‌until midnight, but he was long able to make $6.50 a day — enough for his family's bare essentials. Now, with liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices surging, he doesn't even make half that.

Ali, 33, is among thousands of Pakistani drivers who run their vehicles on LPG, which is sold in cylinders and mainly ​used for cooking and heating.

Majeed Ghauri, chairman of the Awami Rickshaw Union, calls it "the fuel of the poor". He ​said about 70% of its members' 43,000 auto-rickshaws and nearly 8,000 Qingqis — motorcycle-based three-wheelers that carry several ⁠passengers on set routes — run on LPG.

Read: LPG hits Rs550/kg as price spiral deepens

Regional tensions are hitting Pakistani households. Cooking gas prices have risen after the closure of key border crossings with Iran. Pakistan relies heavily on imported LPG, and Iran is one of its biggest suppliers. pic.twitter.com/WVgfGp7MOW

— TRT World (@trtworld) November 3, 2026

LPG prices have surged since October 17, when two Iranian border crossings closed, halting ​imports, traders say, in the latest energy shock since the US-Iran war began in February.

With Ali now lucky to make $3 a ​day, his family has cut back on meals, eating only twice a day.

"Previously, when LPG was cheap, we could earn a decent income," Ali said. "Now, it's just not possible to get by on seven or eight hundred [rupees], is it?"

Before the border closures, Pakistan imported about 7,000 metric tonnes of ​LPG a day from Iran, the Pakistan LPG Association said.

Traders said the price of a 12-kg cylinder jumped 56% within days ​of the closure to Rs7,000 or about 583 rupees per kg in the open market.

The Balochistan government cited security and smuggling for the decision, while Iran's foreign ministry said technical issues were to blame. Iran's ambassador later said Iran had imposed no restrictions, including on LPG exports, and blamed changes in Pakistan's import paperwork.

Read More: Iran ships some LPG, jet fuel despite US blockade, data shows

Walking away

Ali pays Rs600 a day to rent his rickshaw, filling up with gas four or five times a day, at Rs300 to 400 a time.

As well as ​daily expenses, Ali also pays Rs​11,000 a month for ⁠his home and has two young children to support.

Adding to his problems, passengers, he said, do not want to pay higher fares.

"For a trip that should cost Rs200 or 250, they ​might only offer Rs80, 100, or 150," Ali said.

Passenger Mohammad Ramzan said when a ​driver asked Rs500  for a ride in the city, he offered half that. When the driver declined, he walked away, he said.

Inflation hit 9.6% in October, and the central bank last week raised interest rates to 12%, citing energy and wheat prices. Petrol hit a ⁠record Rs458 per litre on April 3 and remains about 40% above its ​pre-war price.

Back home at midday, Ali said his two boys still needed their lunch. He would go out again until late at night, he said, hoping ​to make enough to bring something for the children to eat at night.

headline: Taylor Red singer Nicole Taylor dies at 35 after breast cancer battle
description: Her triplet sisters, Nika and Natalie Taylor, confirmed the news in a YouTube video
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Country singer Nicole Taylor, one-third of the musical trio Taylor Red, has died aged 35 following a battle with breast cancer.

Her triplet sisters, Nika and Natalie Taylor, confirmed the news in a YouTube video.

Nicole died on September 28. In the emotional video, her sisters said she was “at peace and no longer suffering” as they began sharing details of her illness and final months.

Natalie revealed that Nicole was diagnosed with breast cancer in 2022 after the sisters received the news while they were in a “public place”.

Nika later explained that the cancer was Stage 3 and “very aggressive”.

Despite undergoing chemotherapy, Nicole continued to encourage those around her to enjoy life.

“She pushed us all to have fun and not live in fear and hopelessness and she even did CrossFit during the time she was getting chemo treatments,” Natalie shared.

The sisters also paid tribute to Nicole in a statement on a page created in her memory.

“Nicole, the oldest of us three sisters, will be greatly missed. She was our leader and our best friend,” they wrote.

“We are heartbroken, but we know she is in Heaven and will see her again,” they added. Nika and Natalie also confirmed that a private funeral had already taken place.

The identical triplets began their musical journey playing instruments including guitar, banjo, fiddle and mandolin.

Originally performing as Red Roots, they later built a substantial online following through comedy videos, musical challenges and social media content.

Taylor Red reportedly amassed more than 13 million TikTok followers and 16 million YouTube subscribers, alongside brand partnerships with major companies.

headline: Adam Brody regrets keeping his proposal to Leighton Meester too simple
description: The actor shared advice for anyone planning to propose, saying the story lasts a lifetime
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Adam Brody has admitted that he wishes he had made his proposal to wife Leighton Meester more romantic, reflecting on the moment during a recent podcast appearance.

The 46-year-old actor discussed the subject on the October 26 episode of Armchair Expert with Dax Shepard, where he appeared alongside his Nobody Wants This co-stars Kristen Bell, Justine Lupe and Timothy Simons. The conversation turned to marriage proposals while the group discussed romantic developments involving characters in their Netflix series.

Brody chose not to reveal the details of his proposal but acknowledged that it fell short of what he now feels Meester deserved.

“The only thing romantic about it was the speed,” he explained, referring to how quickly their relationship progressed. He added that they got married soon after becoming engaged, describing the proposal itself as “very pedestrian”.

Brody and Meester's relationship became public in February 2013, and they became engaged by November of that year. The couple married in a private ceremony in Northern California in early 2014. They have largely kept details of their relationship and wedding away from public attention.

During the podcast, Brody also offered advice to anyone preparing to propose. He suggested that people should consider how the moment will be remembered and retold throughout their lives.

“At the time, you are like, whatever, but you are going to tell that story the rest of your life,” he said, encouraging people to make the occasion memorable.

When Timothy Simons suggested that Brody might have approached the proposal pragmatically, the actor admitted that he still thinks about it.

“There is that. And yet, and yet, I do kick myself a little,” Brody said. “She deserved a little more.”

Brody and Meester share two children and have been married for more than 12 years. The actor is currently starring in the third season of Nobody Wants This, which is streaming on Netflix.

headline: Govt cuts petrol price by Rs5.45, HSD by Rs3.68 for Nov 4
description: Petroleum minister says govt is working on a strategy to ensure adequate gas supplies during the winter
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The federal government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Rs5.45 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.68 for November 4.

According to a notification issued by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra), the new price of petrol is Rs369.06 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs391.52 per litre.

The announcement came after the government earlier today said that consumers could expect further "good news" on petroleum prices, adding that it was taking steps to address excessive liquid petroleum gas prices by opening up the market to competition.

Addressing a press conference in Islamabad, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik, alongside Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, stated that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had issued clear instructions to provide "maximum relief to low-income groups", further noting that the government had prevented a potential increase in petrol prices on Friday with the support of oil refineries.

Malik stated: "You saw a reduction in petrol and diesel prices yesterday, and today you will also receive good news about petrol prices."

Malik stressed that the government would pass on the benefit of any reduction in international petroleum prices to consumers, adding that it was taking measures to provide relief to vulnerable segments amid challenges facing the global energy market.

The minister noted that regional challenges had created difficulties in importing liquefied natural gas (LNG), prompting the government to strengthen the country's energy security infrastructure.

He added that the government had taken all possible measures to provide relief to consumers, keeping in view the country's economic constraints, and had extended Rs130 billion in subsidies under its public relief scheme.

Malik said Pakistan had around 10 million gas connections, while households without access to piped gas relied on liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), adding that local LPG production stood at between 2,000 and 2,500 tonnes, while some market players had attempted to "exploit consumers" through excessive pricing.

The minister said the government was working on a strategy to ensure adequate gas supplies during the winter, adding that efforts were underway to provide the commodity to consumers at affordable rates.

Malik stated that complaints had been received from various cities about LPG being sold for as much as Rs800 per kilogram, blaming market players for disrupting the sector.

He said the government's priority was to import fuel at competitive prices, noting that the country met around 70 per cent of its fuel requirements through imports, further stating that companies importing fuel would be required to publish their prices on their websites to ensure transparency.

Malik said the government would also ensure fair distribution of LPG quotas for hard-to-reach areas and was exploring measures to extend relief to vulnerable consumers in the gas sector, including through assistance from the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP).

Malik further stated the government would also ensure fair distribution of LPG quotas for hard-to-reach areas and was exploring measures to extend relief to vulnerable consumers in the gas sector, including through assistance from the Benazir Income Support Programme.

Also speaking at the press conference, Tarar said PM Shehbaz had prioritised public relief throughout the crisis and provided subsidies on petroleum products to ease the burden on consumers.

He said the premier had taken a major decision to introduce competition in the LPG sector, adding that, for the first time in history, funds had been obtained from oil refineries to provide relief to the public.

He further noted that the government had provided Rs130 billion in subsidies to consumers.

The press conference comes after the government announced on Monday that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

Malik expressed his gratitude to oil refineries for standing with the government to provide assistance to the public during difficult times.

The petroleum minister also stated that apart from the fuel relief scheme that was offering "targeted relief" to 13 million people, the government had undertaken several other measures to alleviate the burden on the masses.

The federal government on Friday revised the petrol pricing mechanism, directing refineries to surrender the difference between import and ex-refinery prices as a petroleum levy, with the resulting benefit to be passed on to consumers through a corresponding reduction in petrol prices.

Under the revised arrangement, petrol's import price would be determined on the basis of the actual import cost of the relevant Pakistan State Oil (PSO) cargo. If the actual import cost was unavailable for a particular day's pricing, the premium, incidentals and customs duty of the last available cargo might be used.

For the next 30 days, refineries would be entitled to an ex-refinery price calculated by fixing the premium, incidentals and customs duty at the levels applicable on March 7, 2026, before the war.

headline: China's Baidu launches AI model simulating road environment for robotaxis
description: Baidu says Apollo World is training Apollo Go's robotaxi fleet for global deployment
author: Reuters
article_text:
China's Baidu launched Apollo World on Tuesday, an ‌AI system designed to simulate real-world environments for training robotaxis and predict how they evolve, as automakers race to cut the cost of developing autonomous vehicles.

Apollo World can generate "up to 100,000 ​km" (62,000 miles) of simulated driving daily, equivalent to about three years of ​real-world testing by a safety-driver-equipped autonomous vehicle, Baidu said. The system ⁠is capable of producing real-time multimodal data streams, such as camera and lidar ​observations, enabling self-driving systems to directly sense and navigate simulated environments.

Baidu said Apollo ​World is already being used for training Apollo Go’s robotaxi fleet to be operated globally. Baidu-owned Apollo Go is China's largest robotaxi service operator and competes with rivals such as WeRide, Pony.ai and Momenta Global.

Volkswagen's ​Chinese partner XPeng also plans to launch robotaxi operations in 2027.

Morgan Stanley has ​estimated China's robotaxi fleet could grow to 1 million vehicles by 2035.

Technology development is expensive

Chinese ‌robotaxi firms ⁠have largely pursued asset-light expansion strategies, supplying autonomous-driving technology and partnering with automakers, ride-hailing platforms and local fleet operators overseas rather than bearing the full cost of owning and operating fleets.

But developing the technology itself remains expensive.

"They still have the ​capex of training models ... ​and vehicles, a ⁠challenge that every autonomous vehicle company is going to face," said Frank McCleary, an expert in autonomous mobility and urban ​transportation at management consulting firm Arthur D. Little.

"The speed at ​which you ⁠can launch comes down to your technology's ability to adapt and understand and learn (how to drive in) that environment," he said, adding AI has helped accelerate advances in ⁠autonomous driving.

Tesla , ​which is seeking to expand its Cybercab robotaxi ​fleet, uses an "end-to-end neural network" trained on video of human driving to develop its self-driving technology.

headline: Chinese researchers achieve breakthrough in underground positioning and navigation
description: China's BeiDou micro-station system extends precise navigation underground, beyond satellite signal coverage
author: xinhua.
article_text:
A driver pulls into an underground car park in Xiongan New Area, north China's Hebei Province, taps "park" on a smartphone app and is guided directly to a vacant space. If the spot has already been taken, the system automatically recommends another.

Behind this convenience is a technological breakthrough by a research team at the 54th Research Institute of China Electronics Technology Group Corporation (CETC54).

Developed under the name "Xingyuan," the BeiDou micro-base-station system for underground positioning and navigation extends high-precision location services into spaces beyond the reach of satellite signals. The project behind the system has passed a national acceptance review by China's Ministry of Science and Technology, marking an important advance in the country's efforts to build an integrated spatio-temporal network for underground environments.

CETC54 engineer Chen Chong said the system offers more than convenience, opening up new possibilities for intelligent transportation, mining and other sectors and reflecting the expanding use of high-precision positioning technology underground.

Satellite navigation has long faced challenges in underground car parks because satellite signals cannot penetrate underground structures, making accurate positioning on ordinary smartphones difficult and leaving gaps in navigation services.

To address these challenges, the Xingyuan system deploys BeiDou micro base stations underground, enabling accurate positioning and navigation on ordinary smartphones. BeiDou, or the BeiDou Navigation Satellite System, is China's global navigation satellite system.

Tests show the system can achieve static positioning accuracy better than 0.2 meters for pedestrians, with sub-meter navigation accuracy for high-speed unmanned vehicles.

To make positioning reliable in complex underground environments, the team developed a digital-twin channel modeling method that combines real-time data collection with offline model optimization.

The approach creates a "wireless environment map" that shows signal strength, signal delay and propagation direction, providing reliable support for underground positioning and navigation.

The project has also produced China's first fully independently developed pulse positioning chip. Based on an original HNav-UWB signal standard, the chip achieves ranging accuracy better than 10 centimeters and angle accuracy better than 3 degrees, reducing reliance on foreign UWB positioning standards and core chips.

Beyond parking, the Xingyuan system is being extended to underground coal mines. There, it supports personnel tracking, unmanned transportation and integrated surface and underground positioning, providing technical support for the intelligent upgrading of the coal industry.

headline: Soldier martyred, 17 terrorists killed in Balochistan IBOs: ISPR
description: Ten terrorists killed in Kachhi, seven in Kharan as forces conduct intelligence-based operations in Balochistan
author: Web Desk
article_text:
A soldier was martyred while security forces killed 17 militants in two intelligence-based operations in Balochistan’s Kachhi and Kharan districts, the military’s media wing said on Tuesday.

“On November 1, 2026, security forces conducted two intelligence-based operations in Kachhi and Kharan districts of Balochistan on the reported presence of terrorists belonging to Indian proxies, Fitna al-Hindustan and Fitna al-Khawarij, neutralising 17 Indian-sponsored terrorists,” the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement.

The federal government last year officially designated all militant groups operating in Balochistan as Fitna al-Hindustan, accusing India of sponsoring a proxy war through these outfits. Fitna al-Khawarij is a term used by the state for terrorists affiliated with the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

The first operation was conducted in the Sanni area of Kachhi district, where security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to establish a roadblock, killing 10 of them. Weapons and ammunition were also recovered.

In the second operation in Kharan district, security forces busted a terrorist hideout. Following an intense exchange of fire, seven TTP members were killed, the ISPR said, adding that weapons and ammunition were also recovered.

“Meanwhile, during the intense fire exchange, Sepoy Hikmatullah, having fought gallantly, paid the ultimate sacrifice and embraced martyrdom,” the statement said.

Sanitisation operations were underway to eliminate any other terrorists found in the area, it added.

The ISPR said the counterterrorism campaign under the vision of Azm-e-Istehkam, approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, would continue at full pace to eliminate the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country.

President Asif Ali Zardari praised the security forces for killing the 17 terrorists in the two operations.

In a statement, the president commended security forces for foiling the attempt to block a road in Kachhi district, saying their timely and effective action had thwarted the militants’ designs.

He also lauded the successful operation in Kharan district and expressed grief over the martyrdom of Sepoy Hikmatullah.

Zardari said the soldier’s sacrifice for the defence, peace and security of the country would always be remembered.

The president said operations under Azm-e-Istehkam would continue until terrorism sponsored and supported by foreign elements was eliminated.

He also praised the continued efforts and sacrifices of security forces and law enforcement agencies in the fight against terrorism, describing them as a source of pride.

Meanwhile, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif paid tribute to the security forces for successful operations against India-backed Fitna al-Hindustan terrorists in Balochistan's Kachhi and Kharan districts.

According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister's Office, the prime minister commended the security forces for the operations while also paying tribute to Sepoy Hikmatullah, who was martyred during an operation against terrorists in Kharan.

He said the security forces were achieving significant successes against terrorism under the vision of Azm-e-Istehkam and reiterated the government's resolve to eliminate terrorism from the country in all its forms.

Separately, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi paid tribute to security forces for their successful operations against Indian-sponsored militants in Balochistan, commending their professionalism in foiling the militants’ nefarious designs.

“I salute the security forces for sending 17 Indian-sponsored terrorists to hell,” he said.

He also paid tribute to Sepoy Hikmatullah, who was martyred during the operations, saying the soldier had set a supreme example by sacrificing his life for the country.

Terrorism is a growing problem for Pakistan, with the number of attacks rising every year since 2022, according to Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), a global monitoring organisation. Data from ACLED shows attacks in Pakistan rose nearly fourfold to 2,425 in 2025 from 658 in 2022, and over the same period, TTP attacks increased more than sevenfold to 838 from 118.

Although K-P has borne the brunt of terrorism, Balochistan has also remained a major target of Indian proxies, which often target civilians and military installations in the province.

Over the past few years, Balochistan has witnessed an increase in terrorist attacks, with militants frequently targeting convoys, abducting security personnel and civilians, and attacking security and civilian installations.

However, attacks declined noticeably in October, offering a temporary respite after two consecutive months of rising violence. A sharp increase in kidnappings, particularly in Balochistan, nevertheless continued to pose a serious security challenge.

According to statistics released by the Islamabad-based Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS), Balochistan registered one of the sharpest improvements in its security indicators, with terrorist attacks falling by 46 per cent, from 132 in September to 71 in October.

Overall, 143 terrorist attacks were recorded across the country during October, compared with 226 in September.

The reduction was accompanied by a 57 per cent fall in fatalities and a 71 per cent decline in injuries, while suicide attacks also registered a substantial decrease.

PICSS data showed that the attacks claimed 111 lives in October, compared with 260 in September. The number of people injured dropped from 242 to 69, indicating a 71 per cent reduction.

The number of suicide attacks was jointly the lowest recorded during the same period. However, the 169 terrorists killed also represented the lowest monthly figure in the preceding 12 months, reflecting a decline in terrorist fatalities, the report noted.

headline: PCB Patron's XI to face Sri Lanka tomorrow
description: Seven Test players feature in the hosts’ side as Sri Lanka fine-tune for Test series
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
The PCB Patron's XI will take on the Sri Lanka Test squad in a three-day practice match starting on Wednesday (today) at the Islamabad Club Ground as the touring side steps up preparations for the upcoming two-match Test series.

Both squads held training sessions at the Islamabad Club on Tuesday.

Patrons XI head coach Ijaz Ahmed Junior said the fixture would provide an important opportunity for players selected for the Test series to prepare under match conditions.

"It is a good opportunity for the players included in the Test series to prepare. All the players in our squad have been playing domestic cricket, so we expect a good contest," Ijaz told PCB digital.

Patrons XI captain Saad Baig said adapting to the demands of red-ball cricket would be a key challenge for the players.

"There is time in red-ball cricket, and players need to adjust themselves quickly to its demands," Baig said.

Baig recently hit a 75-ball 74 to play a key role in Pakistan’s title winning triumph in the ODI tri-series which concluded at Lahore on October 31.

Baig added that he was feeling good about leading the side and considered the captaincy an honour.

Seven members of Pakistan's Test team are included in the Patrons XI squad.

Two additional fast bowlers from the Patrons XI squad will also be added to the Pakistan Test squad after the conclusion of the practice match, the Pakistan Cricket Board said.

The three-day fixture is expected to provide both sides with valuable preparation ahead of the Test series.

Following the warm-up game there will be two-day gap before both Sri Lanka and Pakistan will meet in the first Test which will be held at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium from November 9-13.

The second Test will be held at Gaddafi Stadium Lahore from November 17-21.

The series is part of the World Test Championship 2025-2027 cycle.

Of the nine-team contest Sri Lanka trail seventh as they have played six Tests, having won just one and lost two.

Pakistan are at the rock bottom with two wins and seven defeats from nine matches they have played so far.

New Zealand top the race, followed by South Africa, Australia, India, Bangladesh and England follow.

PCB Patron’s XI squad: Saad Baig (captain), Abdullah Fazal, Ali Shabbir, Ali Usman, Azan Awais, Mohammad Salman, Mohammad Suleman, Mohammad Tayyab Arif, Mohammad Taha, Saqib Khan, Sameer Minhas, Shoaib Akhtar Junior, Ubaid Shah.

Sri Lanka Test squad: Kusal Mendis (c), Anjala Bandara, Dinesh Chandimal, Dhananjaya De Silva, Sonal Dinusha, Asitha Fernando, Prabath Jayasuriya, Lahiru Kumara, Dilshan Madushanka, Eshan Malinga, Kamindu Mendis, Pathum Nissanka, Keshara Nuwantha, Milan Rathnayaka, Pasindu Sooriyabandara

headline: Trump says US will stop $4 billion in funding to Israel at end of 2026
description: Says democrats, left-wing politicians using US financial support to Israel as a talking point to criticise Republicans
author: Reuters
article_text:
President Donald Trump on Tuesday said he made ​a deal with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that Washington would stop $4 billion in funding to Israel after the end of ‌this year.

It was not immediately clear which funding Trump meant or how exactly the funding would be stopped at the end of the year, given that the memorandum of understanding that provides $3.8 billion in US military aid to Israel each year does not expire until 2028. Conversations have been underway on how ​Washington's assistance to Israel would evolve beyond that date.

Speaking to Fox News' "Fox & Friends" programme, Trump said Israel no longer needed ​the funding and that some Democrats and left-wing politicians were using the US financial support to Israel as ⁠a talking point to criticise Republicans.

"Now, as far as paying Israel, Bibi Netanyahu and I have made a deal that we give Israel $4 ​billion a year, and we made a deal months ago that we're stopping," Trump said. "We've already agreed that by the end of this year ​we won't be paying Israel. Now we'll help Israel if they need it," he said.

Neither the White House nor Netanyahu's office responded to Reuters' requests for comment.

US public support for Israel has fallen since the Gaza war began in 2023, particularly among Democrats. A June Quinnipiac University poll found 48% of voters ​and 66% of Democrats believe the US is too supportive of Israel, up from 16% and 20%, respectively, when the question was first asked ​in 2017.

Criticism of Israel

Support for Israel among Democratic voters has plummeted, candidates critical of Israel are winning Democratic primaries, and even moderate lawmakers are increasingly willing to ‌challenge decades ⁠of US support for Israel.

Abdul El-Sayed, who would be the first Muslim US senator if he wins in Michigan in the midterm elections on Tuesday, opposed unconditional military aid to Israel, saying US funding should prioritise US citizens.

Trump said the left used the US funding as a "signal of unfairness" and that he could not allow that to happen. He specifically mentioned El-Sayed when explaining why he said Washington was stopping the money.

"Because ​they (Israel) don't need it, and because ​why should we suffer the ⁠slings from lunatics like an El-Sayed when they don't need it? It's a bad, it's a bad talking point," Trump said.

Some members of Trump's Make America Great Again movement have also become increasingly critical ​of Israel, accusing it of having misled Trump — who campaigned in 2024 on a promise to avoid ​foreign military interventions — ⁠into believing Iran could easily be defeated in a war.

Congress passed a law in 2020 authorising the funding for Israel, but the Senate and House of Representatives must still pass appropriations bills every year to distribute and release the funds.

Netanyahu said in an interview with an Israeli television channel in ⁠October: "If you ​think we're going to continue receiving what I secured twice, and that's tens of ​billions of dollars in American aid for the defence budget, prepare yourselves and get used to the fact that it won't happen because America has changed."

headline: Pakistan conducts maiden flight test of locally developed Fa’az air-to-air missile
description: Fa’az air-to-air missile, equipped with advanced terminal guidance system, can engage aerial targets at longer ranges
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Pakistan has successfully conducted the flight test of its first indigenously developed Fa’az air-to-air missile, marking a significant milestone in the advancement of the country’s aerospace and defence capabilities, the military’s media wing said on Tuesday.

According to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the missile is equipped with a state-of-the-art terminal guidance system and can engage enemy aerial targets at longer ranges.

“Fa’az will significantly enhance the operational flexibility of the Pakistan Air Force, further strengthening the country’s overall defence posture,” the statement said.

It added that the successful flight test demonstrated the "technical maturity, innovation and self-reliance" achieved by Pakistan’s defence industry.

The launch was witnessed by senior officers of the Pakistan Armed Forces, along with scientists and engineers who played a key role in developing the weapon system.

The president, prime minister, chief of army staff and chief of defence forces, and services chiefs congratulated the scientists and engineers on the achievement.

Separately, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi congratulated the nation on the successful test, describing it as an important development in the defence sector.

“Our scientists and engineers have once again achieved a remarkable feat,” he said, adding that the nation was proud of its scientists and engineers.

Earlier this month, the Pakistan Army successfully test-fired the extended-range version of its Fatah-2 hypersonic ballistic missile, which was equipped with advanced navigation and state-of-the-art avionics.

The ISPR had said the missile was capable of engaging targets with high precision and defeating enemy missile defence systems because of its unique trajectory and manoeuvrability. Its extended range would further enhance the army’s reach and ability to engage deep targets, it added.

A week before that announcement, an extended version of the indigenously developed Fatah-4 ground-launched cruise missile was successfully test-fired. The weapon system was equipped with advanced avionics and state-of-the-art navigational aids and could engage targets at extended ranges with high precision and lethality, the ISPR had said.

The test also validated additional technical parameters of various subsystems incorporated to improve accuracy and survivability, it added.

In September 2025, the Pakistan Army had conducted a successful training launch of the Fatah-4 at a range of 750 kilometres. The missile was designed to evade enemy missile defence systems through its terrain-hugging capabilities, enabling it to engage targets with high precision.

headline: Nine things on US voters' minds ahead of midterm elections: poll
description: Poll highlights living costs, Trump, Iran, election trust and other key concerns for US voters
author: Reuters
article_text:
The rising cost of living will be top of mind for Americans as they head to the polls in Tuesday's midterm elections which will determine control of Congress for the last two years of President Donald Trump's term.

What follows are results from a Reuters/Ipsos poll of ​1,765 US adults conducted nationwide Thursday through Monday — making the survey distinct from an exit poll which includes voters surveyed ‌as they leave polling stations. The poll had a margin of error of 3 percentage points for registered voters.

The cost of living

Some 48% of registered voters in the poll say the cost of living is the top issue for deciding how they will vote, compared with 26% who say democratic norms and 13% who point to ​immigration. US fuel prices have surged since the start of the US-Israeli war with Iran in February.

Donald Trump

Trump has urged supporters to ​pretend he is on the ballot in an effort to energise his Republican Party. The Reuters/Ipsos poll showed ⁠that 48% of people who planned to vote — or already had done so — said they thought of their ballots as a vote against Trump, ​compared to 25% who said they were voting for him. Some 25% said Trump was not a factor in their vote.

Iran

Trump has argued that war ​was necessary to prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons. Some 25% of voters think military action has been worth the cost, and 55% say it has not been worth it. Some 18% weren't sure.

Election integrity

Voters overall trust the US electoral process, with 77% saying they are confident their ballots will be counted but 45% saying they think ​voter fraud is a widespread problem. Trump has falsely claimed that massive numbers of non-citizens vote illegally and election officials worry the administration could disrupt ​the election or certification of results it views unfavourably. The White House says its goal is to safeguard election integrity and voting security.

Household finances

Some 49% of Americans think ‌their household ⁠finances have gotten worse since January 2025, when Trump returned to power, compared with 13% who said their finances have gotten better and 37% who say things are about the same. Trump campaigned ahead of the November 2024 presidential election with a promise to turbocharge the economy, but his presidential approval has fallen in recent months to the lowest levels of his political career, including among Hispanic Americans who swung in his direction in ​2024. The latest poll showed 54% ​of Hispanics said their household ⁠finances have suffered, while 10% said they had improved.

Transgender sports

Some 38% of voters ahead of the election said keeping transgender girls and women out of women's sports was a very important issue or the most important issue, ​compared to 25% who said that about protecting the rights of transgender people.

Data centers

Some 42% of registered ​voters in the poll ⁠said limiting the construction of data centres used to power AI was very important or the most important issue.

Mega donors

article_html:
The rising cost of living will be top of mind for Americans as they head to the polls in Tuesday's midterm elections which will determine control of Congress for the last two years of President Donald Trump's term.

What follows are results from a Reuters/Ipsos poll of ​1,765 US adults conducted nationwide Thursday through Monday — making the survey distinct from an exit poll which includes voters surveyed ‌as they leave polling stations. The poll had a margin of error of 3 percentage points for registered voters.

The cost of living

Some 48% of registered voters in the poll say the cost of living is the top issue for deciding how they will vote, compared with 26% who say democratic norms and 13% who point to ​immigration. US fuel prices have surged since the start of the US-Israeli war with Iran in February.

Donald Trump

Trump has urged supporters to ​pretend he is on the ballot in an effort to energise his Republican Party. The Reuters/Ipsos poll showed ⁠that 48% of people who planned to vote — or already had done so — said they thought of their ballots as a vote against Trump, ​compared to 25% who said they were voting for him. Some 25% said Trump was not a factor in their vote.

Read More: US voters head to polls to deliver midterm verdict on Trump

Iran

Trump has argued that war ​was necessary to prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons. Some 25% of voters think military action has been worth the cost, and 55% say it has not been worth it. Some 18% weren't sure.

Election integrity

Voters overall trust the US electoral process, with 77% saying they are confident their ballots will be counted but 45% saying they think ​voter fraud is a widespread problem. Trump has falsely claimed that massive numbers of non-citizens vote illegally and election officials worry the administration could disrupt ​the election or certification of results it views unfavourably. The White House says its goal is to safeguard election integrity and voting security.

Household finances

Some 49% of Americans think ‌their household ⁠finances have gotten worse since January 2025, when Trump returned to power, compared with 13% who said their finances have gotten better and 37% who say things are about the same. Trump campaigned ahead of the November 2024 presidential election with a promise to turbocharge the economy, but his presidential approval has fallen in recent months to the lowest levels of his political career, including among Hispanic Americans who swung in his direction in ​2024. The latest poll showed 54% ​of Hispanics said their household ⁠finances have suffered, while 10% said they had improved.

Transgender sports

Some 38% of voters ahead of the election said keeping transgender girls and women out of women's sports was a very important issue or the most important issue, ​compared to 25% who said that about protecting the rights of transgender people.

Data centers

Some 42% of registered ​voters in the poll ⁠said limiting the construction of data centres used to power AI was very important or the most important issue.

Mega donors

The ultra-rich face few limits on how much they can spend to influence federal elections. A bipartisan majority of registered voters — including 93% of Democrats and 71% of Republicans — think it is ⁠inappropriate for ​billionaires to contribute tens of millions of dollars to influence elections.

Political options

While poll respondents appeared ​to narrowly favour Democrats over Republicans for this year's congressional elections, they remain divided on which party has good ideas. Some 43% of registered voters in the poll said Democrats ​had at least some good ideas, while 39% said the same of Republicans.

headline: Rizwan, Najab hit tons in Quaid-e-Azam Trophy
description: Huraira scores 13th first-class century as four matches of the premier first-class event begin
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
Mohammad Rizwan and Najab Khan struck unbeaten centuries to put Peshawar Blues in a commanding position against Faisalabad on the opening day of the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy Gold tournament on Tuesday.

Peshawar reached 306-3 at stumps after being asked to bat first at Abbottabad Cricket Stadium, with Rizwan and Najab sharing an unbroken 179-run partnership for the fourth wicket.

Rizwan was unbeaten on 111 off 142 balls, including 21 boundaries, registering his 16th first-class century. Najab made 101 not out from 168 deliveries, hitting 18 fours to claim his maiden first-class hundred in only his third match.

Earlier, Nabi Gul scored 48 and Maaz Sadaqat contributed 29, while Faisalabad pacer Asad Raza claimed two wickets.

At the National Ground in Islamabad, Mohammad Huraira struck his 13th first-class century but Sialkot Blues were dismissed for 241 against defending champions Karachi Blues.

Huraira scored 117 off 143 balls, hitting 13 fours and a six, after Sialkot had slumped to 14-4. He shared an 89-run stand with Hamza Nazar, who made 24, before Ahmad Hasan added 43.

Karachi pacer Muhammad Umar took 4-19, while Mohammad Asghar claimed three wickets and Danish Aziz two. Karachi were 9-1 at the close, with Haroon Arshad dismissed by Athar Mehmood.

At Diamond Cricket Ground in Islamabad, FATA reached 311-6 against Lahore Whites, with Fawad Arshad unbeaten on 91 and Rehan Afridi scoring 69.

The pair added 132 for the sixth wicket to revive FATA's innings after early setbacks. Lahore's Hammad Aziz took four wickets for 81 runs.

Meanwhile, Islamabad were bowled out for 215 against Multan at Shoaib Akhtar Stadium in Rawalpindi. Mohammad Hammad Khan top-scored 50, while Sarmad Bhatti made 40 and Sudais Ulfat contributed 38.

Multan's Muhammad Shahzad and Mohammad Irfan claimed three wickets apiece, while Aamer Yamin took two.

headline: European supermarkets rush to patch vulnerabilities after region-wide fridge hack
description: EU cybersecurity agency ​says attacks underscore importance of European cooperation, rapid information-sharing
author: Reuters
article_text:
European supermarkets targeted in a second wave of cyberattacks that cranked up ​fridge and freezer temperatures were rushing on Tuesday to upgrade their systems and protect themselves against further hacking attempts.

Stores in ‌eight European countries were forced to throw away vast quantities of food after hackers tampered with their fridges on Monday, in an attack identical to one that swept dozens of supermarkets in France three weeks ago.

In Sweden, supermarket chain Coop said it was switching systems to 5G networks and modern modems, instead of 4G connections - a process that had ​already started since the French incident.

The seven stores hit by the attack are back up and running, but their refrigeration systems have ​been disconnected from the internet, a spokesperson said.

"We are looking quite thoroughly and deeply into the status of the ⁠entire network of stores to see if we risk any vulnerability anywhere in the entire network," the spokesperson added.

Software provider Danfoss, whose systems were ​again among those targeted, said it has been in close contact with customers over the past three weeks to help them manage the situation, and ​recommended that systems should not be directly accessible via the internet.

“Retailers need to act now. They should identify whether their refrigerator controllers are vulnerable, check if they are connected to the internet, ensure they've got the latest security updates and are supported by the manufacturer. And if they don’t even know, then remove them from the public ​internet immediately,” said Frank Groenewegen, cybersecurity expert at Deloitte in The Hague.

“With disconnecting, you haven’t fixed the root cause, but you’ve at least isolated ​those systems so that an attacker is not able to do this anymore.”

'Heightened alert'

Many European supermarkets are run by independent business owners in a cooperative structure, meaning ‌systems are ⁠not the same across stores.

Swedish grocer ICA said all 23 stores hit in Monday's cyberattack had equipment connected outside the chain's centrally managed store network.
