headline: Gold holds steady at Rs412,136 per tola
description: Gold holds steady at Rs412,136 per tola
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Gold prices remained unchanged in Pakistan on Tuesday as international bullion rates edged lower, under pressure from a strengthening US dollar and rising Treasury yields, while investors awaited the outcome of US midterm elections for clues about the country's fiscal policy and their potential impact on financial markets.

In the local market, gold prices held steady at Rs412,136 per tola, while the price of 10-gram gold remained unchanged at Rs353,340, according to rates released by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association. On Monday, gold had gained Rs2,400 per tola.

Internationally, spot gold fell 0.5% to $3,928.49 per ounce by 12:11 pm ET (1711 GMT), after declining as much as 1% earlier in the session to a low of $3,893.31. Similarly, US gold futures for December delivery slipped 0.8% to $3,938.90 per ounce.

The stronger dollar and higher Treasury yields weighed on bullion, making the non-yielding metal less attractive to investors. "The dollar has been strengthening, and yields are going higher," said Phillip Streible, Chief Market Strategist at Blue Line Futures.

Adnan Agar, Director of Interactive Commodities, said international gold prices were fluctuating between $3,895 and $3,970 per ounce, reflecting continued uncertainty in the market.

He said investors were closely watching the US midterm election results, adding that their implications for gold could become clearer over the next one to two days as the outcome would determine which party secured a majority.

Agar said gold could remain under pressure in the near term, while a sustained move above $4,080 and $4,150 levels could bring some stability to the market. However, if prices failed to recover, bullion could potentially decline towards $3,700 per ounce, he warned.

Meanwhile, oil prices fell around 2% to a three-week low on Tuesday as traders assessed diplomatic efforts to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran against concerns over further supply disruptions following attacks in both conflicts. The decline in oil prices eased some inflation concerns, offering temporary support to bullion before gold resumed its downward movement.

In the domestic market, silver prices declined Rs120 to Rs5,368 per tola. Meanwhile, the rupee gained Rs0.01 against the US dollar to close at Rs276.71, compared with Monday's close at Rs276.72.

headline: SECP notifies rules against Ponzi schemes
description: SECP notifies rules against Ponzi schemes
author: APP
article_text:
The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) has notified the Companies (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Regulations, 2026, setting criteria to define and prohibit Ponzi schemes, pyramid schemes, deceptive multi-level marketing and unlawful referral marketing.

The regulations apply to all companies, including foreign companies, and cover schemes operating through physical and digital channels, including websites, mobile applications and social media.

They identify prohibited practices including deriving income primarily through recruitment rather than genuine product sales, using funds from new investors to pay earlier ones, promising unrealistic or guaranteed returns, imposing excessive joining fees and concealing the use of investor funds.

They also cover schemes involving products with little genuine market demand, misleading claims, inadequate refund or buy-back arrangements and the sale of unregistered or illegal goods.

Pyramid schemes with unclear terms, unreasonable purchase requirements or multiple positions designed to generate recruitment-based rewards are prohibited.

Bona fide direct selling, where compensation is primarily derived from actual sales to end consumers, remains permissible.

The regulations extend to existing schemes exhibiting unlawful characteristics, whether physical or digital, and bar companies from promoting or facilitating them.

Violations may attract penalties against companies, directors and officers.

headline: North cement exports fall to zero
description: North cement exports fall to zero
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
North-based cement mills recorded no exports in October 2026, against 114,082 tonnes a year earlier, as total industry despatches edged up 0.37% to 4.810 million tonnes, according to data released by the All Pakistan Cement Manufacturers Association.

Local despatches rose 1.17% to 4.041 million tonnes from 3.994 million tonnes, while export despatches declined 3.67% to 768,754 tonnes from 798,019 tonnes.

Total despatches by North-based mills fell 3.13% to 3.397 million tonnes from 3.507 million tonnes, while South-based mills despatched 1.41 million tonnes, up 9.90% from 1.29 million tonnes.

The identical domestic and total figures for the north reflect the absence of exports, which had amounted to 114,082 tonnes in October last year. North-based mills despatched 3.397 million tonnes into local markets, up 0.13% from 3.393 million tonnes.

South-based mills despatched 643,816 tonnes locally in October, up 7.05% from 601,401 tonnes, and exported 768,754 tonnes, up 12.40% from 683,937 tonnes.

During the first four months of the current fiscal year, total despatches were 17.953 million tonnes, 2.93% higher than 17.442 million tonnes a year earlier.

Domestic despatches rose 5.93% to 14.889 million tonnes from 14.055 million tonnes during the period, while exports fell 9.51% to 3.064 million tonnes from 3.387 million tonnes.

North-based mills despatched 12.344 million tonnes domestically in the four months, up 4.87% from 11.770 million tonnes, but total despatches fell 1.61% to 12.344 million tonnes from 12.546 million tonnes after exports of 775,948 tonnes a year earlier were not repeated.

South-based mills despatched 2.545 million tonnes domestically, up 11.36% from 2.285 million tonnes, while exports rose 17.38% to 3.064 million tonnes from 2.611 million tonnes.

Total despatches by South-based mills increased 14.57% to 5.610 million tonnes from 4.896 million tonnes.

In the four months, exports from South-based mills reached 3.064 million tonnes against 2.611 million tonnes a year earlier, while the north, which had exported 775,948 tonnes in the same period last year, recorded no exports.

headline: PSX gains 1,455 points on ME peace talks
description: PSX gains 1,455 points on ME peace talks
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) extended its recovery on Tuesday as the benchmark KSE-100 index gained 1,455 points, fuelled by purchases of heavyweight stocks following recent market weakness.

The positive momentum continued despite the Middle East conflict including reports of a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island and an Iranian official's remarks that Tehran and Washington were far from a deal to end the war. These developments reversed somewhat the oil market relief, with crude prices rebounding after a steep decline in the previous session.

The bourse opened on a positive note and maintained its upward trajectory throughout the session. It touched the intra-day high of 168,469.78 and low of 167,308.66 before settling at 168,018.87, up 1,454.80 points, or 0.87%.

Despite renewed pressure from geopolitical developments and rising oil prices, investors kept their interest in local equities, with bargain hunting in heavyweight stocks providing crucial support.

"PSX experienced a green session on Tuesday as the KSE-100 index gained 1,455 points (+0.87%) day-on-day, with 212 million shares traded," Ahmed Sheraz of KASB KTrade wrote in his market wrap.

The market witnessed broad-based buying, led by commercial banks, fertiliser companies, cement firms and investment banks, reflecting improved investor sentiment. Individually, Fauji Fertiliser, Engro Holdings, HBL, Pakistan Services, Meezan Bank and Engro Fertilisers were the major contributors to the index.

Oil prices remained relatively lower compared to the previous session, trading in the range of $104-106 per barrel after briefly touching $107. Meanwhile, market participants were focused on the US midterm elections, alongside US-Iran negotiations through mediators. Sentiment received support from President Trump's indication that the US had no immediate plans to strike Iran, raising hopes of a potential diplomatic breakthrough. "Going forward, developments on the geopolitical front, particularly the US elections and US-Iran parleys, will remain key factors shaping market direction," Sheraz added.

"The market opened on a strong note in anticipation of resolution of the US-Iran conflict as fresh diplomatic efforts raised hopes again," Arif Habib Limited Deputy Head of Trading Ali Najib said. He attributed across-the-board buying, especially of blue-chip stocks, to softer oil prices, which assisted the benchmark index to close above 168k.

Fauji Fertiliser, Engro Holdings, Pakistan Services, Meezan Bank and Engro Fertilisers were the major laggards, collectively eroding 702 points. "Going forward, the market is likely to stay volatile amid evolving US-Iran developments and global political uncertainty. Progress on diplomatic efforts may support sentiment, while investors remain cautious ahead of US election outcome," Najib said.

Cumulatively, trading volumes increased to 517.3 million from Monday's total of 443.4 million. The value of traded shares stood at Rs20.7 billion. Shares of 500 companies were traded in the ready market. Of these, 270 stocks closed higher, 189 fell and 41 remained unchanged.

Cnergyico Pk was the volume leader with trading in 114.8 million shares, losing Rs0.54 to close at Rs11.74. Foreign investors sold shares worth Rs492.9 million, the National Clearing Company reported.

KARACHI:

Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) extended its recovery on Tuesday as the benchmark KSE-100 index gained 1,455 points, fuelled by purchases of heavyweight stocks following recent market weakness.

The positive momentum continued despite the Middle East conflict including reports of a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island and an Iranian official's remarks that Tehran and Washington were far from a deal to end the war. These developments reversed somewhat the oil market relief, with crude prices rebounding after a steep decline in the previous session.

The bourse opened on a positive note and maintained its upward trajectory throughout the session. It touched the intra-day high of 168,469.78 and low of 167,308.66 before settling at 168,018.87, up 1,454.80 points, or 0.87%.

Despite renewed pressure from geopolitical developments and rising oil prices, investors kept their interest in local equities, with bargain hunting in heavyweight stocks providing crucial support.

"PSX experienced a green session on Tuesday as the KSE-100 index gained 1,455 points (+0.87%) day-on-day, with 212 million shares traded," Ahmed Sheraz of KASB KTrade wrote in his market wrap.

The market witnessed broad-based buying, led by commercial banks, fertiliser companies, cement firms and investment banks, reflecting improved investor sentiment. Individually, Fauji Fertiliser, Engro Holdings, HBL, Pakistan Services, Meezan Bank and Engro Fertilisers were the major contributors to the index.

Oil prices remained relatively lower compared to the previous session, trading in the range of $104-106 per barrel after briefly touching $107. Meanwhile, market participants were focused on the US midterm elections, alongside US-Iran negotiations through mediators. Sentiment received support from President Trump's indication that the US had no immediate plans to strike Iran, raising hopes of a potential diplomatic breakthrough. "Going forward, developments on the geopolitical front, particularly the US elections and US-Iran parleys, will remain key factors shaping market direction," Sheraz added.

"The market opened on a strong note in anticipation of resolution of the US-Iran conflict as fresh diplomatic efforts raised hopes again," Arif Habib Limited Deputy Head of Trading Ali Najib said. He attributed across-the-board buying, especially of blue-chip stocks, to softer oil prices, which assisted the benchmark index to close above 168k.

Fauji Fertiliser, Engro Holdings, Pakistan Services, Meezan Bank and Engro Fertilisers were the major laggards, collectively eroding 702 points. "Going forward, the market is likely to stay volatile amid evolving US-Iran developments and global political uncertainty. Progress on diplomatic efforts may support sentiment, while investors remain cautious ahead of US election outcome," Najib said.

Cnergyico Pk was the volume leader with trading in 114.8 million shares, losing Rs0.54 to close at Rs11.74. Foreign investors sold shares worth Rs492.9 million, the National Clearing Company reported.

headline: Argentina to help curb high agri-losses
description: Argentina to help curb high agri-losses
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Argentine Ambassador Sebastian Sayus has offered Argentina's expertise in advanced agricultural machinery, grain storage technologies and post-harvest management to help Pakistan tackle significant losses in its agricultural produce, while identifying promising opportunities for joint ventures and business-to-business partnerships in agriculture, dairy and pharmaceuticals.

Speaking during his visit to the Karachi Chamber of Commerce & Industry, Sayus highlighted that Pakistan lost 10-20% of its grain production and 35-40% of its horticultural produce annually, largely due to inefficient storage facilities and inadequate post-harvest management. He noted that Argentina, being one of the world's leading food-exporting countries, possessed considerable expertise in agricultural machinery and modern storage solutions, including silo bags and metallic silos, which could be effectively introduced and developed in Pakistan.

He expressed confidence that Argentina could play a meaningful role in helping Pakistan strengthen its agricultural supply chain, reduce wastage and improve the value of its agricultural output. With Pakistan increasingly focusing on large-scale agricultural storage solutions, he saw considerable scope for cooperation, technology transfer and mutually beneficial investment in this critical sector.

The ambassador also identified significant potential for collaboration in the dairy industry, besides highlighting Argentina's advanced pharmaceutical capabilities, especially in the manufacturing of oncology products used in cancer treatment.

headline: Committee warns GSP+ access at risk
description: Committee warns GSP+ access at risk
author: Shahbaz Rana
article_text:
Pakistan's duty-free access to the European Union (EU) could be in the doldrums because of a deteriorating human rights situation, National Assembly Standing Committee on Finance Chairman Syed Naveed Qamar said on Tuesday, amid the government's assurance that there was no such threat.

The standing committee also expressed disappointment over yet another failed trader scheme, as the government announced enforcement action against all traders except the 222 who joined, subject to approval by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

"We are getting signals that the GSP+ status is in the doldrums because of human rights issues," Qamar, a former finance and commerce minister, said while chairing the committee.

He did not specify the exact concerns that could lead to an adverse EU decision. The last monitoring report on the Generalised Scheme of Preferences Plus (GSP+) highlighted scores of human rights and fundamental rights violations, a weakening judicial system and curbs on freedom of expression.

The scheme runs until December 2028, and a deputy prime minister-led committee is preparing an application to qualify for the new scheme from January 2029, Minister of State for Finance and Revenue Bilal Kayani told the committee

Pakistan was the top beneficiary of the EU's GSP+ trade scheme, recording 7.5 billion in exports to the bloc in 2024 under preferential tariffs, according to the fifth GSP report, which evaluated the implementation of 27 international core conventions in beneficiary countries.

Continuation of the scheme is critical for Pakistan, which remains unable to bring substantial improvement in its exports despite decades of protection and fiscal incentives given to exporters.

The EU monitoring report underlined that Pakistan needed to take robust steps to reverse negative trends on enforced disappearances and violations of freedom of expression. "In this regard, laws on blasphemy, cybercrime (such as PECA), defamation, counterterrorism and sedition should be amended or repealed."

In view of the revised GSP rules from 2027, the EU said key priorities for future engagement include accountability for human rights violations, increased efforts against torture, in-prison and capital punishment reforms, and reversing negative developments on enforced disappearances and freedom of expression.

During the 2023-2025 monitoring period, Pakistan has faced compliance issues with its GSP+ obligations, the report noted. "It has regressed in a number of areas while positive change was limited."

Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) MNA Dr Nafisa Shah raised the closure of Pakistan's borders with Iran and Afghanistan and its implications for exports to the Central Asian republics.

"There is an impact on trade with Central Asia but we closed our borders with Afghanistan because of national security priorities," Kayani said.

Despite a conflict between China and India, neither country has suspended trade, Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) MNA Jawed Hanif said.

Trade scheme fails

The standing committee expressed disappointment over the failure of the fixed tax scheme for traders, as only 222 new shopkeepers joined against a hope of one million out of 3.7 million non-filers.

"We did not get the kind of response that we had hoped for," Kayani said in response to a question from Dr Nafisa Shah, adding that traders now had no excuse after the government accepted all their demands, including exemption from audit, a fixed tax rate and no dealings with the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR).

There will be no further extension of the scheme after it expires on October 31, and the government is beginning a new phase of imposing fines and taking enforcement action, he said.

Traders remain largely outside the tax net, and the government offered them a new scheme in June, the third since 2022. This too failed, with only 222 new traders joining.

The minister of state said the government had consulted the attorney general for Pakistan before taking legal action and did not disclose the nature of the action.

However, sources said there could be legal and ethical issues if the government gives traders a Rs10,000 first default notice under the new scheme with a direction to file returns, whereas any non-trading person is required to pay a Rs25,000 fine for late filing.

Qamar repeatedly asked whether Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and the federal cabinet were in favour of punitive action and would not budge when traders threatened to observe a strike.

"The government is very much committed to take action and we are preparing an enforcement plan for the approval of the prime minister," Kayani said.

He said there was no reason traders would observe a strike, as the scheme had been prepared with their extensive input, and sought Parliament's support before enforcement action.

The committee chairman was of the view that the FBR did not have the manpower to go after all traders.

Given limited enforcement capacity, the FBR could use powers to suspend bank accounts or other services to compel traders to become filers, Hanif recommended.

Kayani said the government was considering severing services but that these could be measures of last resort.

headline: 'Climate finance must go beyond green investment'
description: 'Climate finance must go beyond green investment'
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) Governor Jameel Ahmad has said that climate change and financial exclusion are deeply interconnected, and the people most exposed to climate shocks are smallholder farmers, micro and small enterprises, and low-income households.

"They are also the least likely to have insurance, savings, or access to formal finance. Climate finance must do more than support green investments. It must also help communities anticipate risks, build resilience, and adapt to a changing climate," he said.

Jameel Ahmad inaugurated a four-day SBP and Alliance for Financial Inclusion (AFI) Joint Learning Programme on Inclusive Green Finance Policy Implementation in Islamabad. The programme brings together 38 international participants of the AFI network, representing central banks and financial regulators of 24 countries from four continents, to move from policy commitments to real-world implementation.

In his address, the central bank governor pointed to Pakistan's experience during the devastating floods of 2022. The deluge caused physical damage of nearly $15 billion and economic losses of another $15 billion. It affected more than 30 million people and damaged 2.2 million homes. He said this showed why financial systems must be both green and inclusive.

Highlighting Pakistan's progress, he noted that financial inclusion had reached 71%, the gender gap narrowed to 27%, and Pakistan was sharing its Green Taxonomy and climate risk framework with peer regulators across the AFI network.

The governor highlighted SBP's progressive regulatory framework, which included the Green Banking Guidelines (2017), the Environmental and Social Risk Management Framework (2022), the Pakistan Green Taxonomy, and regulations on climate-related financial risks, along with the Climate Stress Testing Guidelines (December 2025).

On the initiatives taken to promote women's financial inclusion, he highlighted the Pakistan Women Inclusive Finance Programme, supported by the Asian Development Bank. He noted that Pakistan joined the Women Entrepreneurs Finance Code in 2025, with the SBP serving as the anchor institution for the financial industry.

The governor also outlined Pakistan's work under the AFI's four pillars of promotion, provision, protection, and prevention. The Green Taxonomy provides a science-based classification of green activities, while targeted financing schemes channel credit to underserved segments.

headline: Kazakhstan sets five-year trade roadmap with Pakistan
description: Kazakhstan sets five-year trade roadmap with Pakistan
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Kazakhstan has developed a five-year roadmap to expand trade and investment with Pakistan, Deputy Prime Minister Sirjan Zhomangarin said during a meeting with Qaiser Ahmad Sheikh, as both countries reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral economic relations, increasing trade and exploring new investment opportunities, according to a statement issued by the Board of Investment on Tuesday.

During the meeting, Sheikh emphasised the need to promote business-to-business cooperation, enhance private-sector engagement and improve banking channels to facilitate trade and investment.

He highlighted opportunities in e-commerce, warehousing, textiles and mining, noting that Kazakhstan's affordable energy could attract Pakistani investment in the textile sector.

The memorandums of understanding signed during President Asif Ali Zardari's visit to Kazakhstan in February required early implementation to translate commitments into tangible economic benefits, Sheikh stressed.

Kazakhstan's deputy prime minister expressed his desire for Pakistan's prime minister to visit Kazakhstan and reaffirmed his country's commitment to strengthening bilateral relations.

He emphasised the need to increase bilateral trade and said a five-year roadmap had been developed to advance cooperation.

He noted that Pakistan's market of approximately 250 million people offered significant opportunities for Kazakhstan, while Pakistan could use Kazakhstan as a gateway to the wider Eurasian market.

The deputy prime minister also highlighted the need for direct air connectivity between Pakistan and Kazakhstan to facilitate business, trade and people-to-people exchanges.

He informed that Kazakhstan's foreign minister would visit Pakistan to attend the preparatory meeting for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.

Both sides emphasised the importance of stronger connectivity, effective implementation of existing agreements and greater private-sector engagement to transform the potential of bilateral relations into concrete economic partnerships.

The statement said the meeting focused on stronger trade, investment and connectivity ties, with both sides exploring ways to increase bilateral trade and new investment opportunities between Pakistan and Kazakhstan.

headline: ECC asks about placement of trained agri-experts
description: ECC asks about placement of trained agri-experts
author: ZAFAR BHUTTA
article_text:
Pakistan's economic managers have raised questions about the placement of agricultural professionals trained in China and has directed the food ministry to share their status.

The Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) of the cabinet told the food ministry to disclose the placement status of 885 agricultural professionals following completion of their training.

During discussions in a recent meeting, the ECC, while responding to a query from the minister for power about the placement of 885 trained agricultural professionals, asked the Ministry of National Food Security and Research and the Ministry of Federal Education and Professional Training to share their placement status with the committee to gauge the impact of training.

The Ministry of Education briefed the ECC that the prime minister during his visit to China in June 2024 had said that 1,000 Pakistani agricultural professionals be trained in China to benefit from its expertise in agricultural technology, innovation and research. Accordingly, the Ministry of Food Security developed a training framework, while the Higher Education Commission (HEC) was entrusted with the logistical and financial management of the programme.

The Ministry of Education recalled that the ECC, in its meeting held on November 28, 2024, had approved a technical supplementary grant of Rs3,072 million for implementation of the programme in batches. Of the total, Rs1,950 million was released during fiscal year 2024-25. HEC arranged training of 292 professionals under batch-I, however, batch-II training could not be undertaken within the stipulated timeframe and consequently, Rs1,406 million remained unutilised, while the unutilised balance of Rs544 million was surrendered.

The Ministry of Federal Education apprised the ECC that during FY2025-26 HEC placed a further 593 trainees in two batches, bringing the total number of trained agricultural professionals to 885. The remaining 115 trainees, having Sindh domicile, have met the prescribed requirements and have been registered at the Northwest Agricultural & Forestry University, Xi'an, China. Their departure under Cohort-I, batch-III was scheduled for the last week of September 2026, thereby completing the target of 1,000 trainees.

The Ministry of Education added that to ensure continuity of the programme, a meeting was held with the Finance Division on August 8, 2025, wherein it was agreed in principle that the immediate requirement of Rs1,666 million would be met from HEC's FY2025-26 allocation under the "Promotion of Research" programme and the amount would be recovered through a supplementary grant during the third quarter of FY2025-26. However, the committed grant could not be released during FY26.

Meanwhile, the HEC incurred expenses of Rs897.187 million through internal re-appropriation from its own resources. The Ministry of Education told the meeting that timely release of required funds was essential to ensure the uninterrupted implementation and successful completion of the initiative as well as to recover the released amount, ie, Rs897.187 million, by the commission to safeguard the continuity of the national research ecosystem and meet HEC's committed national and international obligations. The ECC considered a summary dated September 16, 2026, submitted by the Ministry of Federal Education and titled "Technical Supplementary Grant of Rs1,666.176 million for the Prime Minister's Initiative on Short Term Training of three to six months for 1,000 Agricultural Professionals in China", and approved the proposal.

headline: UAE investors invited into eight sectors
description: UAE investors invited into eight sectors
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

The Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) has proposed regular exchanges of trade delegations, joint business forums, trade exhibitions and sector-specific meetings with Emirati business organisations to expand Pakistan-UAE trade, and invited UAE investors into agriculture, food processing, textiles, information technology, construction, logistics, minerals and value-added manufacturing.

LCCI President Ali Hussam Asghar put the proposals to Salem Mohammed Al Zaabi, Ambassador of the United Arab Emirates to Pakistan, at a meeting on bilateral commercial relations, according to a statement issued on Tuesday.

Asghar said Pakistan offered considerable investment opportunities through its large consumer market, industrial capacity, skilled workforce and entrepreneurial potential, and that joint ventures in the identified sectors could contribute to industrial growth, employment generation and economic development.

He said closer engagement could open new avenues for trade and investment.

headline: Pakistan offers energy crisis expertise to BD
description: Pakistan offers energy crisis expertise to BD
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

Pakistan on Tuesday offered to share its experience in managing the global energy crisis with Bangladesh as Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and Bangladesh's Adviser on Finance Rashid Al Mehmood Titumir discussed fuel supply challenges and the impact of disruptions on international energy markets.

During a meeting, both sides discussed their strategies to manage the unprecedented energy crisis, ensure uninterrupted fuel supplies, and reduce the impact of rising uncertainty in energy markets on their economies, according to a press release.

Pakistan offers energy crisis expertise to BD

.

Our Correspondent November 04, 2026 Less than a minute read
facebook twitter whatsup linkded email
Pakistan, Bangladesh discuss energy security, measures to tackle crisis. Photo: APP
ISLAMABAD:

Pakistan on Tuesday offered to share its experience in managing the global energy crisis with Bangladesh as Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and Bangladesh's Adviser on Finance Rashid Al Mehmood Titumir discussed fuel supply challenges and the impact of disruptions on international energy markets.

During a meeting, both sides discussed their strategies to manage the unprecedented energy crisis, ensure uninterrupted fuel supplies, and reduce the impact of rising uncertainty in energy markets on their economies, according to a press release.

headline: NA panel seeks wage hike enforcement
description: NA panel seeks wage hike enforcement
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

The National Assembly Standing Committee on Overseas Pakistanis has called for the "true implementation" of revised minimum wage to be paid as soon as it is announced, across all bodies under the ministry.

The committee expressed reservations over the replies regarding minimum wage payments and recommended that all boards and organisations under the ministry establish rules or mechanisms to ensure that the revised minimum wage is paid as soon as it is increased by the federal government. The body recommended that all provinces and G-B increase grants to workers affected by any incident to Rs3 million.

headline: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia to boost media ties
description: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia to boost media ties
author: APP
article_text:
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and Saudi Ambassador to Pakistan Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy on Tuesday agreed to further strengthen cooperation between the two brotherly countries in the fields of information, broadcasting, media, culture, and public relations.

During a meeting with the Saudi ambassador, the minister welcomed him to Pakistan and congratulated him on his diplomatic assignment, expressing confidence that his tenure would further strengthen the longstanding ties between the two countries.

The minister said Pakistan-Saudi Arabia relations were reaching new heights, with vast opportunities for expanding cooperation in media, culture, drama, music, tourism, and people-to-people contacts.

He noted that the relationship between the two countries spanned generations and was rooted not merely in diplomatic and political engagement but also in shared history, religious bonds and strong public connections.

Referring to the strategic partnership between the two countries, the minister maintained the defence agreement reflected the strength of their cooperation in the defence sector.

He observed that under the leadership of Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the KSA underwent transformation in economic and cultural spheres. The promotion of tourism in AlUla and the modern presentation of the historical and cultural significance of Diriyah were prominent examples of the Saudi leadership's vision, he added.\",Our Correspondent,National

headline: ATC grants bail to Imaan, Hadi in clash case
description: ATC grants bail to Imaan, Hadi in clash case
author: Fiaz Mahmood
article_text:
An Islamabad anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Tuesday granted bail to lawyers Imaan Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha in a case involving allegations of blocking a road and clashing with police.

ATC Judge Abual Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain heard the bail applications and approved them against surety bonds of Rs5,000 each, with lawyer Riasat Ali Azad appearing on behalf of the accused.

During the hearing, police submitted the case record to the court. The judge then asked the parties whether they wished to make any further submissions before announcing his decision. Referring to the show-cause notice matter involving the police, the judge said, "I will look into the matter concerning the show-cause notice to the police."

The court subsequently approved the bail applications of both Imaan and Chattha.

According to the First Information Report (FIR) registered at Islamabad's Kohsar Police Station, which was filed last year and concerned a protest in the grounds of the Islamabad Press Club, Imaan and Hadi led a Baloch Student Council protest with at least 150 demonstrators present. The FIR added that the participants raised anti-state slogans and those against state institutions through loudspeakers and megaphones, while also obstructing police from carrying out their duties.

Filed under Sections 186, 188, 341, 353, and 506 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC), the FIR stated that the participants took a rally out and blocked a road, upon which police informed them that this was against Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Tuesday's verdict came less than a week after an ATC sentenced Imaan and Hadi to 10 years in prison each in a case involving the removal of security barriers. Both were convicted under Section 186 of the PPC and sentenced to "1-year Simple Imprisonment" with a fine of Rs50,000 each, the order stated.

The court also convicted both under Section 353 of the PPC and sentenced them to 2 years' simple imprisonment.\",FIAZ MAHMOOD,National

headline: LPG price hike crushes rickshaw drivers
description: LPG price hike crushes rickshaw drivers
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
For 13 years, Rashid Ali has driven a three-wheeled motorised rickshaw around Lahore.

His day starts at 6am and sometimes does not end ?until midnight, but he was long able to make $6.50 a day - enough for his family's bare essentials. Now, with liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices surging, he doesn't even make half that.

Ali, 33, is among thousands of Pakistani drivers who run their vehicles on LPG, which is sold in cylinders and mainly used for cooking and heating.

Majeed Ghauri, chairman of the Awami Rickshaw Union, calls it "the fuel of the poor". He said about 70% of its members' 43,000 auto-rickshaws and nearly 8,000 Qingqis - motorcycle-based three-wheelers that carry several passengers on set routes - run on LPG.

LPG prices have surged since October 17, when two Iranian border crossings closed, halting imports, traders say, in the latest energy shock since the US-Iran war began in February.

With Ali now lucky to make $3 a day, his family has cut back on meals, eating only twice a day.

"Previously, when LPG was cheap, we could earn a decent income," Ali said. "Now, it's just not possible to get by on seven or eight hundred [rupees], is it?"

Before the border closures, Pakistan imported about 7,000 metric tonnes of LPG a day from Iran, the Pakistan LPG Association said.

Traders said the price of a 12-kg cylinder jumped 56% within days of the closure to Rs7,000 or about 583 rupees per kg in the open market.

The Balochistan government cited security and smuggling for the decision, while Iran's foreign ministry said technical issues were to blame. Iran's ambassador later said Iran had imposed no restrictions, including on LPG exports, and blamed changes in Pakistan's import paperwork.

Ali pays Rs600 a day to rent his rickshaw, filling up with gas four or five times a day, at Rs300 to 400 a time.

As well as daily expenses, Ali also pays Rs11,000 a month for his home and has two young children to support.

Adding to his problems, passengers, he said, do not want to pay higher fares.

"For a trip that should cost Rs200 or 250, they might only offer Rs80, 100, or 150," Ali said.

Passenger Mohammad Ramzan said when a driver asked Rs500 for a ride in the city, he offered half that. When the driver declined, he walked away, he said.

Inflation hit 9.6% in October, and the central bank last week raised interest rates to 12%, citing energy and wheat prices. Petrol hit a record Rs458 per litre on April 3 and remains about 40% above its pre-war price.

Back home at midday, Ali said his two boys still needed their lunch. He would go out again until late at night, he said, hoping to make enough to bring something for the children to eat at night.

headline: YouTube viewership in Pakistan records surge
description: YouTube viewership in Pakistan records surge
author: Naeem Asghar
article_text:
TikTok has around 100 million users in Pakistan, while nearly 150 million videos are watched and uploaded on the platform daily from the country, the National Assembly Standing Committee on Information Technology and Telecommunications was told on Tuesday.

PTA Chairman Major General (retd) Hafeez ur Rehman shared the figures during a briefing on social media usage, highlighting the growing popularity of digital platforms in the country.

He told the committee that 96 million Pakistanis currently use YouTube and watch around 560 million videos on the platform every day, making Pakistan the world's leading country in terms of YouTube video viewership.

Pakistanis also make millions of calls and send millions of messages daily through WhatsApp, he added.

The meeting, chaired by MNA Syed Aminul Haque at Parliament House, also addressed complaints about poor telecom services, frequent internet disruptions and the slow pace of improvements in network infrastructure.

Committee members questioned why users continued to face connectivity problems despite repeated discussions over the past two and a half years.

Member Ahmad Atiq said mobile networks were barely working in his constituency and along the route to Karachi. He complained that connectivity was deteriorating after every committee meeting, adding that even WhatsApp calls were frequently disconnected in Islamabad.

"If this is the situation in Islamabad, what can one expect in rural areas, where even 3G does not work, while you are talking about 5G?" he asked. He also sought details of the fibre-optic network laid over the past two and a half years.

Another member, Asia Ishaq, said 4G services had also deteriorated since the introduction of 5G, asking whether lawmakers would have to approach the Supreme Court to get the telecom companies to improve their services.

The PTA chairman said he had visited 41 districts along with telecom operators to assess service quality and inspect mobile towers. He said the PTA had directed the operators to improve their services, adding that issuing show-cause notices was the authority's last resort because companies often obtained stay orders from courts against financial penalties.

Federal Minister for Information Technology Shaza Fatima Khawaja said data consumption had increased significantly due to the growing use of social media and artificial intelligence.

She said 18 million people were using 5G services in Pakistan and the technology was being rolled out in 24 cities. The government had taken steps to improve telecom services, she added.

Recalling the country's spectrum auctions, the minister said no such auction had been held after Nawaz Sharif left office, adding that his government had introduced 4G services while the present government had conducted the 5G spectrum auction.

Khawaja said disruptions in telecom services had several causes, including theft of infrastructure. In some areas, entire mobile towers were stolen, while diesel and generators installed to keep them operational were also taken away, she told the committee.

Federal Minister for Information Technology Shaza Fatima Khawaja said data consumption had increased significantly due to the growing use of social media and artificial intelligence.
She said 18 million people were using 5G services in Pakistan and the technology was being rolled out in 24 cities. The government had taken steps to improve telecom services, she added.

Recalling the country's spectrum auctions, the minister said no such auction had been held after Nawaz Sharif left office, adding that his government had introduced 4G services while the present government had conducted the 5G spectrum auction.

Khawaja said disruptions in telecom services had several causes, including theft of infrastructure. In some areas, entire mobile towers were stolen, while diesel and generators installed to keep them operational were also taken away, she told the committee.

headline: Pakistan tests indigenous Fa'az missile
description: Pakistan tests indigenous Fa'az missile
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Pakistan has successfully conducted the flight test of its first indigenously developed Fa'az air-to-air missile, marking a significant milestone in the advancement of the country's aerospace and defence capabilities, the military's media wing said on Tuesday.

According to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the missile is equipped with a state-of-the-art terminal guidance system and can engage enemy aerial targets at longer ranges.

"Fa'az will significantly enhance the operational flexibility of the Pakistan Air Force, further strengthening the country's overall defence posture," the statement said.

It added that the successful flight test demonstrated the "technical maturity, innovation and self-reliance" achieved by Pakistan's defence industry.

The launch was witnessed by senior officers of the Pakistan Armed Forces, along with scientists and engineers who played a key role in developing the weapon system.

The president, prime minister, chief of army staff and chief of defence forces, and services chiefs congratulated the scientists and engineers on the achievement.

Separately, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi congratulated the nation on the successful test, describing it as an important development in the defence sector.

"Our scientists and engineers have once again achieved a remarkable feat," he said, adding that the nation was proud of its scientists and engineers.

Earlier this month, the Pakistan Army successfully test-fired the extended-range version of its Fatah-2 hypersonic ballistic missile, which was equipped with advanced navigation and state-of-the-art avionics.

The ISPR had said the missile was capable of engaging targets with high precision and defeating enemy missile defence systems because of its unique trajectory and manoeuvrability. Its extended range would further enhance the army's reach and ability to engage deep targets, it added.

A week before that announcement, an extended version of the indigenously developed Fatah-4 ground-launched cruise missile was successfully test-fired.

headline: Dry weather to prevail in the country
description: Dry weather to prevail in the country
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) has forecast dry weather across most parts of the country over the next 24 hours, while northern areas are expected to remain partly cloudy and cold.

However, isolated light rain and snowfall over hills may occur in upper Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and Gilgit-Baltistan during the period.

According to the Met Office, temperatures recorded in major cities on Tuesday morning were 13°C in Islamabad, 19°C in Lahore, 25°C in Karachi, 15°C in Peshawar, 10°C in Quetta, 6°C in Gilgit, 7°C in Murree and 12°C in Muzaffarabad.

headline: Committee seeks support for dyslexic children
description: Committee seeks support for dyslexic children
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

The National Assembly Standing Committee on Federal Education and Professional Training on Tuesday expressed concern over challenges faced by children with dyslexia.

It called for ensuring that their educational future is not compromised due to lack of identification, institutional support and remedial interventions.

The panel stressed that following the enactment of the Dyslexia Act, its effective implementation has become imperative in both public and private educational institutions.

It called for providing appropriate academic facilitation to such children in various subjects.

headline: FIR alone can't bar public employment
description: FIR alone can't bar public employment
author: Hasnaat Malik
article_text:
The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) has ruled that mere registration of a first information report (FIR) cannot constitute a ground for disqualifying a person from public employment, emphasising that an accusation does not amount to proof or presumption of guilt.

A division bench, led by Chief Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan, issued guidelines for federal and provincial governments, administrative authorities and law enforcement agencies to establish uniform, transparent and constitutionally compliant standards for antecedent verification during public-sector recruitment.

In its 10-page judgment, authored by CJ Khan, the court observed that a fundamental distinction must be maintained between the registration of an FIR and judicially established culpability.

"An FIR is merely an accusatory instrument and constitutes neither proof nor presumption of guilt," the judgment stated, adding that once an accused had been acquitted by a competent court, the appointing authority could not disregard the judicial determination or treat the underlying accusation as established misconduct.

The court further held that judicial acquittal must receive due recognition, subject to an objective assessment of a candidate's antecedents and suitability. It directed that adverse character verification must be based on authentic and independently verifiable material rather than conjecture or suspicion.

The judgment also laid down guidelines for the treatment of criminal cases in police character certificates. Where a candidate had been acquitted, the criminal case should not be reflected adversely in the certificate.

If proceedings were still pending, only their pendency could be disclosed, without any presumption of guilt. The court further emphasised that no candidate should ordinarily be excluded from recruitment without being provided a meaningful opportunity of hearing and a reasoned determination.

It said recruitment decisions must conform to prescribed statutory criteria, merit, proportionality and constitutional guarantees of fairness and equality.

The court examined the matter in the context of Articles 4, 10A, 18 and 25 of the Constitution, which collectively safeguard legality, due process, equality before the law, and protection against arbitrary exclusion from lawful employment.

Explaining the constitutional framework, the judgment said Article 4 required executive authorities to act within the law and on relevant considerations, while Article 25 prohibited discriminatory treatment lacking a reasonable basis and connection with a legitimate statutory objective.

It observed that Article 18, although not guaranteeing an absolute right to public appointment, protected eligible citizens against arbitrary impediments to lawful employment.

headline: 'Imran knew of governor's rule in K-P'
description: 'Imran knew of governor's rule in K-P'
author: ​ Our Correspondents
article_text:
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Tuesday said that party founder Imran Khan was fully aware of the imposition of governor's rule and emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, rejecting reports that he had welcomed the provincial government's removal.

Speaking to the media near Adiala Jail, Gohar said Imran had not expressed satisfaction over the fall of the K-P government.

Regarding Salman Safdar's meeting with Imran, Gohar said it was the lawyer's first meeting with the PTI founder since April 8, after a gap of 380 days and called it a positive development.

He lamented that the prolonged suspension of meetings had led to the prevailing political tension.

Had regular meetings been allowed, the situation could have improved, tensions might not have escalated, and the situation in K-P might not have reached the point of governor's rule or emergency, he added.

Gohar rejected reports that his name had been finalised for a meeting with Imran, saying he had consistently tried to facilitate meetings between political leaders and the PTI founder.

'Raja rules out immediate political breakthrough'

Separately, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said Imran's lawyer, Salman Safdar, had said the party founder was in high spirits during their meeting in jail, with his body language and determination reflecting his resolve to stand by his position.

Speaking to the media at Factory Naka in Rawalpindi, Raja said the meeting between Safdar and Imran had been necessary for the functioning of the judicial system because the PTI founder's cases were not progressing.

He said Safdar had told the court that he would not present arguments until he was allowed to meet his client.

Raja said the meeting was a requirement of the legal process rather than a favour extended to the party.

However, he ruled out any immediate breakthrough, saying the meeting with the lawyer could not be equated with the political-level engagement that the party had been seeking. Unless a political meeting took place, he said, the situation would not move forward.

Raja said he did not see the likelihood of a forward bloc emerging within the party, although he would not rule out any possibility altogether. If anyone within the party harboured reservations or ill intentions, these would eventually become apparent, he said.

Raja also clarified that the PTI was not looking towards Maulana Fazlur Rehman as a saviour. He said that, under a political climate of repression, the party saw no reason to turn away those who stood alongside it.

headline: I don't walk away from a dare, says Ali Zafar of 'Gangs of Khorasan' role
description: I don't walk away from a dare, says Ali Zafar of 'Gangs of Khorasan' role
author: Qaisar Kamran
article_text:
"I've waited for a character that would take me far from my comfort zone. Out of all the scripts I read, Bostan Khan was the one that dared me. And I don't walk away from a dare," actor and singer Ali Zafar told The Express Tribune, explaining what drew him to his upcoming project, Gangs of Khorasan.

Known for his romantic screen presence, stylish appearance and soulful music, Zafar is now preparing to step into unfamiliar territory with a character that is a departure from the roles audiences have traditionally associated with him.

In the upcoming web series, Zafar plays Bostan Khan, a mysterious gangster whose rugged appearance, thick moustache and distinctive glasses have already caught the attention of fans after the actor shared a glimpse of his new look on social media.

Speaking to The Express Tribune, Zafar described Gangs of Khorasan as a mafia-themed web series, calling it the first of its kind in Pakistan. The project will see him explore a darker and more intense character, moving away from the romantic and light-hearted roles that have been a significant part of his acting career.

The transformation is particularly notable given Zafar's relatively limited acting appearances in recent years. His last major live-action film as a lead actor was Teefa in Trouble (2018), opposite Maya Ali. The film, which also marked his debut as a film producer and writer, became a commercial success. He later lent his voice to the animated film Allahyar and the 100 Flowers of God (2023). His appearance in Gangs of Khorasan therefore marks a significant return to screen acting, particularly in a web-series format, after an extended gap.

The series also features Feroze Khan, Humaima Malick, Sonya Hussyn and Syed Jibran. Feroze has established himself through television dramas including Khaani, Khuda Aur Mohabbat 3 and Akhara, while Humaima gained wider recognition through Shoaib Mansoor's film Bol (2011), followed by appearances in Bollywood and Pakistani cinema, including The Legend of Maula Jatt. Sonya Hussyn, known for her performances in Aisi Hai Tanhai, Ishq Zahe Naseeb and Deemak, has built a reputation for taking on challenging characters. Syed Jibran, meanwhile, has remained a familiar presence on television through dramas such as Chup Raho, Neem and Pagal Khana.

Produced by Anas Ali, with direction associated with Hamza Ansari, Gangs of Khorasan brings together an ensemble cast for a story centred on the world of organised crime. While further details about the storyline and the individual characters remain under wraps, the project's mafia theme and its cast have generated interest.

Ali Zafar started out on Pakistani television as an actor before becoming a popular musician, later also established a career in Bollywood and his success led many Pakistani actors to venture into Hindi films. He has received five Lux Style Awards and a Filmfare Award nomination.

Zafar began his music career as a composer and gained popularity with his single "Channo" from his debut album, Huqa Pani (2003), which sold over five million copies worldwide. "Channo" turned out to be a huge success, topping many music charts and earned him several awards for Best Music Album and Artist. Zafar made his acting debut in cinema with a leading role in the 2010 Bollywood satire film Tere Bin Laden, a moderate box office success. His performance in the film garnered critical appreciation and earned him several nominations in the Best Male Debut category, including Filmfare. He then also worked in several films, including Mere Brother Ki Dulhan, Chashme Baddoor, and Dear Zindagi.

Alongside his acting and singing career, Zafar participates in tours, concerts, and stage shows, is active in humanitarian work, and has a number of endorsement deals.

On 23 March 2021, Ali Zafar was awarded the highest literary award, Pride of Performance, for his contribution in the field of arts and music.

For Zafar, however, the attraction appears to lie in the challenge of playing someone unlike the characters he has portrayed before. His decision to take on Bostan Khan suggests an attempt to expand his acting range and reconnect with audiences through a genre he has not previously explored in this way.

Zafar also introduced the character through a bold social media post, announcing himself as Bostaan Khan in Gangs of Khorasan. Sharing the first-person declaration, "Warned you not to mess with me. My world. My rules. I AM BOSTAAN KHAN!".

article_html:
KARACHI:

"I've waited for a character that would take me far from my comfort zone. Out of all the scripts I read, Bostan Khan was the one that dared me. And I don't walk away from a dare," actor and singer Ali Zafar told The Express Tribune, explaining what drew him to his upcoming project, Gangs of Khorasan.

Known for his romantic screen presence, stylish appearance and soulful music, Zafar is now preparing to step into unfamiliar territory with a character that is a departure from the roles audiences have traditionally associated with him.

In the upcoming web series, Zafar plays Bostan Khan, a mysterious gangster whose rugged appearance, thick moustache and distinctive glasses have already caught the attention of fans after the actor shared a glimpse of his new look on social media.

Speaking to The Express Tribune, Zafar described Gangs of Khorasan as a mafia-themed web series, calling it the first of its kind in Pakistan. The project will see him explore a darker and more intense character, moving away from the romantic and light-hearted roles that have been a significant part of his acting career.

The transformation is particularly notable given Zafar's relatively limited acting appearances in recent years. His last major live-action film as a lead actor was Teefa in Trouble (2018), opposite Maya Ali. The film, which also marked his debut as a film producer and writer, became a commercial success. He later lent his voice to the animated film Allahyar and the 100 Flowers of God (2023). His appearance in Gangs of Khorasan therefore marks a significant return to screen acting, particularly in a web-series format, after an extended gap.

The series also features Feroze Khan, Humaima Malick, Sonya Hussyn and Syed Jibran. Feroze has established himself through television dramas including Khaani, Khuda Aur Mohabbat 3 and Akhara, while Humaima gained wider recognition through Shoaib Mansoor's film Bol (2011), followed by appearances in Bollywood and Pakistani cinema, including The Legend of Maula Jatt. Sonya Hussyn, known for her performances in Aisi Hai Tanhai, Ishq Zahe Naseeb and Deemak, has built a reputation for taking on challenging characters. Syed Jibran, meanwhile, has remained a familiar presence on television through dramas such as Chup Raho, Neem and Pagal Khana.

Produced by Anas Ali, with direction associated with Hamza Ansari, Gangs of Khorasan brings together an ensemble cast for a story centred on the world of organised crime. While further details about the storyline and the individual characters remain under wraps, the project's mafia theme and its cast have generated interest.

Ali Zafar started out on Pakistani television as an actor before becoming a popular musician, later also established a career in Bollywood and his success led many Pakistani actors to venture into Hindi films. He has received five Lux Style Awards and a Filmfare Award nomination.

Zafar began his music career as a composer and gained popularity with his single "Channo" from his debut album, Huqa Pani (2003), which sold over five million copies worldwide. "Channo" turned out to be a huge success, topping many music charts and earned him several awards for Best Music Album and Artist. Zafar made his acting debut in cinema with a leading role in the 2010 Bollywood satire film Tere Bin Laden, a moderate box office success. His performance in the film garnered critical appreciation and earned him several nominations in the Best Male Debut category, including Filmfare. He then also worked in several films, including Mere Brother Ki Dulhan, Chashme Baddoor, and Dear Zindagi.

Alongside his acting and singing career, Zafar participates in tours, concerts, and stage shows, is active in humanitarian work, and has a number of endorsement deals.

On 23 March 2021, Ali Zafar was awarded the highest literary award, Pride of Performance, for his contribution in the field of arts and music.

For Zafar, however, the attraction appears to lie in the challenge of playing someone unlike the characters he has portrayed before. His decision to take on Bostan Khan suggests an attempt to expand his acting range and reconnect with audiences through a genre he has not previously explored in this way.

Zafar also introduced the character through a bold social media post, announcing himself as Bostaan Khan in Gangs of Khorasan. Sharing the first-person declaration, "Warned you not to mess with me. My world. My rules. I AM BOSTAAN KHAN!".

headline: Taylor Red singer Nicole Taylor dies at 35
description: Taylor Red singer Nicole Taylor dies at 35
author: News Desk
article_text:
Country singer Nicole Taylor, one-third of the musical trio Taylor Red, has died aged 35 following a battle with breast cancer.

Her triplet sisters, Nika and Natalie Taylor, confirmed the news in a YouTube video.

Nicole died on September 28. In the emotional video, her sisters said she was "at peace and no longer suffering" as they began sharing details of her illness and final months.

Natalie revealed that Nicole was diagnosed with breast cancer in 2022 after the sisters received the news while they were in a "public place".

Nika later explained that the cancer was Stage 3 and "very aggressive".

Despite undergoing chemotherapy, Nicole continued to encourage those around her to enjoy life.

"She pushed us all to have fun and not live in fear and hopelessness and she even did CrossFit during the time she was getting chemo treatments," Natalie shared.

The sisters also paid tribute to Nicole in a statement on a page created in her memory.

"Nicole, the oldest of us three sisters, will be greatly missed. She was our leader and our best friend," they wrote.

"We are heartbroken, but we know she is in Heaven and will see her again," they added. Nika and Natalie also confirmed that a private funeral had already taken place.

The identical triplets began their musical journey playing instruments including guitar, banjo, fiddle and mandolin.

Originally performing as Red Roots, they later built a substantial online following through comedy videos, musical challenges and social media content.

The sister trio started as a musical entity in 2011, with their first independently released album, Red Roots, that was released on January 24, 2011, with Red Hen Records. Their subsequent studio album, The Middle of Nowhere, was released on March 20, 2012, by Red Hen Records. They released, Triplicity, the third studio album, on January 7, 2014, from Red Hen Records alongside Daywind Music. The group was signed to Inpop Records in 2015.

Taylor Red released track Country Money in March 2021. It was produced by Ilya Toshinsky and written by J.T. Harding, Matt Jenkins, and Andrew DeRoberts. The track was added to Spotify Editorial playlists and went viral on TikTok.

Taylor Red was featured in the national Sonic Drive-In campaign commercials for 2020-2021. The trio performed over 1,000 live shows across America and internationally in countries such as Norway and Canada, opening for acts including Amy Grant, Charlie Daniels, Diamond Rio, Don Williams, High Valley, Josh Turner, and Michael W. Smith.

Taylor Red reportedly amassed more than 13 million TikTok followers and 16 million YouTube subscribers, alongside brand partnerships with major companies.

headline: Children's theatre dominates World Culture Festival 2026
description: Children's theatre dominates World Culture Festival 2026
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The sixth day of the 25-day 3rd World Culture Festival Karachi 2026, organised by the Arts Council of Pakistan Karachi, featured two children's theatre productions, music, film screenings, dance and the Urdu-English theatre play English Only. A special Spanish dance performance, Flamenco Blanco Flamenco, was also among the highlights of the day.

The programme for children opened with Little Red Riding Hood, presented by Poland's Miniatura City Theatre. Conceptualised, directed and designed by Chile-born artist David Zawalla, the production offered a contemporary interpretation of the well-known fairy tale, set against a futuristic backdrop. Using puppetry, the play portrayed the struggle of the last human girl on a devastated Earth. Norwegian theatre group Erler Teaterkompani presented the adventure-filled production Gangster Hunting with Daisy Detective. The play followed the detective Daisy as she unravelled a mysterious case and pursued a gangster. Children in the audience were also invited to participate in the investigation.

Music enthusiasts attended a special workshop titled Jam and Improvisation, conducted by renowned Serbian guitarist and musician Aleksandar Lipovan.

Under the film screening segment, Polish Featurette presented four short films from Poland: Blue Bird, Momo & Lulu, Dream Up the Title and The Town That Drove Away.

At 7 pm, the Urdu-English theatre production English Only, directed by Awab Bin Farhat, was staged. Set in an English-language classroom in Karachi, the play revolved around four students brought together by their desire to master English.

The day's programme also featured Spain's special dance performance, Flamenco Blanco Flamenco, under the title The Grace of Movement. Through the traditional Spanish art of Flamenco, the performers showcased their artistic skills, combining expressive hand movements, intricate footwork and rhythmic music. The performance highlighted the emotional depth, energy and expressive spirit of Spanish culture, captivating the audience.

Spectators warmly appreciated the artists with enthusiastic applause.

headline: High-level huddle on K-P agrees to scale up IBOs
description: High-level huddle on K-P agrees to scale up IBOs
author: Khalid Mahmood
article_text:
The civil-military leadership on Tuesday agreed to expand intelligence-based operations (IBOs) against terrorists in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) and strengthen coordination between federal and provincial institutions during a high-level meeting chaired by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

The meeting, attended by Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari, K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, federal ministers, governors and senior officials, reviewed the province's security, political and administrative situation.

The participants reviewed the overall national and internal security situation, with particular focus on law and order in K-P, developments following the imposition of governor's rule and emergency, and progress on ongoing counterterrorism operations and IBOs.

Sources said the meeting decided to broaden the scope of IBOs to eliminate terrorism and make coordination between federal and provincial institutions more effective. Participants agreed that a coordinated approach was essential to address the security challenges facing the province.

The prime minister directed the relevant institutions to work under a coordinated strategy to restore law and order, stressing the need for improved cooperation among government departments to ensure effective implementation of decisions.

The meeting was briefed on earlier decisions concerning K-P, progress in their implementation and the results achieved. Governor Kundi informed participants about measures taken across various sectors of the province and the performance of the Area Development Council (ARDC).

The federal government imposed governor's rule and a state of emergency in K-P on October 11 to rein in terrorism and improve governance in the province. On October 22, Prime Minister Shehbaz chaired an Apex Committee meeting and announced Rs160 billion worth of development projects for the province.

The Rs160 billion development package also came under review at Tuesday's meeting. The package focuses on advancing development projects, strengthening security arrangements and undertaking public welfare initiatives in the province.

According to sources, participants also took stock of the country's broader political situation, while matters relating to possible legislation in the coming days were also discussed.

Since the imposition of governor's rule in K-P, the country has witnessed a significant improvement in several key security indicators, with terrorist attacks declining by 37% compared with September, according to statistics released by the Islamabad-based Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies.

However, the institute warned in a report last week that certain incidents remained a cause for concern. In the latest such incident, two policemen were martyred in Mohmand district when gunmen targeted police personnel guarding a polio vaccination team.

A constable and an alleged terrorist were injured in an exchange of fire in the Tamanzai area, within the jurisdiction of Pindiali police station, during an anti-polio vaccination campaign, District Police Officer (DPO) Raza Muhammad Khan said.

President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the attack, expressing "profound grief and sorrow" over the martyrdom of the policemen and paying tribute to their "dedication, bravery and national services".

In a post on X, the president said targeting personnel performing their duties during the anti-polio campaign "to protect children" was "extremely regrettable and condemnable". "Police personnel deployed to protect polio teams are performing a national duty; their sacrifices will not be forgotten," President Zardari said.

In a separate statement, the prime minister paid tribute to the policemen martyred in the incident, prayed for the elevation of their ranks and extended condolences to their bereaved families. "Such terrorist attacks are deeply regrettable and worthy of condemnation," the prime minister said.

Meanwhile, the funeral prayers of Constables Zahoor Khan and Arabi Khan were offered at Police Lines Ghalanai with full official honours. A large number of civil, military and police officials, along with relatives of the deceased, attended the funeral.

On the occasion, DPO Raza Khan, 114 Brigade Commander Brigadier Iftikhar Mehboob, Mohmand Rifles Commandant Colonel Imran Khalid and Deputy Commissioner Mohmand (retd) Captain Bilal Shahid Rao laid floral wreaths on the bodies of the martyred constables to pay tribute to their sacrifice.

A smartly turned-out police contingent presented a salute to the fallen personnel. Following the funeral prayers, participants prayed for the elevation of the martyrs' ranks, forgiveness for the deceased, and patience and fortitude for their bereaved families.

(WITH INPUTS FROM OUR PESHAWAR CORRESPONDENT)

The participants reviewed the overall national and internal security situation, with particular focus on law and order in K-P, developments following the imposition of governor's rule and emergency, and progress on ongoing counterterrorism operations and IBOs.

Sources said the meeting decided to broaden the scope of IBOs to eliminate terrorism and make coordination between federal and provincial institutions more effective. Participants agreed that a coordinated approach was essential to address the security challenges facing the province.

The prime minister directed the relevant institutions to work under a coordinated strategy to restore law and order, stressing the need for improved cooperation among government departments to ensure effective implementation of decisions.

The meeting was briefed on earlier decisions concerning K-P, progress in their implementation and the results achieved. Governor Kundi informed participants about measures taken across various sectors of the province and the performance of the Area Development Council (ARDC).

The federal government imposed governor's rule and a state of emergency in K-P on October 11 to rein in terrorism and improve governance in the province. On October 22, Prime Minister Shehbaz chaired an Apex Committee meeting and announced Rs160 billion worth of development projects for the province.

The Rs160 billion development package also came under review at Tuesday's meeting. The package focuses on advancing development projects, strengthening security arrangements and undertaking public welfare initiatives in the province.

According to sources, participants also took stock of the country's broader political situation, while matters relating to possible legislation in the coming days were also discussed.

Since the imposition of governor's rule in K-P, the country has witnessed a significant improvement in several key security indicators, with terrorist attacks declining by 37% compared with September, according to statistics released by the Islamabad-based Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies.

However, the institute warned in a report last week that certain incidents remained a cause for concern. In the latest such incident, two policemen were martyred in Mohmand district when gunmen targeted police personnel guarding a polio vaccination team.

A constable and an alleged terrorist were injured in an exchange of fire in the Tamanzai area, within the jurisdiction of Pindiali police station, during an anti-polio vaccination campaign, District Police Officer (DPO) Raza Muhammad Khan said.

President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the attack, expressing "profound grief and sorrow" over the martyrdom of the policemen and paying tribute to their "dedication, bravery and national services".

In a post on X, the president said targeting personnel performing their duties during the anti-polio campaign "to protect children" was "extremely regrettable and condemnable". "Police personnel deployed to protect polio teams are performing a national duty; their sacrifices will not be forgotten," President Zardari said.

In a separate statement, the prime minister paid tribute to the policemen martyred in the incident, prayed for the elevation of their ranks and extended condolences to their bereaved families. "Such terrorist attacks are deeply regrettable and worthy of condemnation," the prime minister said.

Meanwhile, the funeral prayers of Constables Zahoor Khan and Arabi Khan were offered at Police Lines Ghalanai with full official honours. A large number of civil, military and police officials, along with relatives of the deceased, attended the funeral.

On the occasion, DPO Raza Khan, 114 Brigade Commander Brigadier Iftikhar Mehboob, Mohmand Rifles Commandant Colonel Imran Khalid and Deputy Commissioner Mohmand (retd) Captain Bilal Shahid Rao laid floral wreaths on the bodies of the martyred constables to pay tribute to their sacrifice.

A smartly turned-out police contingent presented a salute to the fallen personnel. Following the funeral prayers, participants prayed for the elevation of the martyrs' ranks, forgiveness for the deceased, and patience and fortitude for their bereaved families.

(WITH INPUTS FROM OUR PESHAWAR CORRESPONDENT)
